### FAQs
Everything enterprises ask before they put Gnani AI into production.
#### What does Gnani AI do?
Gnani AI builds frontier speech and language models and the enterprise AI agents that run on them. Enterprises use Gnani AI’s conversational AI and voice AI to automate customer conversations, back-office work, and analytics across voice, chat, and WhatsApp.
#### Why is Gnani AI called a frontier AI company?
We train our own models in-house: Evon for language, Warp for speech to speech, Prisma for speech to text, and Timbre for text to speech. The platform, the agents, and the deployment stack are ours too, so nothing in the system depends on an outside model provider.
#### Can Gnani AI run on our own infrastructure?
Yes. You can run Gnani AI in Gnani cloud, in your private cloud, on-premise in your data centre, or fully air-gapped. In every mode, no request goes to an outside model API.
#### How long does it take to launch an agent?
Most teams build and test an agent in under a week. You start from 1,000+ ready workflows and connect your systems through 150+ enterprise integrations.
#### Which languages does Gnani AI support?
Gnani AI supports 40+ languages and handles code-mixed speech, where callers switch languages mid-sentence. Its speech models are trained on 14M+ hours of real telephony audio, so they work on noisy 8 kHz calls.
#### Which industries use Gnani AI?
Banks, lenders, insurers, healthcare providers, telecom companies, and government bodies run Gnani AI in production for collections, onboarding, KYC, support, and more.
#### How does Gnani AI keep data secure?
Gnani AI is SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified, PCI DSS compliant, and built for GDPR, HIPAA, DPDP, and regional data residency requirements. Data is encrypted with TLS 1.2+ in transit and AES-256 at rest, PII is redacted live, access is role-based, and every interaction leaves a full audit trail.
#### Can developers use the models directly?
Yes. Every model is available through the Gnani AI API, with SDKs and docs to get your first call running in minutes.

### FAQs
Everything you need to know about Gnani's AI platform, models, and deployment.
#### What is Gnani AI?
Gnani AI is a frontier AI company that builds its own speech and language models for enterprise deployments: Gnani Evon v3.3 (language model), Gnani Prisma v3.0 (speech to text), Gnani Timbre v3.0 (text to speech) and Gnani Warp v2.0 (speech to speech). On these models it runs AI agents across voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS, plus agent assist, analytics and voice biometrics. Its speech models are trained on 14M+ hours of real call audio, and 250+ enterprises in banking, insurance, healthcare and government run Gnani AI in production, across 40M+ conversations a day.
#### What is frontier AI?
Frontier AI means models at the leading edge of what AI can do. For Gnani AI, it means training its own language and speech models in-house, so the agents, the platform and the deployment stack don't depend on an outside model provider.
#### Why choose Gnani AI over general-purpose AI providers?
Most general-purpose models are trained on clean studio audio and English-first text. Gnani AI trains on the conditions enterprises run in: 14M+ hours of noisy, code-mixed call audio and 2T+ tokens of Indic text. Its speech models rank #1 in 8 of 9 Indian languages on the Kathbath Noisy 8 kHz benchmark. Gnani AI also runs in your private cloud, on-premise or fully air-gapped, which regulated industries often require, and 250+ enterprises run it in production.
#### Which languages does Gnani AI support?
Gnani AI's speech models support 40+ languages and dialects, with deep coverage across Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Bengali, Gujarati, Marathi, Punjabi and Spanish, and Evon v3.3 is trained natively on 11 Indian languages. Models are trained on multilingual and code-switched data, so they handle conversations where speakers shift between languages, a common pattern across BFSI, telecom and customer service in India.
#### How does Gnani AI handle data privacy and regulatory compliance?
Gnani AI supports cloud, private cloud, on-premise and air-gapped deployment, giving enterprises full control over where their data is processed and stored. This helps meet data residency requirements in regulated industries, including banking (RBI), insurance (IRDAI) and healthcare. No customer voice data is used for model training without explicit agreement. Gnani AI is SOC 2 Type 2 certified, ISO 27001 certified, and HIPAA, GDPR and PCI-DSS compliant. Confirm specifics with your legal and compliance team before deployment.

## Gnani Artha The next frontier of Sovereign AI
Launched by the Hon’ble Vice-President of India
Gnani Artha was unveiled by Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan, Hon’ble Vice-President of India, in New Delhi on 28 August 2026.
“
Bharat is making significant strides in AI. I congratulate Gnani AI on this significant milestone and I am pleased to launch Gnani Artha, which brings together the power of Evon, a large language model, and Plexus, a platform that connects this intelligence with real-world work and institutions. Both these platforms reflect the growing strength of India’s technology ecosystem. May this initiative continue to building a stronger, more self-reliant, and technologically empowered India.
Shri C. P. Radhakrishnan
Hon’ble Vice-President of India
### Moments from the launch in New Delhi
Swipe or scroll sideways to see more photos.
### The Sovereign AI mission: solving India’s high-stakes data, language and operational complexities
An application filled in Marathi. Six months of bank statements. GST filings. Photographs of several identity documents. Reading it takes judgement, not transcription.
Cross-checking declared income against actual turnover. Finding the inconsistencies that matter. Every lender in India handles thousands of these a day, and almost none can do it with AI that reasons well enough in the applicant’s own language, at a cost sustainable at that scale, and without the file ever leaving their own systems.
Intelligence that reasons in one’s own language, economics that survive thousands of files a day, and a way to put both into production inside the lender’s own systems. Indian institutions have had these in fragments.
Gnani Artha brings them together as one stack.
#### Reasons in Indian languages
Not English-first with translation bolted on. Trained natively across eleven Indian languages, on Indic data.
#### Survives Indian volumes
Indian scripts cost more to process than English. Artha attacks that language tax at the tokenizer: every model benchmarked against Evon v3.3 costs at least 2.2× more per point of Indian-language accuracy.
#### Runs inside your walls
Open weights on a single node. DPDP, RBI and IRDAI residency met by where the model runs.
### One stack, under your control
Artha is Gnani AI’s end-to-end sovereign AI solution: the models, the platform, and the infrastructure they run on.

Sovereign frontier-grade intelligence, AI economics that work in India, and real-world impact at scale.

### Gnani Evon v3.3
The sovereign LLM that cuts the language tax on Indian AI.
On MILU, a widely used Indian-language benchmark spanning eleven languages and dozens of academic and professional subjects, Evon v3.3 outperforms a 105-billion-parameter Indic model on ten of eleven languages, and a similarly sized 30B model on all eleven, achieving parity with a similar-size hosted global frontier model.
To make the economics work, Gnani AI rebuilt the model’s tokenizer (the layer that breaks language into the units a model processes) for Indian scripts. Fewer tokens mean lower compute cost, faster responses, and more usable context per query.

### Gnani Plexus
Turning sovereign intelligence into real-world impact.
Each agent on Plexus is a discrete, identity-bearing unit, closer to an employee than a script, combined with other agents into workflows built around a defined outcome. Those workflows run under an orchestration layer that can be human-in-the-loop or AI-led.
Join the Plexus waitlist
#### Agentic AI workforce

#### Trigger-based workflows

#### Multi-system integration and tool-calling

#### Enterprise-grade AI governance
Prompt defense. Jailbreak resistance. Data protection. Output control.
### What Plexus can run, in public service and in the enterprise
Multilingual agents, reasoning and governed workflows, applied to the high-volume work Indian institutions run every day.
Government and public sector
#### Grievance resolution and pattern detection
A multilingual agent captures a citizen’s complaint in their own language. A reasoning agent detects patterns across recent complaints (a spike in one district, one recurring failure), files a single consolidated ticket with the department that owns it, and closes the loop with the citizen once resolved.
#### Beneficiary scheme enrolment and outreach
Plexus cross-references a welfare scheme’s eligibility criteria against population and beneficiary databases to identify citizens who qualify but haven’t enrolled, then reaches out in the citizen’s own language, explaining how to complete enrolment, or where an application is stuck and what to do next.
#### Subsidy and benefit transfer failure resolution
When a direct benefit transfer fails (a pension, a scholarship, an LPG subsidy), usually on a bank or Aadhaar mismatch, Plexus flags it automatically. An agent calls the citizen in their own language, walks them through the fix, and Plexus rechecks the transfer status until it clears.
#### Disaster and emergency response triage
Following a flood or disaster alert, outbound calls run at scale across the affected area, capturing what each household needs (shelter, food, medical help) in their own language. Plexus triages by severity and routes each case to the right relief agency, rather than a single generic helpline queue.
#### Public health outreach and follow-up
Vaccination, TB and maternal-health reminder calls with basic symptom triage, in-language. Plexus escalates any red-flag response to the nearest health centre and assigns a follow-up task to the local health worker automatically.
#### Government financial reconciliation
Plexus matches scheme disbursement records across treasury systems, bank confirmations and payment logs, clears the clean matches, and drafts a root-cause note on each genuine discrepancy for the audit or finance team to review.
Enterprise
#### Document-driven underwriting
Reads loan applications, bank statements, GST filings and identity documents, cross-validates them against bureau and Account Aggregator data, and approves, declines or refers each file within governed thresholds.
#### Reconciliation, banking
An agent matches millions of line items across bank statements, core-banking ledgers and payment-switch logs, drafts a root-cause narrative for each genuine exception, and routes it to the team that owns it, automating one of the highest-cost manual functions in Indian banking.
#### KYC and compliance remediation
Scans KYC repositories for expiring or missing fields, triggers re-KYC workflows automatically, and closes the loop without anyone having to initiate it.
#### Dispute and chargeback resolution
Ingests dispute claims and their supporting evidence, applies card-network rules, resolves straightforward cases autonomously, and routes contested ones to a human.
#### Voice-authenticated instant disbursal
Voice biometrics verifies identity, the agent confirms live eligibility and captures verbal consent, and disbursal is triggered on the call, collapsing a loan or top-up into a single conversation, with no branch visit or app step.
#### Grievance intake and pattern escalation
Multilingual inbound captures the complaint; a reasoning agent detects patterns across calls (a spike in failed UPI reversals, say) and files one bulk ticket instead of many, then calls back to close the loop.
Illustrative of platform capability. None of these describes a specific existing deployment, customer or government department, and none implies partnership with or endorsement by any government body.
### Deployed inside your own infrastructure
Gnani Artha runs where your data already lives: your data centre or your virtual private cloud.
01
#### Single node
Roughly 3.5 billion parameters active on any given token, so Evon v3.3 fits on one inference node rather than a cluster.
02
#### Residency by architecture
DPDP, RBI and IRDAI residency requirements are met by where the model runs, not by a clause in a contract.
03

#### How is voice biometrics different from OTPs and security questions?
Unlike OTPs and knowledge-based authentication, voice biometrics verifies identity through natural conversation. This reduces customer effort, eliminates OTP drop-offs, and helps agents complete verification faster.

Yes. Voice biometrics is designed to integrate with existing telephony platforms, contact centres, IVRs, CRMs, and enterprise workflows without requiring major infrastructure changes.

## Agentic Voice AI Platform for Enterprise
Summarise with
GPT

Oops! Something went wrong while submitting the form.
### Agentic Voice AI Platforms
Software platforms that build, deploy, and manage autonomous voice agents that can understand speech, make decisions, trigger workflows, and complete tasks without constant human supervision. When teams ask which agentic voice AI platforms offer the best enterprise solutions, they are typically comparing depth of voice intelligence, orchestration capability, security, and ability to operate reliably at scale in real production environments.
### Enterprise Voice AI Solutions
End to end stacks that use voice as the primary interface to automate customer conversations, internal service desks, and operational workflows. The strongest enterprise voice AI solutions combine speech recognition, language understanding, orchestration, integrations, and analytics in a single platform instead of stitching multiple vendors together.
### Voice AI Agent
A software agent that listens to a user in natural speech, understands intent, accesses backend systems, and responds in a human like voice. In agentic voice AI platforms, each voice AI agent can be configured for a specific function such as collections, customer support, lead qualification, or HR helpdesk, while still operating under a unified governance and monitoring layer.
### Agentic AI
An AI paradigm where systems are not just predictive but can independently decide what to do next, call APIs, update records, and adjust strategy based on outcomes. When comparing which agentic voice AI platforms offer the best enterprise solutions, the level of true agency in the platform is a critical differentiator compared with legacy rule based IVRs or simple FAQ bots.
### Speech Recognition (ASR)
Automatic Speech Recognition converts spoken language into text in real time. Enterprise grade agentic voice AI platforms rely on high accuracy ASR that works in noisy environments, across accents, and in multiple languages. For a platform like Gnani.ai, Indic language ASR accuracy directly impacts call containment, handle time, and downstream automation quality.
### Text to Speech (TTS)
Text to Speech converts system generated responses into natural sounding audio. Enterprise voice AI solutions use TTS to make voice agents sound human, emotionally aligned, and contextually appropriate. Advanced TTS in agentic voice AI platforms supports multiple voices, languages, and speaking styles while meeting latency SLAs required for live conversations.
### Small Language Models (SLMs)
Domain tuned, compact language models optimized for specific industries such as banking, insurance, telecom, or healthcare. In enterprise deployments, SLMs help agentic voice AI platforms deliver high accuracy on jargon heavy calls while staying cost efficient and latency sensitive compared with generic, very large models.
### Large Language Models (LLMs)
Very large neural models trained on broad text data that can summarize, reason, and generate natural language. In the context of which agentic voice AI platforms offer the best enterprise solutions, LLMs are typically used for free form reasoning, summarization, and response generation while being tightly controlled through guardrails, policies, and orchestration logic.
### Orchestration Layer
The control plane that decides which model, tool, or workflow should handle a given customer utterance. A mature orchestration layer allows enterprise voice AI solutions to route between intents, GenAI, knowledge bases, APIs, and human agents while preserving context. This is a key component that separates capable agentic voice AI platforms from simple point tools.
### Multilingual Voice AI
The ability of a platform to understand and speak multiple languages and dialects within the same interaction. For enterprises in India and other multilingual markets, the question of which agentic voice AI platforms offer the best enterprise solutions often comes down to how reliably they support code switching, regional accents, and local languages across large call volumes.
### Omnichannel AI Agents
Agents that operate consistently across voice, chat, WhatsApp, web, and mobile while sharing a common brain, memory, and policy layer. Enterprise voice AI solutions increasingly extend the same logic to text channels so that customers can start in chat and move to voice without losing context.
### Contact Center AI
A category of solutions that augment or automate inbound and outbound calls, quality assurance, coaching, and reporting. Agentic voice AI platforms in this space integrate deeply with CRMs, dialers, ticketing systems, and workforce management tools to provide measurable uplifts in AHT, FCR, CSAT, and agent productivity.
### Real Time Call Analytics
Continuous analysis of live customer conversations for intent, sentiment, compliance, and outcome. Enterprise voice AI solutions with strong real time analytics can surface churn risk, escalation risk, and sales opportunities inside the call, not after the fact. This capability is a major decision factor when teams evaluate which agentic voice AI platforms offer the best enterprise solutions.
### Compliance Ready AI
Capabilities that ensure conversations, recordings, and data flows adhere to regulations such as RBI, PCI DSS, SOC 2, GDPR, and sector specific norms. Enterprise buyers expect agentic voice AI platforms to provide encryption, data residency options, consent handling, redaction, and audit trails as first class features, not add ons.
### No Code AI Builder
A visual builder that lets non technical teams design flows, configure prompts, map APIs, and deploy agents without writing code. In enterprise environments where business teams need agility, no code builders are often a deciding factor in selecting which agentic voice AI platforms offer the best enterprise solutions.
### Backend Integrations
Connectors and APIs that link AI agents to CRMs, core banking systems, policy engines, ticketing tools, billing systems, and data warehouses. Enterprise voice AI solutions live or die by the stability and breadth of these integrations because real automation happens only when the agent can read and write into production systems securely.
### Voice Biometrics
Speaker recognition technology that uses a caller’s voiceprint to authenticate identity or flag fraud. For industries like BFSI and telecom, agentic voice AI platforms that bundle voice biometrics with automation and analytics deliver stronger security and lower handle time compared with separate authentication tools.
### Human in the Loop Escalation
The ability of an AI agent to recognize its own limits, escalate to a human, and pass complete context, transcripts, and metadata. Enterprise voice AI solutions use structured escalation to prevent customer frustration, preserve SLA commitments, and give supervisors full visibility into what the AI attempted before escalation.
### Evaluation Criteria for Agentic Voice AI Platforms
A practical set of dimensions enterprises use to decide which agentic voice AI platforms offer the best enterprise solutions. Typical criteria include: accuracy across languages, latency under peak load, orchestration sophistication, ease of integration, security posture, compliance, observability, governance, and total cost of ownership across pilots and scaled rollout.
### Gnani.ai Agentic Voice AI Platform
Gnani.ai provides an agentic voice AI platform built for enterprises that need production grade performance in multilingual, regulated, and high volume environments. The stack includes proprietary ASR and TTS for Indic and global languages, industry trained SLMs, LLM orchestration, no code builders, and deep integrations with contact center and core systems. For buyers evaluating which agentic voice AI platforms offer the best enterprise solutions, Gnani.ai positions itself as a full stack, voice first platform that is optimized for measurable business outcomes, not just demos.

text:
## ASR (Automatic Speech Recognition)
Summarise with
GPT
CL
PPLX
Stay Updated
Get weekly update from Gnani AI
Thank You! Your submission has been received.
Oops! Something went wrong while submitting the form.
Automatic speech recognition (ASR) is the technology that converts spoken audio into written text. It is the first step in any voice AI system: nothing downstream, from intent detection to compliance scoring, can happen until the audio has become text.
### How Automatic Speech Recognition Works
An ASR system takes an audio stream and produces a transcript, usually in four stages. It splits the audio into short frames and extracts acoustic features. An acoustic model maps those features to speech sounds. A language model works out which word sequence those sounds most plausibly form. A decoder combines both to output the most likely transcript, often with a confidence score per word.
Streaming ASR does this continuously as the caller speaks, which is what allows a voice agent to respond in real time. Batch ASR processes a completed recording and can afford to be slower and more accurate, which suits call analytics and compliance review.
### What Determines ASR Accuracy
Accuracy is measured as word error rate, the proportion of words inserted, deleted or substituted against a human transcript. Four things move it.
Audio quality. Telephone audio is narrowband and compressed, and scores worse than studio audio on the same model.
Accent and language coverage. A model trained mostly on one accent degrades on others, which matters sharply across Indian languages and regional accents.
Domain vocabulary. Product names, account formats and industry terms are the most common source of errors and the easiest to fix with custom vocabulary.
Code-switching. Speakers who mix languages mid-sentence, such as Hindi and English, break models trained on one language at a time.
Always evaluate word error rate on your own call recordings. A benchmark number from a public dataset says very little about how a model will perform on your traffic.
### Where ASR Is Used
Real-time transcription for voice agents and agent assist.
Post-call analytics, quality monitoring and compliance review.
Voice search and dictation.
Subtitling and meeting transcription.
Keyword and phrase spotting for risk and compliance.
### ASR vs STT: Is There a Difference?
In practice the two terms are used interchangeably, and most vendors treat them as synonyms. Where a distinction is drawn, ASR refers to the underlying recognition technology and the research field, while speech to text refers to the product or API that delivers a transcript. If you are comparing vendors, compare capabilities rather than which of the two labels they use.
### Frequently Asked Questions About ASR
#### What does ASR stand for?
ASR stands for automatic speech recognition. It is the technology that converts spoken audio into written text, and it is the first stage of every voice AI pipeline.
#### What is the difference between ASR and STT?
They are used interchangeably. Where a distinction is made, ASR names the underlying technology and research field, and speech to text names the product or API that returns a transcript. The capability is the same.
#### What is a good word error rate?
It depends entirely on the audio. On clean, wideband audio in a well-covered language a strong system can reach single-digit word error rate. On compressed telephone audio with regional accents and code-switching, expect materially higher. Always measure on your own recordings.
#### Does ASR work for Indian languages?
Yes, though coverage varies widely by language and by vendor. The harder problem is code-switching, where a speaker mixes English with an Indian language mid-sentence, which requires a model trained for it rather than a model trained on each language separately.
#### What is the difference between streaming and batch ASR?
Streaming ASR transcribes continuously as someone speaks, which is required for live voice agents. Batch ASR processes a finished recording, has no latency constraint, and is normally more accurate. Use streaming for conversation, batch for analytics.
#### Can ASR identify who is speaking?
Not on its own. Separating speakers is called diarisation, and identifying a specific person is speaker recognition. Both usually run alongside ASR rather than inside it.

## What Is TTS? Text to Speech Meaning Explained | Gnani AI

Text-to-Speech (TTS)
is a core voice AI technology used in modern call centers to convert system-generated text into natural, human-like speech. In customer experience operations,
Text to Speech for call centers
enables IVR systems, voice bots, and AI agents to communicate clearly, consistently, and in real time across high-volume customer interactions.
Unlike legacy voice systems that rely on robotic audio prompts, modern
neural TTS
produces speech that sounds natural, emotionally neutral or expressive as required, and intelligible even on low-quality telephony lines. This directly impacts call containment, customer satisfaction, and operational efficiency.
#### How Text to Speech Works in Call Centers
In a call center environment, TTS sits between business logic and the customer. Backend systems generate text responses such as order updates, payment reminders, or troubleshooting steps. The TTS engine converts this text into audio instantly, allowing customers to hear accurate and up-to-date information without waiting for a human agent.
Most production deployments use
real-time TTS APIs
that stream audio as the text is generated. This keeps conversations fluid and avoids awkward pauses that break customer trust.
#### Key Call Center Use Cases for TTS
Text to Speech is widely used across inbound, outbound, and self-service call center workflows.
In inbound support, TTS powers IVR menus, voice bots, and self-service flows for balance checks, order status, appointment scheduling, and FAQs. In outbound operations, TTS is used for proactive notifications such as payment reminders, delivery alerts, and service updates. For agent assist systems, TTS helps read out system suggestions or confirmations during live calls, reducing cognitive load for agents.
Because TTS responses are generated dynamically, call centers can ensure that customers always hear the most current information without re-recording prompts.
#### Why Neural TTS Matters for Customer Experience
Traditional TTS systems struggle with pronunciation, pacing, and tone. This leads to customer frustration, repeat calls, and early call abandonment.
Modern
neural Text to Speech
models address these issues by improving:
Pronunciation accuracy for names, brands, and domain terms
Natural prosody that matches conversational speech
Consistency across thousands or millions of calls
Support for multilingual and code-mixed conversations
For call centers operating in multiple regions or languages, high-quality TTS is essential to maintaining a consistent brand voice at scale.
#### Implementing TTS in a Call Center Environment
Successful TTS implementation starts with clear business goals. Teams identify where voice responses reduce agent load or improve speed, then map those flows end to end.
From a technical perspective, implementation typically includes selecting a TTS model optimized for telephony audio, configuring pronunciation dictionaries for domain-specific terms, and using speech markup controls to manage pauses, emphasis, and clarity. Integration is done through APIs or SDKs connected to IVR platforms, conversational AI systems, or CRM workflows.
In production, continuous monitoring is critical. Call centers track latency, error rates, pronunciation failures, and user drop-offs to ensure the TTS system performs reliably during peak volumes.
#### Measuring the Business Impact of TTS in Call Centers
The value of Text to Speech is measured through operational and customer metrics, not subjective feedback. High-performing teams track reductions in average handling time, higher self-service containment, fewer repeat calls, improved call completion rates, and higher customer satisfaction scores.
Because TTS is software-driven, improvements compound over time. Voice quality enhancements, better pronunciation handling, and tighter orchestration lead to incremental gains that directly affect cost and experience.
#### TTS as Part of an AI-Driven Call Center Stack
In AI-powered call centers, TTS is not a standalone feature. It connects language models, business logic, and orchestration layers to real customer conversations. By aligning generated content, voice delivery, and live outcomes, teams create a continuous improvement loop where every release can be validated against real call data.
This approach enables safer deployments, faster iteration, and more predictable CX outcomes.
### FAQ: Text to Speech for Call Centers
#### What is Text to Speech in a call center?
Text to Speech in a call center refers to the use of AI voice technology to convert system text into spoken audio during customer interactions. It is commonly used in IVR systems, voice bots, and automated outbound calls.
#### How does TTS improve customer experience?
TTS improves customer experience by delivering clear, consistent, and real-time responses without agent delays. High-quality neural TTS reduces robotic speech, improves comprehension, and lowers customer frustration.
#### Is TTS suitable for high-volume call centers?
Yes. Modern TTS systems are designed to handle millions of calls with low latency and high reliability. They scale horizontally and are commonly used in large enterprise contact centers.
#### Can TTS handle multiple languages?
Most modern TTS platforms support multilingual speech generation. This allows call centers to serve customers in different languages without maintaining separate recorded prompts.
#### How is TTS quality measured?
TTS quality is typically measured using intelligibility, pronunciation accuracy, latency, and listener satisfaction metrics. In call centers, these are often correlated with call containment and handling time.
#### Does TTS replace human agents?
No. TTS complements human agents by handling repetitive or informational interactions. This allows agents to focus on complex or high-value conversations.

#### Multi-channel communication
The ability of a system to handle conversations across multiple customer touchpoints such as phone, WhatsApp, web chat, mobile apps, email, and social messaging. In the context of what agentic voice AI platforms support multi-channel communication, it means a single AI layer can engage the same customer through different channels without losing context.
#### Omnichannel orchestration
The coordination layer that keeps conversations consistent when customers move between channels. For example, a customer starts with a voice call, switches to WhatsApp, then comes back via web chat. Omnichannel orchestration ensures the agentic voice AI platform carries forward history, intent, and next best actions.
#### Voice AI
Artificial intelligence that processes, understands, and generates human speech. Voice AI includes speech recognition, spoken language understanding, and natural-sounding responses. Agentic voice AI platforms use voice AI to power real-time, human-like conversations over telephony and apps.
#### AI voice agent
A virtual agent that speaks and listens like a human, handles end-to-end workflows, and can take actions on connected systems. In a setup where what agentic voice AI platforms support multi-channel communication is the key question, AI voice agents become the primary interface for phone calls and often complement chat agents on digital channels.
#### Speech recognition (ASR)
Automatic Speech Recognition converts spoken audio into text. High quality ASR is critical for agentic voice AI platforms, especially in noisy environments and multilingual markets. Strong ASR performance improves intent accuracy, reduces average handle time, and directly impacts customer satisfaction.
#### Text to speech (TTS)
The technology that converts text outputs into natural-sounding audio. TTS enables agentic voice AI platforms to respond in a human-like voice across inbound and outbound calls. High quality TTS supports multiple languages, accents, and emotional tones for more engaging multi-channel communication.
#### Small language model (SLM)
A compact, domain-tuned AI model that understands industry-specific terminology and workflows. SLMs are often used inside agentic voice AI platforms when enterprises need low latency, predictable behavior, and cost-efficient scaling for high volume voice and chat interactions.
#### Large language model (LLM)
A powerful AI model trained on large text corpora that can generate and understand human language with high flexibility. In enterprise deployments, LLMs are orchestrated with SLMs and business rules. In the context of what agentic voice AI platforms support multi-channel communication, LLMs help handle complex, open-ended queries while SLMs anchor responses in policies and domain logic.
#### Intent recognition
The process of identifying what the user wants to achieve in a conversation, such as “check balance,” “raise a ticket,” or “reschedule payment.” Accurate intent recognition is foundational for agentic voice AI platforms and directly influences routing, workflow triggers, and handoffs across channels.
#### Context retention
The ability of an AI platform to remember previous messages, calls, and actions in a customer journey. When users explore what agentic voice AI platforms support multi-channel communication, they expect context retention so that customers do not repeat themselves when they switch from voice to chat or from IVR to WhatsApp.
#### Session continuity
The technical capability that keeps a conversation alive across channels and devices for a defined time. For example, a customer can drop from a call and later continue on chat with all previous information intact. Agentic voice AI platforms rely on session continuity for seamless multi-channel workflows.
#### Workflow automation
The execution of business processes such as KYC updates, ticket creation, payment reminders, or lead qualification without manual intervention. Agentic voice AI platforms connect to CRMs, ticketing tools, and core systems to automate workflows triggered by natural language, regardless of channel.
#### Backend orchestration
The layer that manages API calls, data lookups, updates, and business rules behind the scenes. Backend orchestration is what turns an AI conversation into a completed task. In any evaluation of what agentic voice AI platforms support multi-channel communication, backend orchestration is a key differentiator.
#### Channel routing
Logic that decides which channel or agent (human or AI) should handle a specific interaction. Channel routing can move customers from a voice IVR to an AI chat widget or escalate from bot to human based on complexity, risk, or customer profile.
#### Human handoff
A controlled transition from an AI agent to a human agent with full conversation context, transcripts, and key metadata. Agentic voice AI platforms designed for multi-channel communication must support smooth handoff to human agents in contact center tools, including live monitoring and supervisor assist.
#### Real-time analytics
Live dashboards and metrics that show what is happening in conversations as they occur. Real-time analytics for agentic voice AI platforms track intent distribution, sentiment, containment, and drop-off points across channels, guiding operations teams to refine flows.
#### Quality assurance automation
Automated scoring and review of calls and chats using AI. Quality assurance automation checks compliance, empathy, script adherence, and resolution outcomes. For enterprises evaluating what agentic voice AI platforms support multi-channel communication, QA automation is critical to maintain standards at scale.
#### Compliance and security
Controls that ensure conversations, recordings, and data handling meet regulatory and internal policies. This includes encryption, role-based access, PII masking, and adherence to financial or healthcare regulations. Agentic voice AI platforms deployed across channels must enforce consistent compliance rules in every interaction.
#### Customer journey mapping
A structured view of how customers move through channels and touchpoints over time. In the context of what agentic voice AI platforms support multi-channel communication, customer journey mapping helps enterprises design where voice, chat, and human interactions should sit for maximum impact.

In the context of voice AI services, real-time analytics means tracking metrics such as call volume, intent distribution, sentiment, silence duration, and outcome while the interaction is still in progress, not hours later.

Voice AI services with real-time reporting allow operations leaders, supervisors, and QA teams to see live performance, drill down into specific segments, and act on issues while customers are still engaged.
#### Speech Analytics

When embedded in voice AI services with real-time analytics, speech analytics surfaces patterns such as recurring complaints, churn signals, and upsell opportunities across thousands of calls per day.

#### Conversation Intelligence
Conversation intelligence is a layer on top of voice AI services that interprets what happened in each interaction. It aggregates intents, resolutions, objections, and outcomes into real-time analytics dashboards. #### Interaction Dashboards

When powered by voice AI services, these dashboards show real-time analytics such as active calls, average handle time, queue health, sentiment distribution, and first-contact resolution, with drill downs to individual conversations.
#### Quality Assurance (QA) Automation
QA automation uses voice AI services to automatically score calls based on predefined rules such as greeting adherence, mandatory disclosures, empathy markers, and script compliance. Real-time analytics and reporting highlight non-compliant calls, risky phrases, and training gaps without manual sampling of a tiny percentage of interactions.
#### Customer Sentiment Analysis
Customer sentiment analysis detects emotional tone in voice conversations using acoustic signals and language cues. Integrated into voice AI services, sentiment becomes part of real-time analytics so supervisors can identify frustrated customers, prioritize callbacks, or intervene in conversations that are at risk of escalation.
#### Agent Performance Analytics
Agent performance analytics tracks metrics such as handle time, silence, talk ratio, adherence to scripts, and resolution rate. When voice AI services provide real-time analytics, team leads can coach agents during the shift, not just at the end of the month, and correlate individual performance with business outcomes.
#### Contact Center Reporting
Contact center reporting is the set of scheduled and ad hoc reports that summarize performance across queues, campaigns, and teams. Voice AI services with real-time reporting move this from static PDFs to dynamic, always-up-to-date views that operations leaders can slice by product, geography, language, and customer segment.

Compliance monitoring uses voice AI services to ensure agents follow regulatory and internal guidelines, such as consent statements, risk disclosures, or verification flows. Real-time analytics and reporting flag high-risk calls instantly, helping financial services, healthcare, and telecom organizations reduce penalties and audit exposure.
#### KPI Tracking
KPI tracking refers to monitoring key performance indicators like average handle time, first-contact resolution, CSAT, NPS, abandonment rate, and promise-to-pay conversions. #### Root Cause Analysis
Root cause analysis is the process of identifying underlying drivers behind repeated issues such as billing complaints, drop-offs, or low CSAT. Voice AI services with real-time analytics cluster similar conversations, surface common triggers, and help product, operations, and CX teams fix problems at the source, not just treat symptoms.

Executive analytics are summarized, strategic views designed for CXOs and business unit heads. A voice user interface (VUI) is a system that lets people operate software by speaking to it and listening to its replies, instead of tapping or typing. It combines speech recognition, language understanding and speech synthesis so that the conversation itself becomes the interface.
### How a Voice User Interface Works
A VUI runs four steps in sequence, usually in under a second.
Speech recognition converts the caller's audio into text.
Language understanding extracts the intent and the entities from that text, for example "check balance" plus an account type.
Dialogue management decides what happens next, calling whatever system holds the answer.
Speech synthesis turns the response back into audio and plays it to the caller.
Everything a VUI does well or badly traces back to one of those four steps. A VUI that mishears accents has a recognition problem. One that answers the wrong question has an understanding problem. One that sounds robotic has a synthesis problem.
### VUI vs GUI vs IVR

### Where Voice User Interfaces Are Used
Contact centre self-service, where callers complete a task without reaching an agent.
Outbound calling for reminders, collections and verification.
In-car and in-home assistants, where hands and eyes are occupied.
Field and warehouse work, where an operator cannot hold a device.
Accessibility, where a spoken interface is the primary way a user reaches a service.
Multilingual service, where a single voice interface covers languages that would otherwise need separate agent pools.
### What Makes a Voice User Interface Work Well
Three things separate a VUI people use from one they abandon.
Latency. A pause longer than roughly a second reads as a dropped call. Response time matters more than voice quality.
Interruption handling. Real people talk over the system. A VUI that cannot be interrupted mid-sentence feels like a recording.
Recovery. Every VUI mishears. What matters is whether it asks a sensible clarifying question or restarts the whole flow.
### Measuring a Voice User Interface
Containment rate, the share of calls completed without an agent.
Task completion rate, the share of callers who got what they called for.
Average handle time against the same task handled by an agent.
Word error rate on your own audio, not on a benchmark dataset.
Barge-in rate and repeat rate, both of which signal an interface people are fighting.
### ‍ Frequently Asked Questions About Voice User Interfaces
#### What does VUI stand for?
VUI stands for voice user interface. It describes any system that a person operates by speaking and that responds with speech, including contact centre voice agents, in-car assistants and smart speakers.
### What is the difference between VUI and IVR?
A traditional IVR follows a fixed menu and accepts keypad tones or a small set of keywords. A VUI accepts natural speech and works out intent, so a caller can state what they want in their own words without navigating a menu tree.
#### What technologies make up a voice user interface?
Four: automatic speech recognition to turn audio into text, natural language understanding to extract intent, dialogue management to decide the next step, and text to speech to turn the response back into audio.
#### What are examples of a voice user interface?
Contact centre voice agents, smart speakers, in-car assistants, voice search on a phone, and hands-free systems in warehouses and hospitals. Any interface where speaking is the primary input counts.
#### Is a VUI the same as a chatbot?
No. A chatbot is text-based and the user can see and re-read the conversation. A VUI is spoken, so it has to handle accents, background noise and interruptions, and the user cannot scroll back. The design constraints are different.
#### How do you measure whether a VUI is working?
Containment rate, task completion rate, average handle time compared with an agent, and word error rate measured on your own call audio rather than on a public benchmark.

### Questions banks and lenders ask us
Can't find your answer? Talk to our team.
What can AI agents do for a bank or NBFC?
+
They handle conversations on voice, WhatsApp and chat, and the back-office work behind them: reading loan documents, checking them against your credit policy, updating your core and loan systems and routing approvals. Collections, onboarding, service and fraud alerts are the most common starting points.
Is this only for phone calls?
No. Voice is where we started and where most of our results come from. The same agents work on WhatsApp, chat, email and documents.
Do collection calls follow RBI rules?
Yes. Calling hours, approved scripts, disclosures and escalation rules are set before go-live, and the agent cannot call outside them. Every call is recorded and transcribed for audit.
Can Gnani AI run on-premise inside our data centre?
Yes. Public sector banks, including Union Bank of India, run Gnani AI fully on-premise on our own speech models. Air-gapped deployment is also available.
Which languages do the agents speak?
40+ languages at model level, with 10+ Indic languages in production speech recognition, including mixed-language speech such as Hinglish. We confirm the exact set during setup.

## The Great Indian AI Internship Challenge. Build Sovereign AI for India.
Build on Gnani AI's own models and compete for paid internships.
Up to 100
paid six-month internships
Up to ₹1 lakh
stipend per intern, per month
₹5 lakh
in awards, ten of ₹50,000 each
Nov 15, 2026
deadline, 18:00 PM IST
Open to enrolled students in India, aged 18 or older. Build solo or in a team of two.
Awards
### Ten awards for standout builds
Alongside the internship shortlist, ten award categories recognise projects for language, impact, craft and reach. Each award is worth ₹50,000.
01
#### Main Character Award
The best build in a regional or low-resource Indian language.
Indian languages
02
#### Mixed Vibes Award
The best code-mixed voice experience across Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish.
Code-mixed speech
03
#### Real Deal Award
The most useful real-world problem solved, for users such as farmers, kirana stores or rural health workers.
Real-world impact
04
#### Noise Canceller Award
The build that performs best on messy, noisy, real telephonic audio.
Telephony audio
05
#### Two-Person Army Award
The best project built by a team of two.
Duos
06
#### Solo Ninja Award
The best project built by a single participant.
Solo
07
#### Jugaad Genius Award
The most creative or unexpected use of Gnani AI's models.
Creativity
08
#### Small Town, Big Build Award
The best entry from a college or city in a Tier 2 or Tier 3 town.
Beyond the metros
09
#### Demo Day Drop Award
The best 60-second demo video.
60-second video
10
#### Crowd Favourite Award
Decided by public votes on LinkedIn and X using #GreatIndianAIInternshipChallenge & #GnaniAI.
Public vote
LinkedIn
X
Awards are decided on each category's criteria, irrespective of internship selection. No individual or team can win more than one award. Purchased votes, bots and engagement exchanges don't count towards Crowd Favourite or any other award.
#### Need a starting point?
The brief is open, so these are ideas, not requirements. Each one maps to an award category.
A Kannada voice helpline that reads out crop and weather advisories for farmers.
Main Character, Real Deal
A Hinglish voice assistant that takes phone orders for a neighbourhood kirana store.
Mixed Vibes, Real Deal
A call summariser that holds up on noisy phone audio, tested on synthetic calls.
Noise Canceller
A Tamil voice tutor that quizzes students out loud and explains the answers.
Jugaad Genius
What you build on
### Models trained in India, for Indian speech
Gnani AI builds its own speech and language models and trains them on real telephonic audio, so they handle noisy calls, code-mixed speech and Indian languages natively. Deployed together on infrastructure the customer controls, they form
Artha, the sovereign stack
. You get to build on the same models.
Speech to text
#### Prisma v2.5
Trained on 14M+ hours of telephonic audio. Streams in under 200ms across 10+ Indian languages plus Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish, according to Gnani AI's published benchmarks.
Speech to text API
Text to speech, Beta
#### Timbre v2.5
Speaks 10+ Indic languages with context-aware prosody, Indian names, numerals and lakh and crore cadence. Streams over WebSocket and SSE.
Text to speech API
Reasoning, open weight
#### Evon v3.3
A 30B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 128K context and 11 Indian languages natively. Apache 2.0 weights are available by request on Hugging Face.
Evon v3.3 release notes
Eligibility
### Who can apply
The programme is open to students. Check all three conditions before you register.
#### You must be
✓
Currently enrolled in a degree or course at a college or university in India.
18 years or older on the day you register.
Building solo, or with one teammate who also meets these conditions.
#### Solo or a team of two
You register, build and submit on your own.
Team of two
You register and add your one teammate's email. Teams can't be larger than two.
Your teammate accepts the terms independently. Gnani AI keeps their email on record only to verify their eligibility and participation. All contest communication goes to the primary registrant, and each of you is interviewed and considered for an offer individually.
Read before you register
### The rules that matter most
These points shape who gets an offer. The full terms appear on the registration page, and every participant accepts them individually.
1
#### Offers and stipends are individual
Teammates are interviewed separately, and one can receive an offer without the other. Stipends of up to ₹1 lakh a month are paid per intern, never split.
2
#### The brief is open
There's no set problem statement. Build any working application on Gnani AI's models or APIs.
3
#### Your project uses Gnani AI technology
Your submission names the Gnani AI models or APIs it uses and each member's contribution.
4
#### You demo it in public
Post your project on LinkedIn or X with the hashtags #GnaniAI and #GreatIndianAIInternshipChallenge, then nominate those posts in your submission. The post has to be live before you submit.
5
#### The deadline is fixed
Final submissions close at 18:00 PM IST on November 15, 2026. You can edit project details until you submit.
6
#### Keep it authentic
Bought engagement, bots, paid promotion, engagement swaps, plagiarism and misleading demos aren't allowed. Entries with substantiated breaches may be disqualified.
An internship is confirmed only by a written offer from Gnani AI after the interview stage. Gnani AI may modify, suspend or cancel any part of the contest, including rules, timelines and prizes, as set out in the programme terms.
How it works
### Register, build, post, submit
A finished entry is a working application built on at least one Gnani AI model or API, shown working in a public video. Here is what you'll need at each step, so you can prepare before you start.
Step 1
#### Register
Full name, email and phone
College name, degree or course, discipline
Year of study, graduation year and city
Solo or team, and your teammate's email
Each teammate is deemed to accept the contest terms.
Step 2
#### Build
Project title
The problem you are solving
Who will use it
The Gnani AI models or APIs you use
Each member's contribution
You can update these details until your final submission.
Step 3
#### Post your demo
Record a video of your application working
Post it on LinkedIn, X or both
Explain what you built and the Gnani AI technology used
Tag Gnani AI and add #GreatIndianAIInternshipChallenge and #GnaniAI
Tagging alone doesn't complete your entry. You nominate the post in step 4.
Step 4
#### Submit
Your demo video
A written project explanation
The Gnani AI models or APIs you used
One nominated post link per platform
Submit by 18:00 PM IST on November 15, 2026.
Build resources
### Everything you need to ship
Each registration receives 5,000 programme credits. For teams of two, the credits go to the primary registrant's account, and access instructions arrive by email after sign up. Start with the quick start in the
Gnani AI developer docs
, then open the console to create your keys.
API dashboard
Create keys, test voices and track usage against your credits.
Documentation
API reference for speech to text, text to speech and streaming.
Quick start
Make your first transcription and synthesis call from the docs.
Evon v3.3 on Hugging Face
Open weights under Apache 2.0, available by request.
Model overview
Prisma, Timbre, Warp and Evon, with their published specs.
Support on Discord
Ask build questions and get help from the Gnani AI team.
Selection process
### From submission to written offer
Verified engagement on your public demo decides the shortlist. Your skills and your interview decide the offer.
#### Engagement check
Gnani AI verifies reactions, comments and reshares on your nominated posts, recorded by the closing cutoff.
Nominated posts
Verified
#### Eligibility check
Entries must show genuine use of Gnani AI technology and meet the participation requirements.
Gnani AI tech
Rules
#### Shortlisting
The eligible projects with the strongest verified engagement are shortlisted for interview.
Project level
#### Interviews
Every shortlisted person interviews on their own, including both members of a team.
One to one
Individual
#### Written offers
Offers and stipends depend on each candidate's assessed skills, interview performance and fit for available roles.
Stipend
Terms
Timeline
### Key dates
Just under six weeks to build, then review and interviews, then six months inside Gnani AI.
Build window
41 days
Review and interviews
after close
Internship
6 months
Contest starts
Oct 1, 2026
Registration opens and the build window starts.
Build window starts
Contest close
Final submissions close at 18:00 PM IST.
Final submission
After close
Interviews
Shortlisted participants interview individually.
Shortlisted only
Internships start
Jan 1, 2027
Paid six-month internships are scheduled to begin.
Six months, paid
FAQs
### Questions before you register
The programme terms on the registration page are the final word. These answers summarise them.
Is there a problem statement?
No. The brief is open. Build any working application on Gnani AI's models or APIs that addresses a practical need for enterprises, developers or creators.
Do I need to post my demo before I submit?
Yes. Your submission asks for links to your demo posts, so post first. Nominate one post per platform through your submission. Tagging Gnani AI alone doesn't complete your entry.
What can get an entry disqualified?
Purchased engagement, bots, paid promotion, engagement exchanges, plagiarism and misleading demonstrations are not permitted. Invalid interactions may be excluded, and entries involving substantiated breaches may be disqualified.
How does the stipend work?
Each selected intern receives an individual stipend of up to ₹1 lakh per month. The figure is a ceiling, not a fixed amount, and it is not shared between teammates. Your exact stipend appears in your written offer.
If we apply as a team, are we selected together?
No. Teams of two build and submit one project, but each member is interviewed on their own and considered for an offer separately. One teammate can be selected without the other, so record each person's contribution clearly in your project details.
When and how does the internship run?
Internships run for six months and are scheduled to start from January 1, 2027. Location and working arrangements are confirmed in each written offer.
Does it cost anything to take part?
Every registered participant receives 5,000 programme credits to build with. The terms explain what the credits cover and how usage is handled, and your dashboard shows usage against your credits as you build.
How is my data handled?
Gnani AI uses your registration details to run the programme, assess submissions and contact you about selection. The
Gnani AI privacy policy
explains how personal data is processed. Don't put anyone's real phone numbers, account numbers, Aadhaar, PAN or recorded calls into your project or demo. Use synthetic data.
Can I change my project after registering?
Yes. You can update the title, problem, users, models and contributions at any time until you make your final submission.
Can I submit more than one entry?
No. Each participant or team can submit one entry.
Where do I build?
On the Gnani AI API platform at
app.gnani.ai/voice
. Sign in with the email you registered with, then create your API keys and track your credit usage from the dashboard. Docs and quick starts are at
docs.gnani.ai
.
I don't have an institutional email, or mine isn't working. What do I do?
We're opening access to non-institutional emails in the second week of October, so you don't need to write in. Once it's live, you can sign in with your personal email.
Can I use the agent builder? Why can't I find API keys for it?
This challenge covers the API platform at
only. The agent builder sits outside the scope of this internship, and we don't offer APIs for it yet. Your credits work on the models hosted on the API platform.
How do I use Evon?
Evon v3.3 isn't on the API platform yet. It's open weights, so you can request the weights on
Hugging Face
and run it yourself.
Is there a participant workspace?
No. You describe your project and share your build through the submission form sent to your email. There's no dashboard to manage.
Where do I get help?
Ask build and API questions in the
Gnani AI Discord community
. The
developer docs
cover authentication, streaming and code samples.
Are awards linked to the internship shortlist?
No. Awards are given on the category criteria, irrespective of internship selection.
Can a team or individual win more than one award?
No. Each team or individual can win a maximum of one award, and each award is worth ₹50,000.
Deadline 18:00 PM IST, November 15, 2026
### Ship something real on Indian-language AI
Register, claim your 5,000 credits and start building. Up to 100 paid six-month internships and ten ₹50,000 awards go to the people who ship.

## Cookie Policy
### What Are Cookies
As is common practice with almost all professional websites this site uses cookies, which are tiny files that are downloaded to your computer, to improve your experience. This page describes what information they gather, how we use it, and why we sometimes need to store these cookies. We will also share how you can prevent these cookies from being stored however this may downgrade or ‘break’ certain elements of the site’s functionality.
### How We Use Cookies
We use cookies for a variety of reasons detailed below. Unfortunately, in most cases, there are no industry standard options for disabling cookies without completely disabling the functionality and features they add to this site. It is recommended that you leave on all cookies if you are not sure whether you need them or not in case they are used to provide a service that you use.
### Disabling Cookies
You can prevent the setting of cookies by adjusting the settings on your browser (see your browser Help for how to do this). Be aware that disabling cookies will affect the functionality of this and many other websites that you visit. Disabling cookies will usually result in also disabling certain functionality and features of this site. Therefore it is recommended that you do not disable cookies.
### The Cookies We Set
Email newsletters related cookies
: This site offers newsletter or email subscription services and cookies may be used to remember if you are already registered and whether to show certain notifications which might only be valid to subscribed/unsubscribed users.
Forms related cookies
: When you submit data through a form such as those found on contact pages or comment forms cookies may be set to remember your user details for future correspondence.
### Third-Party Cookies
In some special cases, we also use cookies provided by trusted third parties. The following section details which third party cookies you might encounter through this site.
This site uses Google Analytics which is one of the most widespread and trusted analytics solutions on the web for helping us to understand how you use the site and ways that we can improve your experience. These cookies may track things such as how long you spend on the site and the pages that you visit so we can continue to produce engaging content. For more information on Google Analytics cookies, see the official Google Analytics page.
Third-party analytics are used to track and measure usage of this site so that we can continue to produce engaging content. These cookies may track things such as how long you spend on the site or pages you visit which helps us to understand how we can improve the site for you.
From time to time we test new features and make subtle changes to the way that the site is delivered. When we are still testing new features these cookies may be used to ensure that you receive a consistent experience whilst on the site whilst ensuring we understand which optimizations our users appreciate the most.
We use adverts to offset the costs of running this site and provide funding for further development. The behavioral advertising cookies used by this site are designed to ensure that we provide you with the most relevant adverts where possible by anonymously tracking your interests and presenting similar things that may be of interest.
We also use social media buttons and/or plugins on this site that allow you to connect with your social network in various ways. For these to work the following social media sites including; {List the social networks whose features you have integrated with your site?:12}, will set cookies through our site which may be used to enhance your profile on their site or contribute to the data they hold for various purposes outlined in their respective privacy policies.
### More Information
Hopefully, that has clarified things for you, and as was previously mentioned if there is something that you aren’t sure whether you need or not it’s usually safer to leave cookies enabled in case it does interact with one of the features you use on our site.
However, if you are still looking for more information then you can contact us through one of our preferred contact methods:
