Conversational AI use cases in ecommerce, ordered by speed of payback
#### Order status and delivery exceptions
This is the single largest contact driver in most retail operations, and it is fully automatable because the answer is a database lookup. The useful version goes further than reading the tracking status back: it handles the exception. The courier could not reach the address, the shopper was not home, the delivery slot needs to move. An agent that can reschedule, confirm an alternate address or trigger a redelivery closes the loop instead of creating a second contact.
#### Returns, exchanges and refund status
Returns are policy-bound, which suits automation. The agent checks eligibility against the return window and the item category, books the pickup, and tells the shopper when the refund will land. The failure mode to design against is the edge case, so the handoff matters:
Gnani Agents
passes a conversation to a human with the full history attached, so the shopper does not start again.
#### Cash on delivery confirmation
In markets where cash on delivery is a large share of orders, unconfirmed orders become failed deliveries, and failed deliveries become reverse logistics cost. An outbound voice agent confirming the order before dispatch removes a measurable slice of that cost. This is outbound telephony, so consent and DND obligations under TRAI rules apply, and the agent must disclose that it is AI at the start of the call. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
#### Abandoned cart and payment recovery
A failed payment is a shopper who already decided to buy. Reaching them within minutes, on WhatsApp or by voice, with a working payment link recovers orders that an email sequence will not. The same pattern covers instalment and pay-later reminders, which overlaps with the collections workflows in
Gnani AI for collections
.
#### Product discovery and guided selling
This is the use case that gets demonstrated most and deployed least, because it is the hardest to get right and the easiest to get wrong in front of a customer. It works when the catalogue is structured, the attributes are clean and the question is narrow, such as size, compatibility or availability. It works poorly as an open-ended shopping assistant. Treat it as a second-phase project, after the operational use cases are stable.
#### Post-purchase feedback and review collection
A short voice or WhatsApp conversation a few days after delivery collects far more responses than an email survey, and the free-text answers are richer. Running those conversations through
Gnani Analytics
turns them into topic and sentiment data across the whole respondent base rather than a sample.
#### Agent assist for the conversations that stay human
Complex cases, high-value customers and angry shoppers should reach a person. What changes is what that person has in front of them.
Gnani Assist
retrieves policy and order context mid-call and writes the summary and CRM update afterwards, and reports 18% improvement in agent efficiency, 70% faster time to proficiency and a 90%+ reduction in after-call admin.
### What to get right before you launch
Integration first, conversation second.
The agent needs live read and write access to order management, payments and the returns system. Without it you have a chatbot that apologises.
Design the handoff, not just the happy path.
Decide in advance which intents escalate, and make sure the human inherits the transcript. Conversations that restart from zero cost more than the deflection saved.
Disclose that the agent is AI.
This goes in the opening line of every script, voice and text.
Protect the data.
Order records, phone numbers and payment references are personal data under the DPDP Act. Where the model runs decides whether the deployment is compliant, which is why
Artha
supports on-premise and air-gapped deployment alongside cloud.
Measure containment and repeat contact together.
Containment alone rewards an agent that ends conversations. Repeat contact rate within 48 hours tells you whether the conversation actually resolved anything.
### How fast this goes live
The build is no longer the bottleneck.
reports under 20 minutes to go live for a configured agent, with prebuilt integrations into Freshdesk, Salesforce, Zendesk, SAP and Oracle, and context-aware handoff to a human carrying the full conversation history. The platform reports 60%+ reduction in operational costs and 80% of issues resolved on the first call across its deployments, with under 800ms response latency in live conversations.
The bottleneck is scope. Retail teams that try to launch discovery, support, returns and outbound in one release spend two quarters on a pilot. Teams that launch order status alone, prove containment, then add returns and cash on delivery confirmation, tend to be running real volume inside a month.
### Where conversational AI in ecommerce goes next
Three things are changing at once. Voice is getting good enough on ordinary phone lines that it stops being the channel of last resort, which matters in markets where most shoppers never install the retailer's app. Agents are becoming able to act rather than answer, so the measure shifts from deflection rate to orders saved and refunds processed. And language coverage is widening, with Gnani AI supporting 40+ languages at model level and 10+ Indic languages in production ASR.
Conversational AI in ecommerce is worth building where the conversation is repetitive, data-backed and high volume. That is most of retail support, most of the time. Teams sizing a rollout can review the
Gnani AI solutions
stack or
book a demo
to walk through their own contact mix.
### Frequently asked questions
What is conversational AI in ecommerce?
Conversational AI in ecommerce is an agent that holds a two-way conversation with a shopper across voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS and can act on the result rather than only answer. It reads and writes to order management, payments and returns systems, so it can reschedule a delivery or book a pickup rather than only read a status back.
Which ecommerce use cases pay back fastest?
Order status and delivery exceptions, because that is the largest contact driver in most retail operations and the answer is a database lookup. Returns and refund status, cash on delivery confirmation and payment recovery follow. Product discovery is the slowest to get right and belongs in a second phase.
Can conversational AI handle returns and refunds end to end?
Yes, because returns are policy-bound. The agent checks eligibility against the return window and item category, books the pickup and tells the shopper when the refund will land. Design the escalation path for edge cases so the shopper does not have to start again with a human.
What should an ecommerce team measure?
Containment rate and repeat contact rate within 48 hours, together. Containment alone rewards an agent that ends conversations rather than resolving them. For outbound use cases, measure recovered order value per thousand contacts and failed delivery rate.
What rules apply to outbound ecommerce calls in India?
Outbound telephony carries TRAI consent and DND obligations, and the agent must disclose that it is AI at the start of the call. Order records and phone numbers are personal data under the DPDP Act. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.

### Using Conversational AI and Chatbots to Transform the Neobanking Experience
Neobanking, a.k.a. challenger banks emerged from the mounting demand for easy and round-the-clock access to efficient banking processes. With no physical offices & branches, the level of precision, efficiency, and ability to handle load is a deal-breaker. These make Conversational AI and chatbots natural choices for creating the perfect Neo-Banking experience. They successfully enable Neo-Banks to run low-cost, easy-to-use, and digitally accessible services. Think of Neo-Banking and conversational AI like two peas in a pod.
### Benefits of Using Convrsational AI in Banking and Financial Services
Traditionally, banks have relied on physical branches and call centers to provide customer support and handle transactions. However, the rise of neobanking has enabled customers to perform many banking tasks digitally through a mobile app or website. There are several benefits of using conversational AI and chatbots in neobanking:
24/7 Support
: One of the key benefits of using conversational AI and chatbots in neobanking is the ability to provide 24/7 support to customers. With chatbots, customers can get quick answers to their questions or resolve issues at any time of day without having to wait on hold or schedule an appointment at a physical branch. This improves the customer experience and frees up human staff to focus on more complex tasks.
Personalization:
Another advantage of using conversational AI and chatbots in neobanking is the ability to personalize the customer experience. Chatbots can gather information about a customer's preferences and history and use that data to provide personalized recommendations and solutions. For example, a chatbot might suggest a particular credit card or investment product based on a customer's spending habits or financial goals.
Streamlined operations:
The use of conversational AI and chatbots in neobanking can also help banks streamline their operations and save costs. By automating routine tasks and providing instant support to customers, chatbots can help banks reduce the need for human staff and lower overhead expenses.
Improved customer experience & customer loyalty:
Chatbots can provide instant support and personalized recommendations, leading to a more convenient and enjoyable banking experience and help banks increase customer loyalty and retention by providing exceptional customer service and support. As the neobanking industry grows and evolves, we will see more and more banks adopting these innovative solutions.
### Challenges of Neobanking
As with life, no business is without its fair share of problems. Neobanking also faces unique challenges, albeit solvable hurdles. These challenges will only pave the way for further innovation as the industry matures.So, what are some of the challenges that Neobanks are facing today?
#### Attrition of Differentiators
Neobanking is arguably the next significant innovation that challenges the traditional banking system. However, their success depends on how well they sustain the stack of differentiators that created their space in the first place. Factors such as digital distrust, limited services, security, and dependence on other financial institutions are watering down their key differentiators.
#### Regulation
The disparity in financial regulations across countries doesn’t make it any easier for Neo-Banks to make their mark. It obstructs them from entering and growing within specific markets. Neo-Banks need a robust regulatory framework and sound-proof digital banking license systems to deliver value for existing customers and expand.
#### Big Banks owning Neobanks
Although there is an appetite for Neobanking, legacy financial institutions continue to dominate the market. Large banking institutions pose an existential challenge to Neo-Banks because a) they have more resources and b) can bypass regulatory restrictions in many countries. For example, the acquisitions of Anytime Digital Bank by Orange bank and 86 by National Australia Bank have helped these financial juggernauts subdue competition and increase their customer base.Impact of Covid-19Neobanks have grown in popularity recently, and the COVID-19 pandemic has only accelerated this trend. However, it's important to note that customer loyalty is not guaranteed in the neobanking industry. Many customers still prefer traditional banks that they are familiar with, and more than the limited services offered by neobanks may be needed to attract and retain customers. Neobanks may need to invest in technologies like reports and data analysis and expand their services to improve customer experience and increase loyalty.
#### Convincing Customers to Switch from Traditional Banking
Neobanks may struggle to gain customers' trust who may be hesitant to switch to a digital banking only or may not be familiar with the new technology. From a global standpoint, users have been slow to adopt Neobanking. A report says that even among their most lucrative customers, i.e. millennials,
only 3% have used Neobanking in the last 8 to 10 years
. The journey of transitioning a customer towards Neobanking isn’t easy since the services offered are minimal as compared to legacy banks.
### How can Conversational AI solve Neobanking Challenges?
Relevance is in the very DNA of Conversational AI. It syncs seamlessly with new technologies such as Neobanking. The shared objectives of increasing efficiency and convenience make conversational AI a natural choice to create the perfect customer experience. It enables Neobanks to run low-cost, easy-to-use, and digitally accessible services.
#### Credit Decisions
The old saying ‘Cash is King’ is dead. Credit is the new overlord in town! Over time, the use of plastic money became more dominant than cash. Conversational AI
enables smarter assessments in the credit decision-making process
. In other words, it helps facilitate responsible lending. Today, credit unions are open to accepting insights from Conversational AI to boost customer satisfaction (CSAT) and improve banking experience.
#### Risk Management
As an emerging banking solution, Neobanking must be extra cautious in risk management. It needs an improved mechanism to understand, predict, and protect against predictable or unpredictable risks. Conversational AI can forecast events, detect fraud, and analyze patterns to suggest contingency plans in the case of a threat.
#### Personalized Banking & Advice
Bill Gates once said that “Banking is necessary, banks are not.”Neobanks emerged amidst the digital era when customers began to prefer personalization services and trusted advice. Several studies showed that over time, customers began to feel more comfortable interacting with chatbots and voice bots during the banking process.Portfolio Management in TradingTraders are constantly dealing with volatile markets, and conversational AI can help in providing technical analytics along with predictions to assist in assessing transaction costs. It can also break down big-sized trades into parts for better pricing options. Being available 24×7 and data load management are key advantages in this sector.
#### Speeds up the Process
The effectiveness of a neobank's customer journey can be determined by how quickly issues are resolved, how many touch points are created, and the overall response rate. Conversational AI can help by collecting feedback at every stage and providing timely responses without relying on human intervention. This can help neobanks engage at-risk customers in real time and improve relationships using digital technology.
#### Collects Data
Data aggregation and analysis are crucial for understanding and improving customer journeys and neobanking processes. Voice bots and chatbots can analyze large amounts of customer conversation data to gain insights and deliver actionable recommendations.
#### Personalizes the Experience
It is important for businesses to think beyond just personalized messages. Today’s consumers are spoiled for choice with tailor-made services and products. Conversational AI can help with custom-made services and also create opportunities for personalization. They are designed to speak different languages and dialects, so catering to different demographics becomes a cakewalk.
#### The future of Neobanking
As neobanks work to improve their service offerings and products, it's clear that conversational AI will be a valuable resource in achieving their goals. Using AI-powered voice bots and chatbots on various channels and platforms, neobanks can prioritize customer satisfaction and build loyalty. This can ultimately help them increase their market share over time. By utilizing digital solutions like conversational AI, neobanks can streamline their operations, reduce the need for human resources, and provide personalized and instant support to customers. To effectively implement these solutions, neobanks can use reports and data analysis to identify areas for improvement and make informed decisions about their use of conversational AI.If you’re a Neobanking service provider who is looking to up their game,

see how Gnani.ai’s solutions can help create better experiences for your customers.

What is conversational AI and how does it help transform the neobanking experience?
Conversational AI is the use of natural language processing and machine learning to enable computers to have conversations with humans. In neobanking, it helps enhance customer experience by providing 24/7 support, quick resolutions, and personalized services through chatbots.
Can chatbots in neobanking handle complex customer inquiries?
It depends on the sophistication of the chatbot. Advanced chatbots can handle a wide range of inquiries, while simple ones may only handle basic queries. Neobanks can continuously improve their chatbots with machine learning to better handle complex inquiries.

Neobanks can measure the success of their chatbot implementation by tracking metrics such as customer satisfaction, resolution time, and the number of inquiries handled.

TL;DR:
Customer onboarding automation uses a conversational agent to collect, verify and confirm everything a new customer has to provide before the account goes live. It works because onboarding is a fixed sequence of known fields with a rule at the end of each one. Voice carries it further than a form in Indian markets, because a customer who abandons a twelve-field web page will finish the same sequence on a phone call in their own language. The failure mode is almost never the conversation. It is the integration into the system that has to accept the data, and the compliance trail around it.
### What customer onboarding automation actually covers
Onboarding is the stretch between a customer saying yes and the account doing something useful. In banking that means identity verification, document capture, risk scoring and first funding. In telecom it means activation, plan selection and device pairing. In insurance it means proposal capture, medical declarations and the first premium.
The structure is the same underneath. A fixed sequence of fields, a verification step on several of them, a decision rule, and a handoff to a human when the rule cannot fire. That shape is what makes the workflow automatable, and it is also what makes a badly built agent obvious within two steps.
The old generation of automation here was the touch-tone menu, which asked the customer to map their intent onto a numbered list. Modern speech models remove the mapping step. The customer says what they have, the agent takes it, reads back what it captured, and writes it to the system of record.
Gnani Agents
runs that sequence across voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS, with context-aware handoff to a human that carries the conversation history rather than restarting it.
Gnani AI reports under 800ms response latency in live conversations and under 20 minutes to go live on a configured workflow. Both figures come from the company's own product pages, so treat them as the vendor-stated starting point for your own test rather than as a benchmark.
ENTERPRISE VOICE AI
See Gnani AI's Voice AI Agent in action
200+ Enterprises · 30M daily calls · 10 Indic languages
Book A Demo
### Why voice outperforms a form in Indian onboarding
Form abandonment is a reach problem before it is a design problem. A customer who is comfortable in Marathi or Telugu but not in written English will stall on a form long before they stall on a conversation, and no amount of field-level optimisation closes that gap.
Voice also collects data that a form collects badly. Spoken addresses, names with regional spellings and reference numbers read aloud are all easier to capture and confirm in dialogue, because the agent can read the value back and correct it on the spot. A form finds out it got the address wrong when the courier fails.
The engineering bar is real, though. Onboarding calls arrive over 8kHz telephony, in noise, with the customer switching between English and their own language mid-sentence.
Prisma v2.5
is trained on 14M+ hours of real telephonic audio for exactly that condition, and Gnani AI reports 96% code-switching accuracy and under 4% word error rate on Indian speech from its own published benchmarks. Run those numbers against a sample of your own recordings before you size the project.
On the output side,
Timbre v2.5
(Beta) handles the part that makes read-backs work: lakh and crore cadence, Indian names and numerals, and Hindi-English code-switching. A voice that reads "one lakh twenty thousand" as "one hundred twenty thousand" loses the customer's trust at the exact moment the agent is confirming a number.
### Onboarding automation by industry
#### Banking and digital KYC
The agent collects identity details, triggers the document capture link, confirms what came back, and routes anything the risk rule flags to a human reviewer. The compliance surface is the whole game here, because the conversation carries identity numbers and the audit trail has to survive an RBI inspection. See the
banking voice AI solutions
page for how the workflow is configured against core banking systems.
#### Telecom activation and plan selection
Activation is the highest volume onboarding workflow in telecom and the one customers most want finished on the first call. The agent confirms the plan, walks the activation steps, and schedules a callback where a step depends on the network side. Our post on
conversational AI in telecom customer service
covers the wider service workload around it.
#### Insurance proposal capture
Proposal capture is long, and length is what kills completion rates. An agent that can pause, save state and resume on a later call finishes proposals that a single web session loses. Medical declarations need the same clinician-style boundary as healthcare workflows: the agent captures and routes, and an underwriter decides. The
insurance voice AI solutions
page sets out the integration points.
#### Retail and consumer durables
Registration, warranty activation and service scheduling are short workflows with high volume and low risk, which makes them a sensible first build. They also give you a working integration to the CRM that the higher-value workflows will reuse.

### What to measure, and what to ignore
Completion rate on the target workflow is the number that matters, measured from first contact to account live rather than from first contact to end of call. An agent that finishes the conversation but leaves the account in a pending queue has moved the bottleneck, not removed it.
Three supporting metrics are worth instrumenting from day one. Time to account live, which is the customer-visible outcome. Escalation rate broken down by step, which tells you where the agent is actually failing. And the rate of data corrections made after the fact, which is the honest measure of capture quality.
Containment rate on its own is a vanity metric in onboarding. A high containment rate with a low completion rate means the agent is keeping customers in a conversation that goes nowhere.
Gnani Analytics
scores the full conversation corpus rather than a sample, which is what makes step-level failure visible.
### Compliance in an automated onboarding flow
Onboarding automation sits on top of several regimes at once, and which ones apply depends on the industry and the channel rather than on the technology.
The DPDP Act governs the personal data the agent collects from any Indian customer, including consent capture and deletion.
RBI guidance applies to KYC and account opening in BFSI, including the audit trail and the record of who or what made each decision.
IRDAI applies to insurance proposal capture and the disclosures inside it.
TRAI rules govern outbound calling, consent and do-not-disturb registration, which matters for every onboarding workflow that calls the customer rather than waiting to be called.
The agent must disclose that it is AI, in the opening line of the script, on every channel.
Where the data is allowed to sit is often the constraint that decides the architecture.
Artha
is the sovereign deployment of the Gnani AI stack, running the models on infrastructure the customer controls so that residency requirements are met by where the model runs rather than by a contractual promise. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
### Building the first workflow
Start with the onboarding step that carries the most volume and the least judgement, then confirm three things before anyone writes a prompt. Does an integration already exist into the system that has to accept the data? Is there a written rule for every decision the agent will make? And can you name the completion metric you expect to move inside one quarter?
Most teams find the answer is activation in telecom, registration in retail, and the document-capture step in banking. None of those is the most impressive workflow available. All three give you the integration and the audit pattern that the harder ones depend on.
### Where to start
Customer onboarding automation earns its keep on the steps that are high volume, rule driven and measurable, and it fails on the ones that need judgement. Pick the narrow workflow, instrument completion rather than containment, and get the compliance trail designed before the first script. You can compare the underlying models on the
Gnani AI models
page, or
book a demo
to scope a first build.
### Frequently asked questions
What is customer onboarding automation?
Customer onboarding automation uses software to collect, verify and confirm the information a new customer has to supply before their account goes live, without a human running the conversation. In a voice deployment, an AI agent takes the details over a call, reads them back, checks them against the systems of record, and escalates anything a rule cannot decide.
Does automated onboarding work for KYC?
Yes for the capture and confirmation steps, with the decision routed to a reviewer where regulation requires a human. The agent collects identity details, triggers document capture and confirms what came back. The risk decision and the final approval stay with a person, and the audit trail has to record which was which.
How is a voice agent different from an IVR?
An IVR asks the customer to map what they want onto a numbered menu, and it fails when their need does not fit the list. A voice agent takes natural speech, holds context across the conversation, and can both ask for and return information. In onboarding the practical difference is that the agent can correct a captured value mid-call instead of dropping the customer into a queue.
Which languages does onboarding automation need in India?
More than the headline count suggests, and the quality bar is telephonic rather than studio. Prisma v2.5 runs 10+ Indian languages in production speech recognition plus Hinglish, Tamil-English and Bengali-English code-switching, and Timbre v2.5 (Beta) covers 10+ Indic languages for speech output. Test a code-switched call with a real address in it, because that is where capture accuracy breaks.
How long does it take to deploy onboarding automation?
The integration and the compliance review set the timeline. A workflow that writes into a system with an existing API moves quickly. A workflow that needs a new interface into a legacy core system, plus a security review, takes considerably longer, and the two run in parallel rather than one after the other.

### Contact center automation, and what it actually replaces
TL;DR:
Contact center automation is the use of software to handle customer interactions end to end instead of routing every one to a person. Modern automation runs on conversational AI rather than menu trees: the caller states the problem in their own words, the system identifies the intent, authenticates them, acts in the systems of record, and either confirms the outcome or hands to a human with full context. The practical measure is containment, meaning the share of contacts resolved without an agent, and the practical risk is automating the wrong intents.
Most contact centres already run automation. It is the IVR, and it is the thing customers complain about. The question in 2026 is not whether to automate but whether to keep automating with menus, which deflect by exhausting the caller, or with systems that actually finish the task. This guide covers where IVR fails, what replaces it, which intents are worth automating first, and how to measure whether it worked.
### Why IVR hit its ceiling
Interactive voice response was built for a constraint that no longer applies. Touch-tone input meant the system could only receive a digit, so the interaction had to be shaped as a menu. Every limitation follows from that.
The caller has to map their problem onto your org chart.
They know their card stopped working. They do not know whether that is Cards, Fraud or Disputes.
Menus deepen as the business grows.
Each new option adds a branch, and callers abandon or press zero.
Nothing carries forward.
A caller who traverses four levels and reaches an agent usually starts again from the beginning.
It cannot handle two things at once.
A caller with a billing dispute and an address change has to call twice.
Pressing zero defeats it.
Experienced customers skip the automation entirely, so the deflection is on paper.
The common mistake is reading this as an argument for removing IVR. Simple, stable, low-variance routing still works fine as a menu, and it is cheap. The argument is for stopping the practice of forcing high-variance intents through a structure that cannot represent them.
ENTERPRISE VOICE AI
See Gnani AI's Voice AI Agent in action
200+ Enterprises · 30M daily calls · 10 Indic languages
Book A Demo
### IVR and conversational AI compared
The difference is not voice quality. It is how much of the task the software is permitted to complete, and what happens when the conversation leaves the expected path.
Traditional IVR and conversational AI automation
Dimension
Traditional IVR
Conversational AI
Caller input
Digit presses against a fixed menu
Natural speech in the caller's own words
Finding the right path
Caller maps their problem onto your org chart
System infers intent from the description
Two requests in one call
Not supported, caller rings back
Handled in sequence within one conversation
Off-script input
Loops, repeats the menu, or drops to a queue
Re-plans and continues toward the goal
Code-mixed speech
Not applicable, input is numeric
Supported where the speech model is trained for it
Completing the task
Transfers, or reads a value back
Reads and writes to systems of record
Handoff to an agent
Caller repeats everything from the start
Conversation history passed with the transfer
Adding a new flow
Re-cut the menu tree, re-record prompts
Add the intent and connect the system call
Typical failure mode
Caller presses zero and the deflection is on paper
Wrong intent automated, so containment hides a repeat contact
Best suited to
Simple, stable, low-variance routing
High-volume intents that end in a system action
Running both is normal. Keep the menu for the handful of intents where it performs, and route everything else to the conversational layer. Replacing a working IVR wholesale on day one is how these programmes acquire a bad internal reputation before they have proved anything.
### Which intents to automate first
Containment targets set before intent analysis are guesses. The sequence that works is to rank intents by volume, then filter by three tests.
Does it end in a system action?
Balance enquiries, payment collection, appointment booking, address changes and order status all resolve by reading or writing a record. These are the natural first candidates.
Is the outcome reversible?
Automate the reversible before the irreversible. A wrongly booked appointment is a nuisance. A wrongly processed account closure is an incident.
Is the emotional load low?
Bereavement, fraud reports, complaints and hardship cases go to people. Containment is the wrong metric for a distressed customer, and automating these intents produces complaints that cost more than the agent minutes saved.
Collections is the case that repays the most attention, because volume is high, outcomes are structured, and the conversation follows a pattern. Gnani AI groups these flows under
collections and recovery voice AI
. Outbound calling brings TRAI consent and DND obligations, so the compliance work has to happen before the automation work.
### What the stack has to do in Indian contact centres
Automation that performs on clean English audio and degrades on a real queue is the standard disappointment. Indian telephony is 8kHz, noisy, and heavily code-mixed, and the caller will not adjust how they speak.
Speech recognition carries the first risk. Gnani AI's
Prisma v2.5 speech to text model
is trained on 14M+ hours of real telephonic audio, and Gnani AI reports under 4% word error rate on Indian speech, 96% code-switching accuracy across Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish, sub-200ms streaming latency and 35,000+ simultaneous streams. Those figures are measured on telephony audio, so they are not directly comparable to vendor numbers measured on clean studio recordings.
The spoken reply has to sound like a person handling Indian numerals and names. Gnani AI's
Timbre v2.5 text to speech model
, in Beta, covers 10+ Indic languages with lakh and crore cadence, and Gnani AI reports a mean opinion score of 4.23 on 8kHz telephony and sub-100ms time to first audio.
The whole loop has to fit inside conversational timing. Gnani AI reports under 800ms response latency for
Gnani Agents
in live conversations, alongside 40+ languages, context-aware handoff carrying full conversation history, and integrations with Avaya, Cisco, Five9, Vonage, Freshdesk, Salesforce, Zendesk, SAP and Oracle.
### Automating the agent's work, not just the call
Containment is only half the available saving. The other half sits in what agents do around the conversation: searching for policy, writing notes, updating the CRM and waiting for QA feedback that arrives weeks later.
Gnani Assist
works this side of the problem, retrieving policy mid-call, suggesting next actions and generating summaries. Gnani AI reports 18% improvement in agent efficiency, 70% faster time to proficiency and 90%+ reduction in after-call admin.
Quality assurance is the other candidate. Manual QA samples a few calls per agent per month, which is too thin to manage performance or catch compliance drift.
Gnani Analytics
scores the full corpus, and Gnani AI reports 60% reduction in QA costs, 3x more accurate root-cause analysis and 20% improvement in retention.
### Measuring whether it worked
Containment alone is a misleading number, because a system that frustrates callers into hanging up scores well on it. Track containment next to the metrics that catch that failure.
Containment rate, by intent.
An aggregate figure hides the intents that are failing.
Repeat contact within 48 hours.
The cleanest signal that a contained call did not actually resolve.
Escalation reason, not just escalation rate.
Knowing why the system handed over is what drives the next iteration.
Handle time on escalated calls.
Should fall, because context is attached. If it rises, the handoff is losing information.
CSAT split by contained and escalated.
A large gap means the wrong intents are automated.
Gnani AI reports 80% of issues resolved on the first call and 60%+ reduction in operational costs across its deployments. Treat published vendor outcomes as a baseline to test against your own queues rather than as a forecast, because intent mix differs enormously between businesses.
### Governance and the regulatory picture
A contact centre automation programme touches customer data at every step. Call recordings, transcripts and call metadata are personal data under India's DPDP Act, which brings consent, purpose limitation and retention obligations. Banking and lending add RBI expectations, insurance adds IRDAI, outbound calling adds TRAI consent and DND rules, and US healthcare adds HIPAA. If callers are authenticated from their voice, the voiceprint is biometric data and carries a higher bar.
Two practices belong in the design rather than the retrofit. The system discloses that it is AI at the start of every conversation. Every automated decision is logged with the inputs that produced it, so a reviewer can reconstruct what happened. Where data cannot leave the network,
Artha
runs the stack on customer-controlled infrastructure, including on-premise and air-gapped. Gnani AI states it is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and ISO 27001 certified, and HIPAA, GDPR and PCI-DSS compliant. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
### Frequently asked questions
What is contact center automation?
Contact center automation is the use of software to handle customer interactions without routing every one to a person. It covers automated conversations across voice, chat and messaging, plus automation of agent-side work such as knowledge retrieval, call summaries and quality scoring. Modern implementations use conversational AI, so the customer describes the problem in their own words instead of navigating a menu.
How is conversational AI different from IVR?
IVR routes callers through a fixed menu using digit input, so the caller has to map their problem onto your internal structure. Conversational AI identifies intent from natural speech, can handle more than one request in a single call, and completes the task in your systems of record rather than just transferring the call. When the conversation leaves the expected path, IVR loops or fails, while conversational AI re-plans and continues.
Which contact centre tasks should be automated first?
Start with high-volume intents that end in a system action, have reversible outcomes and carry low emotional load. Balance enquiries, payment collection, appointment booking, order status and address changes fit all three tests. Bereavement, fraud reports, complaints and hardship cases should stay with people regardless of volume.
Does contact center automation reduce headcount?
In most deployments it changes what agents handle rather than how many are needed, absorbing repetitive high-volume intents so people take the complex and sensitive cases. Gnani AI reports 60%+ reduction in operational costs across its deployments. The composition of that saving varies by organisation, so model it against your own intent mix rather than assuming it maps to headcount.
How do you measure contact center automation?
Track containment rate by intent alongside repeat contact within 48 hours, escalation reason, handle time on escalated calls, and CSAT split between contained and escalated conversations. Containment on its own is misleading, because a system that frustrates callers into abandoning scores well on it.
Does automation work for Hindi and other Indian languages?
Yes, when the speech models are trained on Indian telephony rather than clean English audio. Gnani AI reports under 4% word error rate on Indian speech and 96% code-switching accuracy for Prisma v2.5 across Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish, measured on 8kHz telephony. Systems that translate into English before interpreting tend to lose politeness registers and regional idioms.

### What is conversational AI for customer engagement?
Conversational AI for customer engagement is the use of AI agents to hold two-way conversations with customers across voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS, at any hour and in the customer's own language. It differs from marketing automation in one respect that matters: the customer can reply, and the system has to do something sensible with the reply.
That distinction decides most of the design. A campaign tool measures sends and opens. A conversational system has to handle a question it did not expect, in a language it was not configured for, from someone who is already annoyed. Most engagement programmes fail at that point rather than at the point of sending.
### Why does conversational AI for customer engagement beat one-way outreach?
Because a reply tells you something a delivery receipt never will. One-way outreach measures whether a message arrived. A conversation tells you why the customer has not renewed, what they were trying to do when they gave up, or which part of the onboarding they could not finish.
There is also a volume argument. Engagement is only worth doing if you can do it at the moment it matters, and the moments that matter are spread unevenly across a day and a year. Staffing a human team for the peak is expensive and staffing it for the average means missing the peak entirely.
The third reason is language. In most Indian portfolios the customers who disengage first are the ones being served in their second language.
Our guide to multilingual voice bots in customer service
covers what changes when the agent speaks the customer's first language.
### Which engagement moments should you automate?
Automate the moments that are predictable, repetitive and time-sensitive, and leave the rest alone. Engagement programmes get diluted when teams try to automate every touchpoint rather than the few where timing changes the outcome.
#### Before the sale
Qualification and scheduling are the useful automations here. An agent that calls a new enquiry within minutes, confirms what the person is looking for and books the next step does more for conversion than a longer nurture sequence does.
#### After the sale
Onboarding is where engagement is won or lost, and it is almost entirely predictable. The steps are known, the sequence is known, and the failure points repeat across customers.
Our guide to automating customer onboarding
covers how to sequence it.
#### At risk of churn
Churn signals arrive before the cancellation does, usually in the tone of a support call rather than in a usage metric.
Our piece on sentiment agents for churn prevention
covers how to act on them. Gnani AI reports that
Gnani Analytics
delivers a 20% improvement in retention and reads sentiment in real time across calls and channels.
### Which channel should each conversation use?
Match the channel to the urgency and the complexity of the reply you want. A question that needs a one-word answer does not need a phone call, and a conversation that needs negotiation does not belong in SMS.
The common mistake is running each channel as its own programme with its own rules, so the customer repeats themselves at every switch.
Our guide to unifying agent behaviour across voice, chat and messaging
covers how to keep one conversation across four channels.
Channel

Where it struggles
Voice
Urgent, emotional or negotiated conversations, and customers who do not read comfortably in the language of your written channels

Web chat

SMS

Gnani AI reports that Gnani Agents runs voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS from one platform, with context-aware handoff to a human carrying the full conversation history. Source: the Gnani AI enterprise page, verified September 2026.
### How do you measure conversational AI for customer engagement?
Measure resolution and retention, not reach. Reach metrics rise the moment you automate, because automation is good at volume, and they tell you nothing about whether the engagement worked.
Four measures carry the signal. First-contact resolution tells you whether the conversation finished the job. Containment tells you what share the agent handled without a human, and a containment rate climbing while satisfaction falls is a warning rather than a win. Escalation quality tells you whether the human who took over had the context to be useful. Sentiment movement across the conversation tells you how the customer felt at the end compared with the start.
Gnani AI reports that Gnani Agents resolves 80% of issues on the first call and responds in under 800ms in live conversations. Customer expectations set the bar those numbers are judged against, and
our piece on customer service expectations
covers where that bar now sits.
### What goes wrong, and how do you avoid it?
The most common failure is an agent that cannot escalate, and the second is an agent that escalates without context. Both produce the same customer experience, which is repeating the whole story to a human who should already have it.
Fix the handoff before widening the deployment. Gnani AI reports that
Gnani Agents
passes the full conversation history to the human who takes over, which is the minimum bar. The other failure worth naming is scripting an agent to sound human while hiding that it is AI. A voice agent must disclose that it is AI, and the disclosure belongs in the opening line.
Where customer data crosses a regulated boundary, the deployment model becomes a compliance decision. Call recordings, transcripts and call metadata are personal data under the DPDP Act, and the relevant sector rules apply on top: RBI for BFSI, IRDAI for insurance, TRAI for outbound telephony and consent. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
### Where to start with conversational AI for customer engagement
Pick one moment, not one channel. Conversational AI for customer engagement works best when it owns a single predictable moment end to end, such as onboarding day one or a renewal reminder, and is measured against how that moment performed before. Widen once the handoff is clean and the numbers hold. For the broader customer experience picture, see

### Frequently Asked Questions
What is conversational AI for customer engagement?
Conversational AI for customer engagement uses AI agents to hold two-way conversations with customers across voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS, in the customer's own language and at any hour. Unlike marketing automation, the customer can reply and the system has to handle the reply.
Which engagement moments are worth automating first?
The predictable, repetitive and time-sensitive ones. Qualification and scheduling before the sale, onboarding immediately after it, and churn-risk outreach when sentiment turns. Moments where timing changes the outcome give the clearest return.
Which channel should a customer engagement conversation use?
Match the channel to urgency and to the complexity of the reply you want. Voice suits urgent or negotiated conversations, WhatsApp suits exchanges that pause and resume, web chat suits questions asked mid-task, and SMS suits short confirmations and links.
How do you measure conversational AI for customer engagement?
By resolution and retention, not reach. Track first-contact resolution, containment, escalation quality and sentiment movement across the conversation. Containment rising while satisfaction falls is a warning rather than a win.
What is the most common reason engagement automation fails?
An agent that cannot escalate, or escalates without context. Both leave the customer repeating their story to a human who should already have it. Fix the handoff before widening the deployment.
Does a customer engagement voice agent have to disclose it is AI?
Yes. A voice agent must disclose that it is AI, in the opening line of the script. Call recordings, transcripts and call metadata are also personal data under the DPDP Act, with RBI, IRDAI and TRAI rules applying by sector and channel.

Acquiring new customers is certainly alluring. However, to maximize revenue, you must make your existing customers keep coming back. Many businesses forget to focus on the fact that the real business value lies in customer retention, not just customer acquisition. In fact, nearly 44% of organizations give importance to customer acquisition, whereas only 18% of businesses focus on customer retention.One of the biggest benefits of customer retention is earning customer loyalty. A loyal customer refers a brand to their friends and family, which in turn amplifies a brand’s marketing and reduces the business expenses on customer acquisition.Do you have any solid customer retention strategies yet? If you don’t, this article will help you. Here we will discuss important customer retention tactics. So, without further ado, let’s dive into the discussion.
### 4 Pillars Of Customer Retention
A study shows if a company
increases its customer retention rate to 5%
, it can boost its revenue from 25% to 95%. What does it take to increase customer retention rate? Well, when a business adheres to the following four pillars of customer retention in their strategy, they can definitely see a significant boost.
#### 1. Keep Customers’ Need at Priority
Understanding customers’ needs are crucial for any business. Listening to the voice of customers and improving the service/product will improve customer retention. CSAT surveys and product surveys are the best way to know the voice of your customer.There are different methodologies like customer interviews, website behavior analysis,
analyzing recorded call data
to get the voice of your customer. The Hubspot article on
Voice of the Customer Methodologies
will help you make a better plan.
#### 2. Keep Your Products & Services Stand Out from the Crowd
Send email newsletters, use social media platforms to run contests, create engaging content, like podcasts, PDF resources, videos, etc. This way, you will be able to not just grab the eyeballs of prospective consumers but also engage with your existing customers.
#### 3. Offer Discounts & Coupons to Add Value
Businesses throughout the globe
spend around 75 billion USD on rewarding loyal customers
. Such rewards include announcing special perks, giving discounts and reward points, sending gifts at specific intervals and holidays, organizing customer loyalty programs, etc.
#### 4. Improve Customer Assistance
With a help desk or live chat section, you can meet your customers’ queries, turn their complaints into solutions, whether they visit your website, through social platforms, or via email. When you resolve a customer’s complaint or reply to a query, an unhappy customer can be turned into a loyal and repeat customer.In short, customer assistance has an important role in customer retention strategy.Offering excellent customer service is important to retain customers and increase business value. According to Statista,
66% of US customers choose a brand because of its customer service
.As you can see, all four pillars of customer retention need a high level of personalization, omnichannel presence, and, most importantly, seamless customer experience. An upcoming brand can’t afford to deploy a huge amount of human resources for this task. Conversational AI bots will be an excellent alternative that will help brands achieve top-class results at a 60% lesser operational cost.
### How Conversational AI Can Help Companies in Customer Retention
According to a
Microsoft report
, by 2025, around 95% of worldwide customer interactions will be via platforms empowered by AI technology. Here are five ways AI helps companies provide excellent customer service:
#### Timely Response
With conversational AI, you can answer your customers’ queries instantly at almost every stage of the customer journey.For example, a customer comes to enquire about your product; the FAQ bots can effortlessly answer the basic questions. Since the data are fetched quickly by the AI bots, the customer doesn’t have to hold on to the call for a longer period of time.Such efficient and immediate response makes the customers love your brand and keep coming back.
#### Round-the-clock Availability
Conversational AI makes all communication channels of a business 24/7 available to the users. Whether the user calls a business after working hours to book an appointment or a patient calls a helpline in case of emergency, the bots are readily available to help the customers in an empathetic manner.
#### Personalized Omnichannel Replies
No matter whether your customers ask something on Instagram or send a direct message on Facebook messenger, you can answer all the queries with conversational AI bots. To make customer interaction more personalized, you can automate customer service throughout all social channels and other communication channels.
#### Guaranteed Security
Securing a customer’s data privacy across digital channels is an integral part of a business’s customer service. As a layer of security, voice biometrics can be integrated into the communication system so that only authorized persons can access sensitive data. Plus, voice biometrics reduces the user authentication complexity in the old methods like PINs and passwords.Agents can provide a seamless customer experience, and at the same time, customers can accomplish their tasks with minimal effort, which results in a fabulous customer experience.
#### More Work in Less Time and Cost
When you integrate AI in your customer service, bots deal with sales and after-sales support, handle processes, answer FAQs, while customer support agents can handle more complicated cases. This way, both time and operating costs can be saved.
### What’s Your Favorite Customer Retention Tactic
Hope you find our customer retention tactics helpful. As long as your customers’ needs are met, they will be happy to come back to you. To make customers completely satisfied, your customer support should be top-quality. ### What Is Conversational AI in Ecommerce?
Conversational AI in ecommerce is the use of speech and language models to hold a two-way conversation with a shopper across voice, chat, WhatsApp or SMS, and to complete the task the shopper came for. It differs from a scripted chatbot because it interprets intent in natural language and can act on backend systems rather than returning a menu.
The working definition matters because the two technologies get the same label and deliver different results. A rules-based bot matches keywords against a decision tree. A conversational AI agent understands the request, retrieves the order or the product record, and completes the action. The first deflects contacts. The second resolves them.
For retailers selling in India, the practical test is whether the system holds the conversation in the language the shopper actually speaks, including code-mixed speech. Gnani AI reports that its

speech to text model supports more than 10 Indic languages in production alongside Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish code-switching, with 96% code-switching accuracy.
### Why Does Conversational AI Matter for Ecommerce and Retail?
It matters because ecommerce support volume is concentrated in a small number of repetitive, high-frequency questions that a human queue handles slowly and expensively. Order status, delivery timing, returns, refunds and payment failures account for the bulk of contacts, and each one is a task an agent can complete without judgement.
Three pressures make this acute for retail specifically. Volume spikes around sale events by an order of magnitude, so staffing to peak is uneconomic and staffing to average produces abandoned contacts. Shoppers contact across several channels about the same order and expect the thread to carry over. And in India the same catalogue is sold to buyers across a dozen language markets, which multiplies the staffing problem rather than adding to it.

It fits at every stage where a shopper has a question and no one to ask. The highest-value placements are the moments where an unanswered question ends the session: a product specification before adding to cart, a delivery date before checkout, and a refund status after a return.
Mapping the deployment to journey stages rather than to channels prevents the common failure, which is a bot that answers pre-sale questions well and then hands the customer to a queue the moment money is involved. Six use cases carry most of the measurable return, and they divide cleanly into revenue-side and cost-side deployments. Start with one cost-side use case to prove the integration, then extend to the revenue side once the backend connections are live.
#### Product Discovery and Recommendation
A conversational agent narrows a large catalogue through dialogue rather than filters. #### Order Tracking and Delivery Questions
Order status is the single highest-volume contact type in retail, and it is fully automatable because the answer already exists in a system of record. A conversational agent authenticates the customer, retrieves the order, states the delivery date and offers to change the slot. #### Cart Recovery and Checkout Support
An abandoned cart is usually an unanswered question rather than a change of mind, most often about delivery cost, delivery date, return policy or a payment that failed. An outbound voice or WhatsApp agent that asks the reason and answers it recovers a share of those carts, and the conversation also tells the retailer which of the four reasons dominates.
#### Returns, Refunds and Exchanges
Returns generate the most frustrated contacts in retail because the customer has already paid and is waiting. A conversational agent that states refund status accurately, every time, in the customer's language, removes the repeat contacts that follow a vague answer. Start by treating every conversation as personal data, because it is. Order histories, delivery addresses, phone numbers and payment references are personal information under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, and call recordings and transcripts carry the same classification.
A deployment checklist that holds up to review covers five points:

### TL;DR
Conversational AI in healthcare is the use of speech and language models to run patient conversations end to end across voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS, so clinical staff spend their time on care instead of on scheduling, screening and follow-up calls. The five use cases that move the most workload are appointment management, triage and escalation, pre-visit screening, remote consultation support, and post-discharge follow-up. Each one needs an explicit handover path to a clinician, an AI disclosure in the opening line, and a data posture that satisfies HIPAA in the United States and the DPDP Act for Indian patient data.
### What conversational AI in healthcare actually does
Hospital and payer contact centres carry a workload that looks nothing like retail support. Call volumes spike without warning, callers are often distressed, and a meaningful share of every shift goes on tasks that need no clinical judgement at all. Appointment changes, insurance pre-checks, prescription refill requests and post-discharge check-ins absorb hours that trained staff could spend with patients.
Conversational AI in healthcare targets exactly that layer. A voice agent answers the call, verifies the caller, resolves the routine request against the hospital information system, and hands anything clinical to a human with the full conversation history attached.
Gnani Agents
runs this pattern across voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS from one platform, with context-aware handoff built in rather than bolted on.
The engineering difference in healthcare sits in the audio, not the script. Patients call from corridors, car parks and noisy wards, often in a regional language, often code-switching mid-sentence. A model trained on clean studio English will mishear a medication name or a date of birth.
Gnani Prisma v2.5
is trained on more than 14 million hours of real telephonic audio and reports under 4% word error rate on Indian speech, with 96% code-switching accuracy across Hindi-English, Tamil-English and Bengali-English mixing. Gnani AI reports those figures for telephony-grade 8kHz audio.
### Five conversational AI use cases transforming healthcare
These five carry the clearest operational case. They are illustrative patterns drawn from published Gnani AI product capability, described so that a contact centre lead can map them onto an existing workflow.
#### 1. Appointment scheduling, rescheduling and no-show recovery
Scheduling is the highest-volume, lowest-complexity conversation in any healthcare contact centre, and it is the one most often abandoned when hold times climb. A voice agent takes the call at any hour, reads availability from the scheduling system, confirms the slot, and sends the confirmation on WhatsApp. The same agent runs the outbound side: reminder calls ahead of the appointment, and a rebooking offer the moment a cancellation lands.
The value compounds on the outbound leg. A cancelled slot that gets refilled the same day protects both clinician utilisation and the revenue attached to it, and neither outcome requires a human to place the call.
#### 2. Triage routing and emergency escalation
Inbound clinical calls need to reach the right department fast, and the routing decision is where generic IVR menus fail hardest. A conversational agent listens to the caller describe the problem in their own words, classifies urgency, and routes to the correct team. Anything that reads as an emergency goes straight to a human, immediately, with no further questions asked by the agent.
Two design rules matter here. The agent never gives clinical advice, and the escalation threshold is set deliberately low. An agent that over-escalates costs a little staff time. An agent that under-escalates is a patient safety problem.
#### 3. Pre-visit screening and symptom intake
Structured intake ahead of a visit shortens the consultation and gives the clinician a head start. The agent collects the reason for the visit, current medications, allergies and recent history, then writes the structured record into the patient file before the patient arrives. Infectious-risk screening ahead of an in-person visit runs the same way.
Intake is collection, not assessment. The agent records what the patient reports and presents it to the clinician. It does not interpret symptoms, and the copy a patient hears should make that boundary plain.
#### 4. Remote consultation support
Telephone and video consultations widen access for elderly patients, for patients with mobility limitations and for anyone a long way from the hospital. Conversational AI handles the work around the consultation rather than the consultation itself: confirming the slot, verifying identity, collecting consent, joining the patient to the call, and producing the summary afterwards.
The post-call summary is where
Gnani Assist
earns its place. It sits alongside the clinician during the call, retrieves policy and knowledge-base answers on request, and writes the summary and record update automatically. Gnani AI reports a 90%+ reduction in after-call administrative work for Assist deployments.
#### 5. Post-discharge follow-up and adherence monitoring
Recovery happens after the patient leaves, and that is precisely when contact drops off. Scheduled follow-up calls ask a short, fixed set of questions about recovery, medication adherence and warning signs, then escalate any concerning answer to a nurse the same day. Surgical site infection checks and medication reminders both fit this shape.
Tone carries real weight on these calls. A patient three days out of surgery is not a support ticket, and the voice has to reflect that. The
Gnani AI text to speech API
applies context-aware prosody, so the same agent sounds empathetic in a recovery call and businesslike in a billing one.

Conversational AI in healthcare: scope, handover point and regulatory flag by use case
### Where a human clinician has to take over
Every one of the five use cases above has a boundary, and the deployment stands or falls on how cleanly that boundary is drawn. Diagnosis, treatment decisions, medication changes, test result delivery and anything involving a distressed or confused patient belong to a human. The agent's job at that point is to transfer fast and transfer with context.
Context is the part teams underestimate. A transfer that drops the patient into a fresh queue to repeat their story undoes the benefit entirely. Gnani Agents carries the full conversation history into the handoff, so the clinician picks up mid-conversation rather than starting over.
Gnani Analytics
then scores those handoffs across the whole call corpus rather than a sampled few, which is how a team finds the escalation rules that are mistuned.
### Compliance requirements for conversational AI in healthcare
Healthcare conversations generate some of the most sensitive data any enterprise system touches. Call recordings, transcripts and call metadata are personal information. Voiceprints and speaker embeddings used for caller authentication are biometric data, and they attract the highest level of protection.
The regimes that apply depend on where the patient is and who holds the record. HIPAA governs protected health information in the United States. The DPDP Act governs personal data for Indian patients. GDPR applies to patients in the European Union. Gnani AI is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and ISO 27001 certified, and HIPAA, GDPR and PCI-DSS compliant.
Three practices carry most of the risk reduction. Disclose that the agent is AI in the opening line of every script, with no exceptions and no softening. Keep data inside the boundary the regulator expects, which for many healthcare providers means on-premise or private cloud rather than a shared tenancy. Log and audit every conversation so a reviewer can reconstruct what the agent said and why.
Deployment location is a design decision, not a procurement detail.
Gnani Artha
runs the speech, reasoning and orchestration stack on infrastructure the customer controls, including on-premise and air-gapped configurations, so patient data never leaves the hospital network. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
### How to evaluate a platform before you commit
Four questions separate a healthcare-ready platform from a demo that looks good in English on a clean line.
What audio was the model trained on?
Telephony audio at 8kHz behaves nothing like studio audio at 16kHz. Ask for word error rate on the former, in the languages your patients actually speak.
How does code-switching perform?
Indian patients mix languages inside a single sentence as a matter of course. A model that handles Hindi and English separately but not together will fail on real calls.
Where can it be deployed?
Cloud, private cloud, on-premise and air-gapped are four different compliance postures. Confirm which ones the vendor supports in production rather than on a roadmap.
What happens at handoff?
Ask to see a live transfer, including what the human agent receives on screen at the moment the call arrives.
None of the scenarios described in this article represents a specific existing deployment, customer or healthcare provider, and none implies partnership with or endorsement by any healthcare body or government department.
### Getting started with conversational AI in healthcare
Start with the highest-volume conversation that carries no clinical judgement, which in almost every healthcare contact centre is appointment management. Instrument it properly, measure containment and escalation quality rather than call deflection alone, and widen the scope once the handoff behaviour holds up under real volume.

Conversational AI in healthcare is the use of speech and language models to run patient conversations end to end across voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS. It handles the high-volume work that needs no clinical judgement, such as appointment management, screening and follow-up, and hands anything clinical to a human with the conversation history attached.
What are the main use cases for conversational AI in healthcare?
The five with the clearest operational case are appointment scheduling and no-show recovery, triage routing and emergency escalation, pre-visit screening and symptom intake, remote consultation support, and post-discharge follow-up. Each one automates coordination work rather than clinical decisions.
Is conversational AI in healthcare HIPAA compliant?
Compliance depends on the platform and the deployment, not on the technology category. Gnani AI is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and ISO 27001 certified, and HIPAA, GDPR and PCI-DSS compliant. Call recordings, transcripts and metadata are personal information, and voiceprints are biometric data. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.

Yes. Gnani Prisma v2.5 runs 10 or more Indian languages in production speech recognition, trained on more than 14 million hours of real telephonic audio, and handles Hindi-English, Tamil-English and Bengali-English code-switching inside a single sentence. Does a patient have to be told they are speaking to AI?
Yes. Voice agents disclose that they are AI, and the disclosure belongs in the opening line of every script with no softening. Treat it as a fixed requirement of the script rather than a configurable option.

### What is conversational AI in insurance?
Conversational AI in insurance is software that handles policyholder conversations in natural language across voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS, and completes the transaction being discussed rather than only answering questions. It spans quoting, onboarding, premium reminders, renewals, first notice of loss and claim status, in the language the policyholder speaks.
The test that separates it from a chatbot is whether the conversation ends in a changed record. Explaining what a deductible is helps. Capturing a claim, verifying the policyholder and setting a callback commitment is the work.
### Why is insurance a strong fit for conversational AI?
Insurance is a strong fit because its customer contact is concentrated into a few predictable, rule-governed moments spread across a long and otherwise silent policy lifecycle. A motor policy may generate four conversations in a year, three of which are reminders.
That shape creates two problems a staffed desk handles badly. Renewal and reminder volume arrives in dated batches rather than evenly, so capacity is either idle or overwhelmed. Claims volume arrives unpredictably, often weather-linked, and a surge lands precisely when service quality matters most to retention.
Language compounds both. An Indian insurer selling through regional distribution is serving policyholders who will not transact in English, and regional-language desks are the first thing to be thinly staffed.
### Where does conversational AI fit across the policy lifecycle?
It fits wherever the next step is determined by rules and data the insurer already holds, and stops where underwriting judgment or discretionary settlement begins. The table below maps each lifecycle stage against that line.

#### Quoting and lead qualification
A conversational quote collects the rating inputs in dialogue rather than through a form, which matters most on voice, where there is no form. The agent asks for vehicle, health or property details, applies the rating rules, and returns an indicative premium. Gnani AI lists lead qualification among the published use cases for

.
#### Onboarding and verification
Policy issuance stalls on missing documents and unverified details more than on underwriting time. Automating the chase, and verifying by voice rather than by callback queue, removes the longest gap in the issuance timeline. Gnani AI publishes onboarding and KYC as a core deployment pattern.
#### Premium reminders and renewals
Renewals are the highest-value automated conversation in insurance because lapse is largely a contact problem. A reminder that reaches the policyholder in their language, with a payment path in the same conversation, converts materially better than one that routes them to a portal.
#### First notice of loss and claim status
First notice of loss is a structured interview conducted under stress, which is exactly the case for a patient, consistent, always-available interviewer. Claim status is the highest-volume inbound query after a loss event, and it is a read from a system the policyholder cannot see.
### How does multilingual voice work for Indian insurers?
It works when the speech models are trained on telephony audio rather than studio audio, because insurance conversations happen on noisy 8kHz lines, in regional languages, with code-mixing throughout. Studio-grade English models degrade sharply on that input.
Gnani AI reports that

It also reports named entity recognition tuned for financial and insurance terms, which is what keeps policy numbers and sums assured intact in a transcript.
On output, Gnani AI reports a mean opinion score of 4.23 on 8kHz telephony for
Timbre v2.5
, its text to speech model, currently labelled Beta, with lakh and crore cadence handled natively. A premium amount read incorrectly is a complaint, not a rounding error.
Benchmark figures measured under different audio conditions do not compare directly across vendors.
### What does IRDAI and DPDP compliance require before deployment?
An insurer deploying conversational AI has to be able to show what the policyholder was told, in what language, with what consent, and how an automated decision was reached. That evidence requirement runs across every regime involved.
IRDAI
governs insurance conduct, including how products are described and what a policyholder is told at the point of sale and at claim.
DPDP Act
covers all personal data of Indian policyholders, including call recordings, transcripts and call metadata. Health information captured during a claim raises the sensitivity further.
TRAI
governs outbound telephony, including consent and DND obligations, which apply directly to renewal and premium reminder campaigns.
Three design rules follow. The agent discloses that it is AI at the start of every conversation. Automated decisions that affect a policyholder need an explanation path and a route to a human. ### What should an insurer measure after deployment?
Measure containment and renewal conversion first, because they are the two numbers that justify the programme. Containment is the share of contacts resolved without a human; renewal conversion is whether the automated reminder actually changed lapse behaviour against a control group.
Add three more. Claim intake completeness shows whether automated first notice of loss produces files that do not need rework. Time to first contact after a loss event shows whether surge capacity held. Scored quality on automated conversations shows whether the experience was acceptable, which matters more in claims than anywhere else in insurance.

At final underwriting acceptance, liability and coverage determination, settlement amount negotiation, discretionary premium concessions, and grievance or ombudsman matters. These need human judgment or regulated handling under IRDAI conduct rules, so the correct pattern is escalation with full conversation context.

It can return an indicative premium by collecting the rating inputs in dialogue and applying the insurer's rating rules, which matters most on voice where there is no form to fill. Final underwriting acceptance stays with the insurer's underwriting process.

It depends on whether the speech models were trained on telephony audio rather than studio audio. An insurer has to be able to show what the policyholder was told, in what language, with what consent, and how an automated decision was reached. IRDAI governs conduct, the DPDP Act covers all personal data including recordings and transcripts, and TRAI governs outbound reminder calls. ### TL;DR
Conversational AI lead generation means an AI agent holds a real conversation with an inbound or outbound prospect, qualifies them against criteria you set, and writes the result into the CRM during the conversation rather than after it. It works on high-volume, predictable steps: first-touch qualification, callback scheduling, form-abandonment follow-up, renewal and repeat-purchase prompts. It does not work on price negotiation, exception handling or any conversation where the prospect is already unhappy. The decision that separates a working deployment from a stalled one is not model choice. It is deciding in advance which conversations the agent finishes and which it hands to a human, with the full context attached.
### What Conversational AI Lead Generation Actually Does
There is a useful line between a system that answers and a system that acts. An answering system tells a prospect that a site visit is possible on Thursday. An acting system reads the calendar, holds the Thursday slot, writes a qualified lead record against the prospect's number, and sends the confirmation before the call ends.
The second kind removes a manual handoff, and it introduces work that the first kind never has to do. Double-booked slots, a CRM write that fails halfway, a misheard phone number, a prospect who changes their mind after the record is created. Any evaluation of conversational AI lead generation that does not ask how the system behaves when a write fails is measuring the easy half of the problem.
Gnani Agents
runs this acting pattern across voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS from one platform, with lead qualification as a published use case alongside collections, appointment booking and onboarding.
#### Where the qualification actually happens
A qualification bot is only as good as the criteria behind it. Vague criteria produce a long list of leads that sales ignores within a fortnight. Useful criteria are the ones a salesperson would ask in the first ninety seconds: what is the use case, what is the timeline, who signs, is there a budget line already. Those four answers, captured consistently and written into the CRM the same way every time, are worth more than a higher raw lead count.

### Which Lead Generation Steps Automate Well
Automation fit varies sharply across the funnel. Treating the whole funnel as one problem is the most common design error, and it is the reason many pilots produce a working demo and a disappointing quarter.
Automation fit across the lead generation funnel.
Funnel step
