What problems does conversational AI solve?
Companies use AI chatbots to automate customer support but also to help optimize conversion rates, improve customer experiences, and contribute to direct revenue.
How can conversational AI help in building better customer engagement?
Conversational AI can automatically collect insights like critical data points, purchasing patterns, and customer habits, enabling companies to be better equipped for upselling conversations.
What is a conversational AI platform?
Conversational AI platforms are technologies that enable computers to understand and respond naturally to human language.
How do conversational AI chatbots help businesses?
Chatbots can help businesses take customer engagement to the next level. By using conversational AI chatbots, engagement can be driven based on the user data and made more interactive.
What is conversational marketing strategy?
Conversational Marketing is a method of engaging with website visitors and converting leads via dialogue-driven activities. This style of inbound marketing puts a focus on interactions with the consumer, not simply one-way transmission by the brand.

### How Can Retrieval Augmented Generation Unlock Domain Intelligence?
RAG voice agents are reshaping enterprise automation by grounding AI decisions in real-time, domain-specific knowledge.
### INTRODUCTION
What makes an AI system genuinely intelligent inside an enterprise? The answer increasingly points toward
RAG voice agents
, a new class of voice-driven AI agents powered by
retrieval augmented generation
. These systems don’t rely only on model memory. They fetch real-time domain knowledge, validate facts, and generate context-aware responses grounded in enterprise data.
Enterprises face a major challenge: large language models are powerful, but they hallucinate when asked domain-specific queries. From banking compliance to HR policies to customer service resolution flows, organizations need
knowledge retrieval
and
context-aware agents
that can combine high-quality reasoning with factual accuracy. Retrieval augmented generation solves this gap by integrating vector search, structured databases, and dynamic document retrieval directly into the conversational loop.
This article explores how RAG voice agents unlock deep domain intelligence, why they matter for BFSI, e-commerce, HR, and customer service, and how organizations can deploy them with precision. You’ll also learn best practices, pitfalls, ROI benchmarks, technical architecture, and more.
### What Is Retrieval Augmented Generation?
Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) is an AI technique that merges real-time
with the generative capabilities of a large language model. Instead of relying solely on internal model parameters, RAG voice agents look up relevant context from enterprise-approved knowledge sources before generating a response.
#### How RAG Works at a High Level
A simple RAG pipeline looks like this:
Speech-to-text conversion
captures the user's voice input.
Vector encoding
converts the query into embeddings.
Knowledge retrieval
finds similar vectors inside enterprise knowledge bases.
Context ranking and filtering
chooses the top documents.
LLM reasoning
generates the output based on retrieved facts.
Voice synthesis
converts the generated answer back to speech.
This achieves two critical outcomes:
Higher factual accuracy
(reduced hallucinations)
Domain intelligence
grounded in enterprise-approved sources
#### Why RAG Matters for Voice Agents
Voice conversations often carry ambiguity: accents, noise, incomplete phrases, or short utterances. RAG helps voice agents:
Infer missing details using retrieved context
Validate industry-specific terminology
Ensure consistency with policies
Minimize flaws in long-running calls
This is why RAG voice agents are emerging as a superior approach for enterprise-grade automation.

### How RAG Voice Agents Actually Work
RAG voice agents use a multi-layer architecture designed for accuracy, speed, and domain grounding. To understand how they unlock domain intelligence, it helps to break the pipeline into simple, functional components.

This matters because if the transcript is wrong, every downstream retrieval step becomes less accurate.

Implementing RAG voice agents requires more than plugging in a vector store and an LLM. Enterprises must optimize retrieval pipelines, improve data governance, and tune conversational flows.

Even strong technical teams encounter issues when deploying RAG agents. These pitfalls can degrade quality, increase cost, or cause compliance failures.

### How do SLMs stay efficient at the edge without losing accuracy?
Small language models voice AI needs to run inside tight hardware and regulatory constraints while still sounding smart, fast, and trustworthy. The central question is simple: how do SLMs stay efficient on edge devices without giving up the accuracy enterprises expect from LLMs?
The short answer is that SLMs use a different playbook. They are smaller, specialized language models that combine model compression, domain focus, and inference optimizations on edge AI hardware. By pruning parameters, quantizing weights, and fine tuning on narrow domains, they deliver low latency and strong accuracy for specific voice AI tasks, especially in regulated industries like banking and finance.
Your customers do not care how many parameters your model has. They care if the voice bot understands them in under 300 milliseconds and gives the right answer every time.

### Introduction
Imagine a credit card customer calling your bank from a noisy street. The voice bot has less than half a second to recognize the speech, understand intent, and respond. Studies show that customers start feeling latency above 250 to 500 milliseconds, and anything beyond 800 milliseconds feels slow and robotic.
gnani.ai
Cloud only large language models are not designed for this environment. They depend on network hops, heavy inference, and shared infrastructure. For real time voice AI in banking, e commerce, or HR support, you need small language models voice AI running as edge AI services inside IVR systems, call center gateways, or even mobile apps.
In this article, we will unpack how SLMs work, how they compare in LLM vs SLM trade offs, why they are efficient language models for latency sensitive voice AI, and what best practices keep accuracy high even on constrained devices. We will also look at how platforms like Gnani.ai combine SLMs with proprietary speech tech and agentic AI to deliver measurable ROI in regulated industries.
### What are SLMs in voice AI and why enterprises care
Small language models (SLMs) are compact language models designed to operate efficiently on resource constrained hardware such as smartphones, embedded servers in contact centers, or edge gateways inside bank data centers. While large language models can have tens or hundreds of billions of parameters, SLMs typically range from about one million to ten billion parameters, depending on the task and architecture.
Unlike generic language models that try to answer everything, SLMs are tuned for specific workflows. In voice AI they usually focus on:
Understanding intents and entities in a narrow domain such as retail banking, collections, or HR policies.
Structuring queries and responses for downstream systems.
Keeping context across turns within a call or chat.
From an enterprise point of view this matters for three reasons:
Latency and responsiveness
Edge AI deployments with SLMs cut the round trip to the cloud. Combined with speech recognition and text to speech on the same node, they deliver sub second experiences that feel human. On device ASR systems have already demonstrated worst case latencies around 125 milliseconds in research settings, which shows what is possible with optimized stacks.
MDPI
Cost efficiency and sustainability
LLMs are heavy not only at training time but also during inference. Reports show that large models can require orders of magnitude more energy than small models, with some LLM training runs consuming tens of gigawatt hours.
DataCamp
SLMs consume a fraction of this, which makes them better suited for high volume voice AI in banks and call centers.
Compliance and data residency
For banking and HR processes, sensitive voice data often cannot leave the country or the bank perimeter. Edge AI with SLMs lets you process language within your own infrastructure, which aligns with regulations around data localization and privacy in markets like India and the EU.
For platforms like
Gnani.ai’s Agentic AI voice bots
, SLMs complement proprietary ASR, TTS, and orchestration layers. The result is small language models voice AI that still delivers natural, multilingual conversations across BFSI, e commerce, and service operations.
### Why SLMs at the edge matter for business outcomes
For CTOs and enterprise decision makers, the question is not only LLM vs SLM from a model architecture viewpoint. The real question is: what does this mean for NPS, cost per call, and risk?
Recent industry research on edge AI shows that running inference closer to the user brings three repeatable benefits.
Lower call lag and higher customer satisfaction
Edge voice AI avoids network jitter and cloud congestion.
In banking deployments, voice bots with sub second latency can reduce perceived call lag by dozens of seconds in peak times, lifting CSAT scores.
Higher containment without scripts
Efficient language models tuned to your domain can handle more intents without needing to escalate to agents. In practice, this means higher automation rates for:
Card block and limit change.
EMI status in lending.
Order tracking in e commerce.
Leave and payroll queries in HR.
Predictable cost for high volume interactions
When every call is routed to a cloud LLM, cost scales linearly with volume. With SLMs and edge AI, inference is mostly bounded by your own infrastructure. This is critical for:
High call volumes in collections and customer service.
Markets where voice minutes are cheaper than cloud compute.
Always on services like fraud hotlines and card disputes.
Better risk posture for regulated workloads
Banking and insurance processes often require strong controls for PCI DSS, SOC2, and local data residency laws. Running small language models voice AI at the edge keeps raw audio and transcripts within your boundary, while still letting you sync anonymised signals or summaries to the cloud for analytics.
### How SLMs stay efficient without losing accuracy
The core concern with small language models is simple: if you shrink the model to make it efficient, will accuracy drop too much?
Modern SLM design tackles this in several layers that combine architectural choices, compression, and domain optimization. Surveys on edge efficient LLMs and SLMs highlight four main techniques.
#### 1. Start with a compact architecture
Efficient language models begin with fewer layers, narrower hidden dimensions, and optimized attention mechanisms. Examples include MiniLM style architectures that focus on strong embeddings and semantic understanding with far fewer parameters than full scale transformers.
#### 2. Compress without destroying knowledge
The next step is to apply compression to shrink the footprint for edge AI:
Quantization
: Converting 32 bit floating point weights to 8 bit or even 4 bit representation.
Pruning
: Removing unimportant weights or whole neurons that add little to output quality.
Knowledge distillation
: Training the SLM to mimic a powerful LLM, preserving behaviour in a smaller network.
NVIDIA notes that model size is a primary driver of ASR deployment latency. Smaller models need less compute per inference, which directly improves response time in voice AI.
NVIDIA Developer
#### 3. Specialize by domain instead of doing everything
Accuracy is protected by making the SLM narrow and deep rather than broad and shallow:
Train and fine tune on domain corpora such as banking FAQs, transaction logs, policy documents, and real call transcripts.
Focus on recurring intents and utterance patterns from your industry.
Use retrieval augmented generation where needed so that the SLM consults external knowledge instead of memorizing everything.
ScienceDirect
This is where LLM vs SLM becomes an architecture plus data problem. LLMs keep high generic accuracy across many domains. SLMs keep high local accuracy by specializing.
#### 4. Optimize the full edge pipeline
You cannot look at the SLM in isolation. For small language models voice AI to feel natural, the full path has to be tuned:
On device or on premise ASR converts speech to text with optimized acoustic and language models.
The SLM interprets intents and context using domain tuned language models.
Business logic runs as an agentic workflow that calls core systems.
TTS returns a natural response.
Research on device ASR shows that optimised pipelines can reach worst case latencies around 0.46 seconds while maintaining state of the art word error rates.

### Common mistakes when moving from LLM to SLM
Enterprises often fail in their first SLM project because they treat it like a smaller LLM instead of a different tool. Here are some common pitfalls.
#### 1. Assuming a one click shrink
Simply quantizing a generic LLM and dropping it on an edge device is not enough. Without domain tuning and evaluation, you will see accuracy drop on complex banking and HR intents. Surveys on edge efficient language models warn that compression without task specific tuning can severely impact performance.
ScienceDirect+1
#### 2. Ignoring the full latency budget
Teams sometimes optimize the SLM and forget that ASR, TTS, network, and backend calls can dominate latency. Voice AI literature shows that even well optimized ASR pipelines need careful coordination between smartphone, FPGA, and server to maintain low real time factors.

#### 3. Overloading SLMs with generic tasks
If you ask your SLM to act as a general purpose chatbot, accuracy will suffer. Keep it focused on your top workflows. Use RAG or cloud LLM support for long tail questions.

You need a strong evaluation harness that checks:

Edge AI nodes run inside your perimeter, but they still need:

As per current trends and reports, 41% of adult users use voice search at least one time a day. This means that the use of voice AI is steadily on the rise.A significant contributor to the upward trend in voice searches among customers is the advent of smart home devices. By ensuring that the responsive voice coming from the smart home devices remains human-like and provides an empathetic experience, users are more inclined to interact with services such as chatbots.In a detailed report published by the American Psychological Association (APA), data shows that even though technology has increased the number of communication channels between users, voice is still preferred. This is because voice AI lends a more intimate experience to interactions and helps create stronger bonds.
### How do voice bots and chatbots work?
Conversational artificial intelligence (AI) is a software solution used by business houses and other chatbot users to engage with customers through email-based bots, chatbots or voice bots. Voice bots interact with customers by analyzing their vocal data and formulating the most accurate response by encoding and decoding spoken content. With the help of machine learning, the system can train itself to continuously improve its accuracy and provide better service.On the surface, the use of chatbots might seem very linear. However, various components go into this technology to ensure accuracy and speed.
### Various Components of Voice Bots
#### Automatic speech recognition (ASR): The backbone of voice bots
Automatic speech recognition or ASR forms the backbone of voice bots, as it’s directly responsible for converting spoken verbatim data into text. When a customer speaks to an AI bot, a chatbot or a voice assistant, the ASR component uses an audio feed to transcribe the voice message into a wav file. The wav file is then filtered by removing background noises and other disturbances, to provide a smoother experience to the customers, after which it is then broken down into phonemes.
Phonemes
basically define how words sound, and by linking that data together, the ASR can deduce what the customer has said.
#### Natural language understanding (NLU) for voice and text-to-speech bots
Natural language understanding (NLU) is a sub-branch of the larger topic of natural language processing (NLP). NLP deals with the entire spectrum of functionality for voice bots, where it interprets input data, deciphers the meaning and formulates responses for the users. NLU plays a vital role in this process, by helping the algorithm identify intent and tone within a short time. In other words, NLU helps the AI-powered virtual chatbot assistant distinguish conversational elements and take the business interaction forward. [caption id="attachment_24617" align="aligncenter" width="538"]
Source: Rolof Computer Academy[/caption]
#### Voice bot conversation module for correct responses
A well-defined conversation module allows users to effortlessly interact with the voice bot service without having to follow a directive course (like in the case of IVR systems). The entire style and experience of interaction revolves around the user’s service requirement and intent, and subsequently retrieving relevant information to help the user.
#### Text-to-speech AI voice bots system
Text-to-speech or TTS is the business component that ‘reads aloud’ the text data that is visible on a computer screen or digital interface. In other words, the system uses various deep learning techniques over time to read a response and mimic a human voice when reading it aloud to the customer. When the NLP-NLU component analyses the input data from a user, it formulates a relevant service response that is fed into the TTS component. The output from the TTS is what the customer hears and experiences.
### How do voice bots comprehend complex languages and accents?
Global adoption of voice-based technologies has established ‘voice’ as a preferred business service medium amongst customers, and the numbers and data speak for themselves. However, a common roadblock that most conversational AI solution providers endure is the process of training their interactive voice bot for the optimum user engagement and experience.Today, there are over 7,000 different languages and dialects. Yet, this isn’t the real problem. If we were to take one single language, we’d soon learn that this one language is spoken differently across the world.The English language is the biggest example of this problem. English is spoken across all 195 countries in the world and has over time grown to be the official or business language for 67 of them. That means there are over 100 different accents for the English language alone! For each accent, there are a definitive set of phonemes that makes it difficult for the AI-powered voice bots, chatbots and text-to-speech bots to comprehend.[caption id="attachment_24616" align="aligncenter" width="387"]
Source: Google Images[/caption]
#### With the help of voice AI for speech recognition optimization
Speech recognition optimization is a branch of computer science that deals with the business of computational linguistics. It helps the AI understand specific languages and accents by benchmarking them against an existing database of knowledge. With the help of a voice biometrics solution, the AI can, in very little time, identify the customer’s accent to begin processing conversational input.
#### By implementing pre-trained multilingual AI voice bot speech encoders
With the help of modern machine learning models, text-to-speech bots can be trained with billions of customer conversations to help create a strong foundation for the NLP component. For example, Gnani.ai is continuously strengthening its foundation by training its model in 20+ international languages to broaden its service of customer experience. As opposed to building new models for multiple languages, we can now deploy any language on-demand in a few days or within very less time.
#### By utilizing a multilingual AI voice bot value extractor
Value extraction and its degree of data service accuracy could make or break your customer experience (CX) goals. When a customer interacts with an AI voice bot, certain crucial values regarding name, address, reference numbers etc., are extracted irrespective of the language used. If a user is talking to an AI voice assistant in French, crucial values might be in English (age, phone number). Hence, the value extractor must be trained to analyze languages and decipher critical business data.
### What lies ahead with AI, voice and text-to-speech bots?
The global market size of AI-powered virtual assistants will be worth a business of over USD 1.3 billion by the end of 2024, and trends point towards voice-based assistants owning over 50% of this service share. Hence, it’s clear that the power of ‘voice’ will take over business processes and customer engagement initiatives and voice bot experiences.If you’re interested in learning more about how you can leverage AI and voice bot service for your business, talk to us any time.

What is AI voice bot?
Voice bots are software powered by artificial intelligence (AI) that enable a caller to navigate an interactive voice response (IVR) system with their voice using natural language generally. Callers don't have to listen to the menus and press corresponding numbers on their keypads.

The generative AI revolution is reshaping how B2B SaaS companies operate, from automating customer support to generating personalized content at scale. However, with great power comes great responsibility—especially when it comes to
data privacy in generative AI solutions
. As organizations increasingly rely on AI-powered tools that process vast amounts of sensitive information, establishing robust privacy frameworks isn't just good practice; it's business-critical.Recent studies show that 73% of enterprise leaders are concerned about data exposure risks when implementing AI solutions. This concern is well-founded, as generative AI systems require extensive datasets that often contain personally identifiable information (PII), proprietary business data, and confidential customer insights. Without proper safeguards, these systems can inadvertently become privacy vulnerabilities rather than competitive advantages.
### The High Stakes of Data Privacy in Generative AI Solutions
When B2B SaaS companies deploy generative AI without adequate privacy measures, they face significant risks that extend far beyond potential fines. Data breaches can destroy customer trust, damage brand reputation, and result in costly legal battles. Moreover, with regulations like GDPR imposing penalties of up to 4% of annual global revenue, the financial implications of privacy violations can be devastating.The challenge becomes even more complex when considering how generative AI models learn and operate. Unlike traditional software that processes data according to predefined rules, AI systems can memorize training data patterns and potentially reproduce sensitive information in their outputs. This phenomenon, known as data memorization, poses unique
privacy risks in AI systems
that require specialized mitigation strategies.
### Essential Strategies for Protecting Data in AI Systems
#### 1. Implement Advanced Data Anonymization Techniques
Effective
data anonymization in AI
goes beyond simply removing names and email addresses. Modern anonymization requires sophisticated techniques that preserve data utility while eliminating identifying characteristics. K-anonymity, l-diversity, and t-closeness are statistical methods that ensure individual records cannot be distinguished within datasets.For B2B SaaS applications, consider implementing dynamic anonymization that adjusts protection levels based on data sensitivity. Customer transaction data might require stronger anonymization than general usage metrics, allowing you to maintain analytical value while protecting
sensitive data in machine learning
processes.
#### 2. Leverage Differential Privacy for Mathematical Guarantees
Differential privacy represents the gold standard for quantifiable privacy protection. By adding carefully calibrated statistical noise to datasets, this technique provides mathematical guarantees that individual privacy is preserved, even when attackers have auxiliary information.Leading tech companies have successfully implemented differential privacy in production systems. Apple uses it to collect user insights while protecting individual privacy, and Google applies it to location data analysis. For B2B SaaS companies, differential privacy can enable valuable analytics while ensuring
AI privacy compliance
with the strictest regulatory requirements.
#### 3. Deploy Federated Learning Architectures
Federated learning allows AI models to learn from distributed data without centralizing sensitive information. Instead of moving data to a central server, the model travels to where data resides, processes it locally, and only shares aggregated insights. This approach is particularly valuable for B2B SaaS platforms serving clients in highly regulated industries like healthcare or finance.Consider a customer support AI that learns from multiple client interactions. Through federated learning, the model can improve its responses based on patterns across all clients without any single organization's data leaving their secure environment.
#### 4. Utilize Synthetic Data Generation
One of the most promising applications of generative AI for privacy protection is synthetic data creation. By training models to generate artificial datasets that mirror real data's statistical properties without containing actual sensitive information, organizations can enable safe testing, development, and collaboration.
Synthetic data privacy
offers multiple advantages: it eliminates re-identification risks, enables unlimited data sharing for development purposes, and allows for stress-testing AI systems without exposing real customer information. However, ensuring synthetic data doesn't inadvertently leak information from the original dataset requires careful validation and testing.
#### 5. Establish Comprehensive Consent Management
Modern privacy regulations require explicit, informed consent for data processing, particularly for AI applications. This means going beyond simple checkbox agreements to provide clear explanations of how
Agentic AI
systems will use customer data, what insights they'll generate, and how long data will be retained.Implement granular consent mechanisms that allow customers to approve specific AI use cases while potentially declining others. For instance, a customer might consent to AI-powered personalization but not to data sharing for model training purposes.
### Building Privacy-First AI Governance
Successful
requires more than technical controls; it demands organizational commitment to privacy-first principles. Establish cross-functional teams that include data scientists, privacy experts, legal counsel, and business stakeholders to ensure privacy considerations are embedded throughout the AI development lifecycle.Regular privacy impact assessments should evaluate new AI initiatives before deployment, identifying potential risks and mitigation strategies. These assessments should consider not just immediate privacy implications but also long-term risks as AI models evolve and learn from new data.Documentation plays a crucial role in demonstrating compliance and building stakeholder trust. Maintain detailed records of data sources, processing purposes, retention periods, and privacy controls. This documentation proves invaluable during audits and helps teams make informed decisions about AI system modifications.
### Navigating Regulatory Complexities
The regulatory landscape for AI privacy continues to evolve rapidly. The EU's AI Act introduces specific requirements for high-risk AI systems, while various jurisdictions are developing their own AI governance frameworks. Staying compliant requires continuous monitoring of regulatory developments and proactive adaptation of privacy practices.
GDPR compliance for AI
requires particular attention to principles like data minimization, purpose limitation, and the right to explanation. When individuals request explanations for automated decisions, your AI systems must be capable of providing meaningful insights into their decision-making processes.
### Technical Implementation Best Practices
From a technical perspective, privacy protection should be architected into AI systems from the ground up. Implement encryption for data at rest and in transit, ensure secure model serving environments, and establish robust access controls that limit data exposure to authorized personnel only.Regular security audits and penetration testing help identify vulnerabilities before they can be exploited. Pay particular attention to model inference endpoints, which can potentially be probed to extract training data information through carefully crafted queries.Monitor AI system outputs for signs of data leakage, implementing automated scanning tools that flag potentially sensitive information before it reaches end users. This proactive approach helps prevent privacy incidents and demonstrates your commitment to responsible AI deployment.
### The Competitive Advantage of Privacy Excellence
Organizations that excel at
don't just avoid risks—they create competitive advantages. Privacy-conscious customers increasingly prefer vendors who demonstrate clear commitment to data protection. This preference is particularly strong in B2B relationships, where data security directly impacts customer business operations.Privacy-by-design approaches often result in more robust, efficient AI systems. When teams must consider privacy implications from the outset, they tend to develop cleaner data architectures, more efficient processing pipelines, and better-documented systems that are easier to maintain and audit.
### Future-Proofing Your AI Privacy Strategy
The intersection of generative AI and data privacy will continue evolving as new techniques emerge and regulations mature. Stay ahead by investing in privacy-enhancing technologies, participating in industry privacy initiatives, and fostering a culture of continuous learning within your organization.Consider emerging technologies like homomorphic encryption, which enables computation on encrypted data, and secure multi-party computation, which allows multiple parties to jointly compute functions over their inputs while keeping them private. While these technologies are still maturing, they represent the future of privacy-preserving computation.
### Building Trust Through Transparency
Ultimately, successful
comes down to building and maintaining trust with customers, partners, and stakeholders. This trust is earned through consistent actions, transparent communication, and demonstrable commitment to privacy principles.Regular privacy reports, clear privacy policies written in plain language, and proactive communication about privacy improvements all contribute to stakeholder confidence. When privacy incidents do occur—and they occasionally will, despite best efforts—transparent communication and swift remediation help maintain trust and demonstrate organizational maturity.

### Voice AI for business in one paragraph
Voice AI for business means software that holds a spoken conversation with a customer or an employee, understands what they want, and completes the task rather than routing them to a menu. It combines speech recognition, a reasoning layer and speech synthesis, and in an enterprise it typically replaces an IVR tree, an outbound calling team, or both.
Gnani AI
reports that
Gnani Agents
runs across voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS, resolves 80% of issues on the first call, responds inside 800ms, and delivers operational cost reductions above 60%, across more than 200 enterprise deployments handling over 30 million daily voice interactions.
### What voice AI actually replaces
The honest version of the business case starts with what is being removed, not with what is being added.
The first thing is the IVR tree. A menu makes the customer translate their problem into the company's internal categories before anything happens, and most people get it wrong, which is why so much IVR traffic ends at an agent anyway. A voice agent takes the problem in the customer's own words and acts on it.
The second is routine outbound calling. Payment reminders, appointment confirmations, renewal notices and survey calls are high volume, low variation and expensive to staff. They are also the calls agents least want to make, so turnover in those teams is high and quality is uneven.
The third is the queue itself. A voice agent has no hold music because concurrency is a capacity decision rather than a staffing one.
publishes support for more than 35,000 simultaneous streams, which is the number that matters on a billing-cycle spike rather than on an average Tuesday.
What does not get removed is the hard conversation. The complaint, the exception, the distressed customer. Those should escalate, and the quality of that handoff decides whether the deployment is seen as a success internally.
ENTERPRISE VOICE AI
See Gnani AI's Voice AI Agent in action
200+ Enterprises · 30M daily calls · 10 Indic languages
Book A Demo
### Where voice AI for business pays back
Deployments succeed when they start with one high-volume, well-defined call type. Four functions consistently produce that kind of starting point.
#### Collections and recovery
Early-stage collections is the clearest case in Indian financial services. Volumes are large, the conversation is structured, the regulatory boundaries are explicit, and the outcome is measurable to the rupee.
publishes a dedicated
collections use case
, and the language coverage matters here more than anywhere else, because a reminder call that lands in the borrower's own language gets answered.
#### Customer support
Order status, balance enquiries, appointment rescheduling and policy questions all have knowable answers sitting in a system the agent has to look up. Automating them frees the human queue for the conversations that need judgement. The
customer support use case
covers the pattern in detail.
#### Onboarding and KYC
Verification conversations are scripted by regulation, which makes them a good automation target and a demanding one. Every mandatory step has to be completed and evidenced, so the audit trail is part of the product rather than an afterthought.
#### Internal service desks
Employee queries about leave policy, payroll and benefits follow the same shape as customer support and carry none of the external risk, which makes them a low-stakes place to learn how the technology behaves before pointing it at customers.

### How a voice AI deployment is put together
Four layers sit behind a spoken conversation, and the weakest one sets the quality of the whole thing.
Speech recognition
converts the caller's audio to text. On Indian telephony this is the layer that breaks most often, because the audio is 8kHz, the line is noisy and the speaker switches between languages inside a sentence.
Gnani Prisma v2.5
is trained on more than 14 million hours of real telephonic audio for exactly this, with 10 or more Indic languages in production and Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish code-switching.
Reasoning
decides what the caller wants and what to do about it.
publishes
Evon
for this layer, tuned for BFSI, insurance, healthcare and telecom.
Speech synthesis
returns the answer as audio.
Gnani Timbre v2.5
, which is in beta, covers 10 or more Indic languages with Indian names, numerals and lakh and crore cadence handled natively.
Integration
connects the agent to the systems that hold the answer.
publishes integrations with Avaya, Cisco, Five9, Vonage, Freshdesk, Salesforce, Zendesk, SAP and Oracle. This layer is where most timelines slip, so scope it before the pilot rather than during it.
### Where it goes wrong
Four failure patterns account for most disappointing deployments.
Automating everything at once.
Broad scope produces flows nobody can test and a payback date nobody can defend. One call type first.
Treating language as a configuration setting.
If the model was not trained on the accents and code-switching your customers actually use, recognition accuracy decides the outcome and no amount of flow design rescues it.
Designing without an escalation path.
Customers hit the edge of the flow on day one. A deployment with no clean handoff converts its hardest conversations into complaints.
Skipping the baseline.
Without cost per contact, resolution rate and handle time captured before launch, the readout becomes an argument about attribution.
### Compliance and deployment control
Voice AI in India touches several regimes at once. Customer data sits under the DPDP Act. Financial services deployments sit under RBI guidelines, insurance under IRDAI, and outbound calling under TRAI rules covering consent and do-not-disturb registries. US healthcare deployments sit under HIPAA.
Two design requirements follow directly. The agent must disclose that it is AI, in the script, at the start of the conversation. And call recordings, transcripts and customer identifiers are personal data, so retention, encryption and access control are part of the deployment design rather than a later hardening exercise.
Where data residency decides the architecture, deployment modes span cloud, private cloud, on-premise and air-gapped, and the
Artha sovereign stack
runs the models inside infrastructure the customer controls.
is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and ISO 27001 certified, and runs HIPAA, GDPR and PCI-DSS compliant deployments. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
### Getting started with voice AI for business
Pick one call type with enough monthly volume to produce a readable result in a quarter. Capture cost per contact, resolution rate and handle time before anything launches. Design the escalation path on day one rather than after the first week of complaints. Then test the speech recognition on your own call recordings, in your customers' languages, because that single measurement predicts more about the outcome than any other part of the evaluation. The
solutions overview
covers the wider stack, and technical detail for each API sits in the
Gnani AI documentation
.
### Frequently asked questions
What is voice AI for business?
Voice AI for business is software that conducts a spoken conversation with a customer or employee, understands the request in natural language, and completes the task by acting on backend systems. In an enterprise it commonly replaces an IVR menu, a routine outbound calling team, or both, and it runs across voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS from one platform.
How is voice AI different from an IVR?
An IVR makes the caller choose from a menu that reflects the company's internal structure. A voice agent takes the request in the caller's own words, works out the intent, and completes the task without the caller navigating anything. The practical difference shows up in containment: menus push a large share of traffic to agents regardless, because people pick the wrong option.
Which business functions benefit most from voice AI?
Collections and recovery, customer support, onboarding and KYC, appointment booking, lead qualification and survey automation. The common pattern is high volume, a knowable correct answer, and a conversation structured enough to test. Internal service desks work well as a first deployment because the risk is contained.
How long does a voice AI deployment take?
Gnani AI publishes under 20 minutes to go live for Gnani Agents on a standard configuration. The realistic enterprise timeline is set by integration and compliance review rather than by building the agent, so scope the systems it must read and write before committing to a date.
Does voice AI work in Indian languages?
Yes, and the quality depends on what the speech models were trained on. The underlying recognition covers 40 or more languages at model level with 10 or more Indic languages in production, including Hindi, Bengali, Kannada, Gujarati, Punjabi, Marathi, Telugu, Tamil and Malayalam, plus code-switched Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish. Models trained mainly on clean English audio degrade sharply on 8kHz Indian telephony.
Can voice AI run inside our own infrastructure?
Yes. Gnani AI publishes cloud, private cloud, on-premise and air-gapped deployment, with the Artha sovereign stack built for buyers whose regulator will not accept customer audio or transcripts leaving the network.

TL;DR:
Automotive lead generation AI uses voice and messaging agents to contact every enquiry within minutes, qualify it against the questions a salesperson would ask, book the test drive, and keep following up until the lead either converts or is genuinely dead. It works in this sector because the failure it fixes is structural rather than skill-based: dealership enquiries arrive faster than the floor can call them back, and a lead that goes uncontacted for a day is competing with three other dealers who did call. The constraints that decide whether a deployment works are language coverage across the dealer network, DND and consent handling on outbound dialling, and a handoff that reaches a named salesperson rather than a queue.
This guide covers where enquiries actually leak in an automotive funnel, which parts of the lifecycle are safe to automate, and what has to be in place before an outbound campaign goes live in India.
### What automotive lead generation AI does
An enquiry arrives from a web form, a marketplace listing, a missed call, a WhatsApp message or a walk-in register. Automotive lead generation AI picks it up automatically and runs the first contact: it calls or messages the prospect, confirms which model they asked about, establishes budget band, finance intent, trade-in and timeline, offers test drive slots from the dealer's calendar, and writes the whole thing back to the CRM with a qualification score attached.
Three properties matter more than the conversational polish. Speed, because the first dealer to make contact has a structural advantage over the second. Consistency, because the same qualifying questions get asked on every lead regardless of how busy the floor is on a Saturday. Persistence, because most enquiries need several attempts across more than one channel, and manual follow-up decays after the second try.
What it does not do is sell the car. Negotiation, objection handling on price, and the relationship that closes the deal stay with the salesperson. The agent's job is to make sure the salesperson spends their day talking to people who are ready to buy.
### Where automotive enquiries leak
Dealer group funnels tend to lose volume at four predictable points, and none of them is a shortage of enquiries.
#### Response lag on inbound enquiries
Enquiries arrive around the clock and get called back during showroom hours, by staff who are also serving walk-ins. The gap between submission and first contact is where most of the loss happens, because the prospect has usually enquired with several dealers at once and engages with whoever reaches them first.
#### Inconsistent qualification
When qualification depends on who picks up the phone, the CRM fills with records that have a name and a model interest and nothing else. Downstream, nobody can prioritise, so the sales team works the list in the order it arrived rather than in the order of likelihood to close.
#### Follow-up decay
A prospect who says "call me next month" needs a call next month. In practice that reminder competes with today's walk-ins and loses. Automated sequencing is the part of this problem that software solves cleanly, because it never gets busy.
#### Language mismatch across the network
A dealer group operating across several states is serving prospects in several languages, and the enquiry routing rarely accounts for it. A prospect who is comfortable in Marathi and gets called in English will answer the questions briefly and disengage. Handling this properly needs production-grade recognition and synthesis per language, which is covered in this guide to
multilingual voice bots in customer service
.
### What to automate across the enquiry lifecycle
The same three tests apply here as anywhere else in voice automation. Is the outcome verifiable in a system of record? Is a wrong action cheap to reverse? Is the prospect likely to be calm? Enquiry handling passes all three; price negotiation and delivery complaints do not.

The handoff deserves specific attention in this sector. A qualified lead should arrive with a named salesperson, not in a shared queue, and should carry the transcript, the model and variant discussed, the budget band, the finance and trade-in answers, and the booked slot. A handoff that loses the qualification answers forces the prospect to repeat themselves, which undoes most of the advantage of having called them quickly. The general design principles are set out in this piece on
what an AI to human handoff should be
### Designing the follow-up sequence
First contact inside the response window you can defend.
Decide the target, measure it, and treat a miss as a defect rather than a busy day. No other variable in the funnel moves as much.
Channel order by how the lead arrived.
A WhatsApp enquiry gets a WhatsApp reply first; a phone enquiry gets a call. Switching channel on the first attempt reads as a different company getting in touch.
Cap attempts and vary the time of day.
Three or four attempts across different parts of the day and week finds most reachable prospects. Beyond that the calls become an irritant and a compliance exposure.
Route by language before you route by model.
Detect the prospect's preferred language on turn one and hold it for the whole sequence, including the messaging follow-ups.
Stop cleanly.
A prospect who says they have bought elsewhere or asks not to be contacted should be suppressed across every channel immediately, including the ones they did not say it on.
Send the booked slot to a person.
The test drive confirmation should name the salesperson the prospect will meet, because that is what makes the appointment stick.
### The technical constraints that decide this
Recognition accuracy on telephony audio is the first ceiling. Prospects answer from cars, roadsides and factory floors, on mobile connections at 8kHz through a lossy codec. Model names, variant names and numbers are exactly the tokens that get lost, and they are the ones the qualification depends on. Gnani AI trains
Prisma v2.5
on telephonic audio for this reason, and Gnani AI reports more than 14 million hours of it in the training corpus.
Synthesis quality decides whether people stay on the call. A voice that mispronounces the model the prospect asked about undermines the whole interaction in the first sentence, so custom pronunciation control for model, variant and dealership names is a requirement rather than a nicety. Gnani AI's synthesis model is
Timbre v2.5
, covering more than ten Indian languages with multiple accents.
CRM write access decides whether any of it produces value. An agent that can qualify a lead but cannot write the qualification back leaves the sales team retyping call notes, which is slower than the process it replaced.
### Consent, DND and data handling
Outbound calling to prospects is regulated, and the automotive funnel is mostly outbound. Before a campaign runs, scrub against the DND registry, record the consent basis for every number, respect permitted calling windows, and keep an auditable record of which consent covered which call. Purchased or scraped lead lists are the usual source of trouble here.
Call recordings, transcripts and prospect details are personal data under India's DPDP Act, so establish retention periods, deletion paths and who can read transcripts. TRAI rules govern outbound telephony and consent specifically. The agent should also disclose that it is an AI at the start of the call, in the script rather than in a policy page. None of this is legal guidance. Confirm the specifics with your legal and compliance team before a production decision.
### Where Gnani AI fits
Gnani AI builds the recognition, synthesis, reasoning and orchestration layers in house, which keeps one vendor accountable for the audit chain across an outbound campaign. Gnani Agents runs the conversation across voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS, Plexus handles the triggers and the audit trail, and Gnani Analytics covers call quality review. Automotive is one of the named verticals under
industry solutions
, with the full product set described on the
enterprise page
Gnani AI reports 30 million daily voice interactions across more than 200 enterprise deployments and capacity above 35,000 simultaneous streams, which is the relevant figure for campaign bursts when a new model launches. Those are vendor-stated numbers and should be tested against your own lead volumes. Related reading covers
conversational AI in lead generation
more generally and the equivalent problem in
real estate lead generation
, or you can
book a technical walkthrough
### Getting the first contact right
Automotive lead generation AI pays for itself in the gap between an enquiry arriving and someone calling it back, and that gap is a staffing problem that automation is unusually well suited to close. Scope it narrowly: one enquiry source, the languages your network actually serves, CRM write access confirmed before launch, and a handoff that reaches a named salesperson with the qualification intact. The selling still belongs to the sales team.
### Frequently Asked Questions
What is automotive lead generation AI?
Automotive lead generation AI is a voice and messaging agent that contacts dealership enquiries automatically, qualifies them on budget, finance, trade-in and timeline, books test drives against the dealer calendar, and writes the result back to the CRM with a score. It handles the first contact and the follow-up sequence, then hands qualified prospects to a named salesperson.
How quickly should a dealership respond to an online enquiry?
As fast as the process allows, because prospects usually enquire with several dealers at once and engage with whoever reaches them first. The practical point is that the target should be defined, measured per enquiry, and treated as a service level rather than an aspiration. Automation matters here because it is the only way to hold the same response time at 2am on a Sunday as at 11am on a Tuesday.
Can an AI agent book test drives directly into the dealer calendar?
Yes, provided the integration allows write access to the scheduling system. This is the part to scope first, because an agent with read-only access can discuss availability but cannot commit a slot, which leaves the salesperson to make a second call and removes most of the benefit.
Does automotive lead generation AI work in Indian languages?
It depends entirely on which languages, tested individually. Dealer networks spanning several states need production-grade recognition and synthesis per language, plus correct handling when a prospect mixes their regional language with English mid-sentence, which is common on model and variant names. Test each language you serve on your own call recordings rather than accepting a headline language count.
What are the compliance rules for outbound calling to car buyers in India?
Outbound telephony, consent and DND are governed by TRAI rules, and prospect data falls under the DPDP Act. Before any campaign, scrub against the DND registry, record the consent basis for each number, respect permitted calling windows, keep an auditable log tying consent to calls, and set retention and deletion terms for recordings and transcripts. Confirm the specifics with your legal and compliance team.
What should a dealer group measure in the first ninety days?
Time to first contact, contact rate by attempt number, qualification completeness on the records written to the CRM, test drive bookings per qualified lead, and show rate against those bookings. Lead volume touched is the metric most likely to look impressive while meaning nothing, because reaching more people badly is not an improvement.

### The Financial Advisory Revolution: Generative AI's Impact on Investment Strategies
In financial world, investors are overwhelmed by a growing maze of market choices, shifting conditions, and economic uncertainty. Traditional methods of investment advice often fall short in handling the vast data and personalization modern investors expect.
Generative AI for investment advice
is rapidly reshaping the industry, enabling financial institutions to analyze complex market dynamics, provide tailored recommendations, and engage clients in smarter, more adaptive ways.
According to a recent McKinsey report,
financial institutions implementing generative AI solutions have seen a 35% improvement in client satisfaction scores and a 28% increase in portfolio performance metrics
. This revolutionary technology is reshaping the investment advice landscape in ways previously unimaginable.
As someone who has worked closely with financial technology innovations for over a decade, I've witnessed the remarkable evolution of investment advisory services. The integration of generative AI represents perhaps the most significant advancement yet—one that promises to democratize access to sophisticated financial guidance while enhancing the capabilities of human advisors.
### What is Generative AI in Banking and Finance?
Generative Artificial Intelligence refers to AI systems that can create new content, insights, or recommendations based on patterns learned from vast datasets. Unlike traditional AI that follows pre-programmed rules, generative AI can synthesize information to produce novel outputs that weren't explicitly programmed.
In the
banking and financial services sector
, generative AI is being deployed to:
Create personalized investment portfolios tailored to individual risk profiles and goals
Generate detailed market analyses and forecasts using multiple data sources
Craft customized financial advisory communications that resonate with specific client segments
Simulate various economic scenarios and their potential impacts on investments
Develop natural language interfaces that make complex financial concepts accessible
The technology combines several advanced capabilities, including natural language processing, deep learning, and predictive analytics.
By 2024, approximately 67% of financial institutions worldwide had incorporated some form of generative AI into their investment advisory services
, according to Financial Technology Partners' industry analysis.
What makes generative AI particularly valuable for investment advice is its ability to process enormous volumes of financial data—from market trends and economic indicators to company performance metrics and global news events—at speeds and scales impossible for human analysis alone.
### The Transformation of Investment Advisory Services
#### From Standardized to Hyper-Personalized Advice
Traditional investment advice typically followed standardized models based on broad demographic factors and risk assessments. Generative AI has fundamentally changed this approach by enabling true hyper-personalization.
Modern generative AI systems can analyze hundreds of data points about an individual investor—from transaction history and spending patterns to life goals and social media sentiment—to create truly customized investment recommendations. This represents a shift from broad asset allocation models to truly individualized financial strategies.
For example, Bank of America's AI-powered investment advisory platform can now factor in a client's evolving life circumstances, behavioral finance tendencies, and even their emotional responses to market volatility when crafting investment advice. This level of personalization was impossible before generative AI technologies matured.
#### Real-Time Portfolio Optimization
One of the most powerful applications of generative AI in investment advice is continuous portfolio optimization. Rather than periodic rebalancing based on calendar dates, AI systems can monitor market conditions, economic indicators, and individual portfolios in real-time.
These systems can identify optimization opportunities as they emerge and recommend strategic adjustments accordingly.
Research from Goldman Sachs indicates that AI-driven portfolio optimization has reduced volatility by up to 18% while improving annualized returns by 3-5% compared to traditional rebalancing approaches
.
The ability to constantly monitor and adapt to changing conditions represents a significant advantage over conventional methods, especially during periods of market turbulence when timely adjustments can preserve capital and capitalize on emerging opportunities.
#### Enhanced Market Analysis and Forecasting
Generative AI has dramatically improved the scope and accuracy of market analysis by processing vast datasets that would overwhelm human analysts. These systems can simultaneously track thousands of securities, economic indicators, geopolitical events, and social media sentiment to identify emerging trends and potential investment opportunities.
The technology can also recognize complex patterns that might escape human detection, such as subtle correlations between seemingly unrelated market sectors or early warning signs of economic shifts.
According to research from MIT's Financial Engineering Department, generative AI forecasting models have demonstrated 23% greater accuracy in predicting market movements compared to traditional statistical methods
Beyond simple prediction, these systems can generate detailed narratives explaining their analyses—making complex financial concepts more accessible to both advisors and clients.
### Voice AI: The New Interface for Financial Guidance
Voice AI represents one of the most transformative applications of generative AI technology in investment advisory services. By combining natural language processing with financial expertise, voice-powered solutions are creating more accessible, intuitive ways for investors to receive guidance.
#### Conversational Finance
Investment advice is increasingly delivered through conversational interfaces that allow clients to ask questions, request information, and receive guidance using natural language.

Generative AI has transformed portfolio construction by enabling truly customized investment strategies based on individual goals, constraints, and preferences.

Short and long-term financial goals
Risk tolerance and behavioral tendencies
Tax considerations and optimization opportunities
Environmental, social, and governance (ESG) preferences
Liquidity needs and time horizons
Existing assets and liabilities

This personalization extends beyond initial portfolio construction to ongoing management. The technology can continually adjust strategies as client circumstances change, markets evolve, or new investment vehicles emerge.

Generative AI excels at extracting insights from unstructured data sources that traditionally fell outside the scope of investment analysis. These systems can process:
Social media conversations and sentiment
News articles and press releases
Earnings call transcripts and corporate communications
Satellite imagery and geospatial data
Consumer spending patterns and trends
Regulatory filings and government data

Analyze company financials across hundreds of metrics simultaneously
Compare performance against sector peers and historical trends
Identify potential red flags or inconsistencies in financial reporting
Summarize key findings in easily digestible formats

Handles data gathering and initial analysis

### FAQs
1. What is agentic AI, and how is it different from the automation BPOs already use?
Agentic AI refers to systems that complete a task end to end rather than assisting a human through part of it. Traditional RPA follows fixed rules and breaks when the input varies or a screen changes. A conversational bot answers a question but hands off anything that needs action. An agentic system interprets the request, decides which steps to take, calls the systems it needs such as CRM, ERP, or a knowledge base, handles the exceptions it can, and escalates the ones it cannot. For a BPO, that is the difference between automating a step in a process and owning the process for a defined set of cases.
2. Which BPO processes are the best candidates for agentic AI?
The strongest candidates are high volume, rule bounded, and currently people intensive. Customer support and inquiry handling for repetitive intents. Data entry and document processing, where OCR and intelligent document processing replace manual keying. Invoice processing and accounts payable, where validation and matching rules can be applied consistently. Compliance checks and reporting, where the same checks must be applied uniformly every time. HR onboarding and employee query handling. Lead qualification, where scoring and initial discovery run at scale. Workload forecasting for staffing. Judgement heavy, low volume, or relationship dependent work is a poor first candidate.
3. How does agentic AI reduce cost in a BPO model?
Through four routes. It removes the linear relationship between volume and headcount, so a spike does not require a hiring cycle. It runs continuously without shift premiums or the scheduling complexity of follow the sun coverage. It reduces rework, since errors caught at entry cost far less than errors corrected downstream in penalties, disputes, and reprocessing. And it cuts the recurring cost of attrition, which in a labour intensive model means constant recruitment and retraining. The offsetting costs are real and should be modelled up front: integration work, data preparation, ongoing model maintenance, and the human review layer that quality assurance still requires.
4. Does automation actually improve accuracy, or just speed?
It improves accuracy where the failure mode is human inconsistency, which covers most repetitive BPO work. A system applies the same validation rules, the same compliance checks, and the same knowledge base answer on the thousandth transaction as on the first, without fatigue or shift to shift variation. Anomaly detection also catches outliers that a person scanning volume tends to miss. Accuracy is not automatic, though. It depends on clean source data, correctly encoded business rules, and continuous monitoring, and it degrades quietly when a process changes upstream and nobody retrains the system. Sampling based human review remains necessary, especially for regulated work.
5. What about data security and compliance in an outsourced setup?
This is usually the deciding constraint, because a BPO processes client data under contract rather than owning it. A deployment needs encryption in transit and at rest, role based least privilege access, audit logging of every automated action, defined retention and deletion policies, and data residency that matches each client's requirements. Voice recordings and transcripts are personal data and voiceprints are biometric data, so anything involving call audio sits in the highest sensitivity tier and should be de-identified before analysis wherever possible. India's DPDP Act applies to Indian customer data, GDPR to EU data subjects, HIPAA to US healthcare, and sector rules from RBI, IRDAI, or TRAI may apply depending on the client and channel. Client contracts and data processing agreements often impose stricter terms than the regulation itself, so route production decisions through your legal and compliance teams.

### Gnani AI reviews: the short version
Most Gnani AI reviews describe a voice AI vendor. That undersells what is actually on offer. Gnani AI builds its own speech and language models and ships four products on top of them, and it will run the whole stack inside your own data centre if your regulator requires it. The four models are
Prisma v2.5
for speech recognition,
Timbre v2.5
for speech synthesis,
Warp v2.0
for native speech to speech, and
Evon
for reasoning. The products are Gnani Agents, Gnani Analytics, Gnani Biometrics and Gnani Assist.
If you are evaluating the platform, the questions that decide the outcome are not about features. They are about which model version you are actually being sold, where it runs, what it costs, and how it behaves on your own audio rather than on a demo script.
### What Gnani AI sells
Gnani AI operates at two layers. The lower layer is a set of proprietary models. The upper layer is a set of products that package those models for a business buyer who does not want to write inference code.
That split matters during procurement. A developer team can take the
speech to text API
or the
text to speech API
and build their own application. A contact centre operations team is more likely to buy Gnani Agents and never touch an API. Both routes use the same underlying models, so accuracy and latency behaviour should be comparable, but the commercial terms and the support model are not.
### The models behind the platform
Gnani AI publishes model specifications on its
models page
. The figures below are the ones Gnani AI states there. They are vendor-reported and worth reproducing on your own data during a pilot.
Specifications as published by Gnani AI on its models page. Vendor-reported figures, worth reproducing on your own data during a pilot.

Two of those numbers deserve a second look. Gnani AI reports that Prisma v2.5 was trained on 14M+ hours of real telephonic audio, which is a different quantity from the clean, read-speech corpora many open models train on. Telephonic audio is narrowband, compressed and noisy, and a model trained on it tends to degrade less on an 8kHz call leg. Gnani AI also reports Prisma v2.5 placing first in eight of nine Indian languages on the Kathbath Noisy 8kHz benchmark, which is a named public benchmark you can look up and rerun.
Evon v3.3 is released under Apache 2.0 at 30 billion parameters with roughly 3.5 billion active per token. An open weight licence changes the risk calculation for a bank or an insurer, because the model can be inspected, fine tuned and run without a dependency on the vendor's uptime.
### What the four products do
#### Agents
Voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS agents with handoff to a human. This is the product behind most of the deployments Gnani AI describes in its
customer stories
. The interesting engineering question here is turn taking, because a voice agent that answers correctly but 900 milliseconds late still feels broken to a caller. Gnani AI's writing on
voice AI latency budgets
sets out how those budgets are usually split.
#### Analytics
Conversation intelligence over completed and in-flight calls: sentiment, compliance flagging, automated scoring and quality checks across the full call volume rather than a sampled few percent. If your current QA process reviews two calls per agent per month, the change is one of coverage rather than of method.
#### Biometrics
Voice authentication, anti-spoofing and deepfake detection. Gnani AI reports extracting more than 300 voice features per call to build a voiceprint. Voiceprints are biometric data under the DPDP Act and under most banking supervision regimes, so the storage and consent design here is a legal question as much as a technical one. Confirm the handling with your legal and compliance team before you scope a rollout.
#### Assist
Real time guidance for human agents: knowledge retrieval mid-call, next best action, and automated CRM updates. It sits alongside a human rather than replacing one, which usually makes it the easiest of the four to get past a change management review.
### What Gnani AI reviews rarely cover: deployment and residency
The deployment question is where this platform separates from most of the market. Gnani AI offers cloud, private cloud, on-premise and air-gapped deployment, and its
Artha sovereign stack
packages Evon, Prisma, Timbre and Plexus to run inside your own infrastructure on a single node. Gnani AI's position is that DPDP, RBI and IRDAI residency requirements are met by controlling where the model runs.
That is a design choice with a real cost attached. Running models on your own hardware means you own the capacity planning, the GPU budget and the upgrade cycle. It is the right answer for a regulated institution that cannot send call audio to a shared cloud, and the wrong answer for a team that wants to ship in a fortnight. Decide which of those you are before the first demo.
On certifications, Gnani AI lists SOC 2 Type 2, ISO 27001, HIPAA, GDPR and PCI-DSS. Ask for the current attestation reports rather than accepting the logos, because scope and expiry dates matter more than the badge.
### What Gnani AI does not publish
Gnani AI does not publish a public pricing page. There is no per-minute rate, no tiered plan table and no published enterprise floor anywhere on the site. For a buyer running a shortlist, that is a genuine disadvantage against vendors who post their rate card, because you cannot size a business case without a sales conversation.
Latency figures are published for some models and not others. Gnani AI states sub-100ms time to first audio for Timbre v2.5 and sub-200ms P95 for Warp v2.0, and gives 302ms to first token with 257 tokens per second sustained for Evon v3.3. Prisma v2.5 has no published latency figure on the models page. If streaming recognition latency is on your requirements list, ask for it directly and ask for the measurement conditions alongside it.
### How to evaluate Gnani AI in a pilot
A shortlist decision made on marketing pages is a decision made on the wrong data. Run these six checks instead.
Bring your own audio.
Use 200 or more of your real recorded calls, not the vendor's sample set, and include the accents, the background noise and the code switching your callers actually produce.
Measure word error rate per language, not in aggregate.
An average across eleven languages hides the one language where the model fails.
Measure latency at P95, not at the mean.
The mean hides the calls where the agent talks over the caller.
Test the handoff.
Ask what happens when the model is not confident, and watch a live transfer to a human rather than reading about it.
Price the deployment you will actually run.
A cloud quote tells you nothing about the cost of an on-premise node.
Run the same test on two vendors.
The
comparison hub
lists the alternatives worth putting alongside it.
Developers can start without a sales conversation. The
API documentation
covers the speech endpoints, and the
enterprise product pages
cover the packaged applications. If you want the deeper technical background on how the recognition side works, the explainer on
ASR versus speech to text
is a good starting point.
### Frequently asked questions
Is Gnani AI an Indian company building its own models?
Yes. Gnani AI trains its own speech and language models rather than wrapping a third party API, and publishes the specifications for Prisma v2.5, Timbre v2.5, Warp v2.0 and Evon on its models page. Evon v3.3 is released under an Apache 2.0 open weight licence, which means the weights can be downloaded and run independently.
How many languages does Gnani AI support?
Gnani AI reports 40+ languages at the model level for speech recognition and 21+ for speech synthesis, with 10+ Indian languages in production automatic speech recognition. Evon v3.3 is trained natively on eleven Indian languages. Language counts vary by product and by model version, so confirm the specific list for the languages your callers use.
What does Gnani AI cost?
Gnani AI does not publish pricing. Rates come from a sales conversation, and they will vary with deployment model, volume commitment and the difference between API access and a packaged product. Ask for a per-minute rate and an annual floor in the same quote so you can compare it against vendors who publish theirs.
Can Gnani AI run on-premise or air-gapped?
Yes. Gnani AI offers cloud, private cloud, on-premise and air-gapped deployment, and the Artha stack is built for single-node self-hosted operation. This is the main reason regulated Indian institutions shortlist it. Confirm the hardware requirements and the support terms for a self-hosted deployment early, because they differ substantially from a cloud contract.
How accurate is Gnani AI speech recognition on Indian languages?
Gnani AI reports Prisma v2.5 ranking first in eight of nine Indian languages on the Kathbath Noisy 8kHz benchmark. That is a public benchmark on narrowband noisy audio, which is closer to telephony conditions than most clean-speech benchmarks. Accuracy on your own call recordings is the number that should decide the purchase, so reproduce it during the pilot.
What should I look for in Gnani AI reviews before I shortlist?
Look past the feature list for three things: which model version the review is describing, which deployment mode it was tested in, and whether the reviewer measured anything on their own audio. Reviews that describe a cloud trial tell you very little about how the same models behave on a self-hosted node, and model versions move fast enough that a review from last year may describe software you cannot buy today.

The practical test for any ASR for Indian languages is not a published accuracy number. It is what the model does to your own call recordings, with your own vocabulary, at the bandwidth your carrier delivers.
### What ASR for Indian Languages Has to Solve
The Eighth Schedule of the Constitution of India recognises 22 languages, and Indian contact centres field calls in most of them alongside English. A speech recognition model trained mostly on clean, read, 16kHz English audio meets none of the conditions that define an Indian production call.
Four properties separate this problem from generic speech recognition.
#### Telephony bandwidth, not studio audio
Most enterprise voice traffic in India arrives over narrowband telephony at 8kHz. Compression removes the high-frequency detail that distinguishes similar consonants, and the loss is permanent by the time the model sees the waveform. A model evaluated on 16kHz studio recordings has been measured on a different signal.
#### Code-switching inside a single sentence
Speakers move between English and Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Marathi or Bengali within one utterance, often on the words that matter most: product names, finance terms, dates and amounts. A language-identification router that picks one language per call will mis-transcribe exactly those tokens.
#### Retroflex consonants, aspiration and vowel length
Indian languages use phonetic contrasts that English does not. Tamil separates retroflex from dental consonants. Hindi distinguishes aspirated from unaspirated pairs. Dravidian languages carry agglutinative morphology, so a single spoken word can encode tense, person, number and case at once, which enlarges the effective vocabulary the model has to cover.
#### Alphanumeric strings under noise
Account numbers, policy numbers, registration numbers and one-time codes are the highest-value tokens on a call and the most fragile. Blended accuracy on conversational speech tells you nothing about how a model handles a fourteen-character alphanumeric string spoken quickly over a moving vehicle.

### Where ASR for Indian Languages Breaks in Production
Deployments fail in predictable places, and most of them are testable before contract.
#### Evaluating on the wrong audio
A pilot run on hand-picked clean recordings will flatter every vendor on the shortlist. Run the evaluation on a stratified sample of real calls: peak hour, low signal, crosstalk, and the accents your actual customer base has.
#### Ignoring the long tail of vocabulary
Product names, scheme names, branch names and local place names rarely appear in general training data. Ask how domain vocabulary is injected, how quickly a new term takes effect, and whether it needs a retrain.
#### Treating one blended accuracy number as the answer
Break the measurement apart. Word error rate on conversational speech, entity-level accuracy on identifiers, and speaker attribution accuracy are three different results, and a system can be strong on the first while being unusable on the second.
#### Skipping the failure path

What is a good word error rate for ASR for Indian languages?
There is no single threshold, because word error rate depends entirely on the audio it was measured on. Gnani AI reports under 4% WER on Indian speech for Prisma v2.5, and a first-place result in 8 of 9 Indian languages on Kathbath Noisy 8kHz. Can ASR handle people mixing English and Hindi in one sentence?
Yes, when the model is trained on code-switched speech rather than on separate monolingual corpora. Gnani AI reports 96% code-switching accuracy for Prisma v2.5. How much does telephony audio quality affect accuracy?
Substantially. Narrowband 8kHz telephony discards high-frequency information that helps separate similar consonants, and that information cannot be recovered downstream. ### AI patient engagement: the short version
Patient engagement is the work of staying in contact with a patient between clinical encounters: confirming the appointment, preparing them for a procedure, checking they are taking the medication, and following up after discharge. Hospitals have always known this work matters. Most do not do it at scale, because it is thousands of short phone calls a week and the staff making them are also running the front desk.
Voice AI changes the volume constraint rather than the clinical model. An agent places the reminder call, confirms or reschedules, answers the preparation question, logs the response in the patient record, and escalates anything clinical to a human. It handles the routine contact. It does not triage, diagnose or give clinical advice, and a deployment that lets it do any of those is badly designed.
### What patient engagement means operationally
#### The gap between appointments
A hospital's systems are built around the encounter. The patient arrives, is seen, and leaves with instructions. What happens over the following six weeks is largely invisible to the organisation until the patient either returns as planned or turns up in emergency.
Closing that gap is a contact problem before it is a technology problem. Every missed appointment is a wasted clinical slot and a patient who did not get care. Every unfilled prescription is a treatment plan that exists only on paper.
#### Why voice rather than messaging alone
Messaging is cheap and works well for patients who read it. For older patients, patients on basic handsets, and patients who do not read the language the message was sent in, a phone call still outperforms a link. Voice also allows a response that is more than a tap: a patient can say they are unwell, that they cannot afford the medication, or that they were never told about the follow-up.
The practical approach in most hospitals is both. Messaging carries the confirmation and the link, and voice handles the patients who do not respond to it and the conversations that need an answer rather than an acknowledgement.
