TL;DR.
Predictive analytics for banks means using historical and live customer data to estimate what a customer is likely to do next, then acting on that estimate before they ask. The common applications are next-best-product recommendations, credit risk scoring, fraud detection, churn prediction and collections prioritisation. The hard part is rarely the model. It is getting clean signals out of systems that were never designed to share them, and acting on a prediction inside a channel the customer actually uses.
### What predictive analytics for banks means in practice
A prediction is only useful if something happens because of it. That gives you a three-part test for any use case: is there a signal, is there a decision, and is there a channel to act through. Most stalled programmes have the first and are missing one of the other two.
Take churn. The signal might be a falling balance, a lapsed standing instruction and two complaint calls in a month. The decision is whether this customer gets a retention offer, a service call or nothing. The channel is whoever reaches the customer, which in Indian retail banking is usually an outbound call rather than an email. A model that produces a churn score with no owned decision and no outbound capacity produces a report, not a result.
ENTERPRISE VOICE AI
See Gnani AI's Voice AI Agent in action
200+ Enterprises · 30M daily calls · 10 Indic languages
Book A Demo
### Five applications of predictive analytics in banking
#### Next-best-product recommendations
Transaction patterns, life-stage signals and product holdings feed a ranking of what to offer and when. The discipline is suppression as much as selection: a customer who was declined a card last month should not be offered the same card this month.
#### Credit risk and loan decisioning
Alternative signals supplement bureau scores for thin-file applicants. This is the use case where governance matters most, because the model decides who gets credit and the bank carries the explanation burden when it declines.
#### Fraud detection
Deviation from a customer's own behaviour, scored in real time rather than reviewed overnight. Where the channel is voice, caller verification becomes part of the same decision.
Gnani Biometrics
verifies callers passively from voice and flags synthetic or cloned audio, with Gnani AI reporting a 99%+ fraud detection rate and verification in under five seconds.
#### Churn prediction and retention
Early signals from behaviour and from conversations, acted on while the relationship is still recoverable. Conversation data is the underused half of this, because dissatisfaction shows up in how a customer speaks to the contact centre well before it shows up in their balance.
#### Collections prioritisation
Propensity to pay decides who gets a reminder, who gets a call and who gets a settlement conversation, which keeps effort off accounts that would have paid anyway. The
collections voice AI
page covers the execution side.

### The data work underneath
Four problems come up in almost every Indian bank programme, in this order.
Fragmented customer identity.
The same person exists as different records in core banking, the cards platform, the loan system and the CRM. Until identity is resolved, every model is trained on partial behaviour.
Latency mismatch.
A fraud model needs signals in milliseconds, a churn model is fine with yesterday's batch. Building everything to the strictest requirement is how programmes run out of budget.
Unstructured conversation data.
Call recordings hold the clearest statements of customer intent in the bank and are usually the last source connected, because turning them into structured signals needs accurate transcription in the languages customers actually speak.
Action plumbing.
A score has to arrive in the agent desktop, the outbound dialler or the app, at the moment the decision is made. This is unglamorous integration work and it is what separates a pilot from a deployment.
### Where conversation data fits
Banks already own a large behavioural dataset they rarely model: what customers say on the phone. Turning it into a predictive signal takes two layers. The first is transcription accurate enough on 8kHz telephony audio in code-mixed speech to be worth modelling.
Gnani Prisma v2.5
is trained on 14M+ hours of real telephonic audio, reports under 4% word error rate on Indian speech and 96% code-switching accuracy, and carries domain vocabulary for terms such as CIBIL, PAN, NEFT, RTGS and UPI.
The second is structuring what was said into topics, sentiment, complaint drivers and compliance flags across every call rather than a sample. That is the job of
Gnani Analytics
, which Gnani AI associates with a 20% improvement in retention and three times more accurate root-cause analysis. Those are vendor figures, so prove them against your own corpus before putting them in a business case.
### Governance, bias and regulation
Predictive models in banking sit inside a dense regulatory perimeter. Customer data is personal data under India's DPDP Act, credit and collections decisions carry RBI expectations, insurance cross-sell carries IRDAI, and outbound contact carries TRAI consent and DND rules. Voiceprints and speaker embeddings are biometric data and are handled at the highest sensitivity tier.
Three controls do most of the work. Keep a documented record of what each model uses as input and why, so a declined customer can be given a reason. Test outcomes across customer segments for disparate impact rather than assuming the model is neutral because no protected attribute was passed to it. Decide where the model runs: for banks that cannot let data leave their network,
Gnani Artha
describes the sovereign deployment of the stack, and Gnani AI offers cloud, private cloud, on-premise and air-gapped options, with SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 certification and HIPAA, GDPR and PCI-DSS compliance. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
### Getting started with predictive analytics for banks
Start with one decision that someone already owns and that has a channel attached. Collections prioritisation and churn save are the usual first choices, because the action is clear, the owner exists, and the outcome is measurable within a quarter. Capture the baseline before the model goes live, then compare like with like: contact rate, promise-to-pay conversion, save rate, and cost per successful action.

### Frequently asked questions
What is predictive analytics for banks?
It is the use of historical and live customer data to estimate what a customer is likely to do next, then acting on that estimate. Common applications are next-best-product recommendations, credit decisioning, fraud detection, churn prediction and collections prioritisation.
Which predictive analytics use case should a bank start with?
The one where a decision owner and a contact channel already exist. Collections prioritisation and churn save usually qualify, because the action is clear and the outcome is measurable within a quarter.
Why do predictive analytics programmes stall in banks?
Usually because of fragmented customer identity across core banking, cards, loans and CRM, or because the score never reaches the agent desktop or dialler at the moment the decision is made.
How does call data improve predictive models in banking?
Call recordings carry the clearest statements of customer intent a bank holds. Converting them into topics, sentiment and complaint drivers needs transcription that is accurate on 8kHz telephony audio in code-mixed Indian speech.
What regulations apply to predictive analytics in Indian banking?
Customer data is personal data under the DPDP Act, credit and collections decisions carry RBI expectations, cross-sell into insurance carries IRDAI, outbound contact carries TRAI consent and DND rules, and voiceprints are biometric data. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
How do banks manage model bias in credit decisions?
Keep a documented record of every model input and why it is used, so a declined customer can be given a reason, and test outcomes across customer segments for disparate impact rather than assuming neutrality because no protected attribute was passed in.

### TL;DR
Prisma v3.0 is Gnani AI’s automatic speech recognition (ASR) model for ten languages, nine of them Indian: Hindi, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Punjabi, Kannada, Telugu, Tamil, Malayalam and English. It is built for code-mixed speech, where a speaker switches languages within a sentence, and its Code-mix mode writes each language in its own script. It takes native 8 kHz telephony audio as well as 16 kHz app and VoIP audio.
Its Auto-LID layer (language identification) identifies the spoken language with 98% accuracy on clips over 3 seconds (Vistaar and Svarah corpora). It recorded a macro word error rate (WER) of 16.93 on Vistaar, against 19.98 for ElevenLabs Scribe v2, 20.51 for Microsoft Azure STT and 26.57 for Deepgram Nova 3, and a lower WER than ElevenLabs Scribe v2 and Azure STT in all nine Indian languages. It offers four output modes (Verbatim, Transcribe, Code-mix and Transliterate), and you choose one per request, so each system that reads the transcript gets text written the way it needs.
Introducing Gnani Prisma v3.0, built for Indian calls that switch between Hindi, English and Kannada in a single sentence, run over busy streets and weak connections, and use brand names a model was never told about.
#GnaniAI #PrismaV3 #SpeechRecognition #IndianLanguages #ASR https://t.co/XBw1E9vktu
— Gnani AI (@GnaniAi)
### What is Prisma v3.0, and why did we build it?
Prisma v3.0 is Gnani AI’s automatic speech recognition (ASR) model for ten languages (nine Indian languages and English), and the successor to Prisma 2.5. It works as a speech to text model for calls, recordings and voice notes, and it is built for how India speaks: code-mixed, with fillers and spoken numbers, and at times over poor connectivity.
We built it because a correct transcript still wasn’t a usable one. Accuracy was the first job. After that, three gaps remained: output format, custom vocabulary and language detection.
Output format:
The text came back in one format, but a voice agent, a compliance team and a search index each need it written differently.
Custom vocabulary:
The model didn’t know your words, so “NACH mandate” became “nack mandate”.
Language detection:
It guessed the language, so a short “haan” landed in the wrong one.
Each gap used to be patched outside the model, with parsers, spelling tables, and a good deal of manual effort. Prisma v3.0 closes all three inside the model. In one request, you choose how the call is written, give it your own terms, and give it language hints or let it detect the language.
### When one word goes wrong, the whole conversation does
When the transcript is wrong, a voice agent has no way to know. Suppose a caller says “barah hazaar paanch sau” and the transcript reads “12” and “500”. The agent quotes the wrong amount, the caller repeats themselves and then asks for a human. A single wrong word can also compound as the call goes on. Across thousands of calls, that is how one recognition error becomes lower customer satisfaction (CSAT). The example is illustrative.
Here is where wrong transcripts come from, and what Prisma v3.0 does about each cause.
Cause
What the agent receives
What Prisma v3.0 does
Spoken numbers
Amounts in words that the next system must parse
Inverse text normalisation (ITN) in Transcribe mode writes spoken numbers as ₹12,500, 3,50,000 or an OTP such as 472916
Mixed languages
English terms in the wrong script
Code-mix mode keeps each language in its own script. Script-constrained decoding cut wrong-script outputs from 12 to 0 across 66,305 clips
Brand and product names
“smart save plus” instead of SmartSave Plus
Keyterm prompting helps the model hear the name, and find and replace fixes its spelling
Accent and diction
The same word written several ways
Keyterm prompting raised recall of supplied terms from 70.9% to 90.3%
Short replies such as “haan”
The wrong language guessed
Language hints nearly halved WER on real Hindi-English calls, from 34.14 to 18.93 compared with the previous model
Noisy or silent audio
Words nobody said, or missed words
Trained and evaluated on six real telephony codecs with native 8 kHz input. False text on noise-only audio fell from 13.4% to 4.2% compared with the previous model
### Choose your output mode based on how you use the text
Prisma v3.0 has four output modes: Verbatim, Transcribe, Code-mix and Transliterate. You set the mode on each request, depending on what the text is for. The table shows what each mode writes, with an example and where it fits.

Transliteration changes how words are written, not what they mean. It is different from translation, which changes the language itself. Only Transcribe mode applies ITN, which turns spoken amounts into written ones with Indian grouping, so “three lakh fifty thousand” becomes 3,50,000. Verbatim, Code-mix and Transliterate keep numbers as spoken words. All four modes work on REST, streaming and batch endpoints.
For Hinglish speech to text, use Code-mix to keep Hindi in Devanagari and English words in Latin script, or Transliterate to write the whole call in Latin letters.
### Get your words right: keyterm prompting
Take a customer who calls about her Crompton geyser. Callers across Hindi, Marathi and Tamil say that word with different sounds, and a generic model writes what it hears: “geezer”, “gizar”, गीज़र, and “crumpton” for the brand. Your dashboard now counts one product several ways, and a search for “geyser” misses many of the calls. These spellings are illustrative, not real model output.
Keyterm prompting fixes this at the source. You pass Crompton and geyser with the request, and the model is biased toward those words. You can send up to 200 terms, plus a topic description, up to four speaker names and the previous transcript, in any combination. Speaker names work the same way: in 1,000 test requests, the model inserted no name that was not spoken.
Heard as
Term supplied
smart save plus
SmartSave Plus
nack mandate
NACH mandate
HB a one see report
HbA1c report
tat kal ticket, P and R
Tatkal ticket, PNR
E Sim
eSIM
These pairs illustrate the kind of error keyterm prompting addresses. In our evaluation, keyterm recall rose from 70.9% to 90.3%, with gains in all ten languages. The share of your terms that went missing fell from about 3 in 10 to about 1 in 10, with no fine-tuning and no training data. The test used public read speech with the correct terms supplied, so treat it as an upper bound. In 200 prompt-injection tests, none of the injected instructions were followed.
Find and replace is the final lock. Keyterms help the model hear your word, and a rule (up to ten per request) sets its exact spelling, or changes the name of a campaign or product, across the whole transcript. Turn “smart save plus” into “SmartSave Plus” once, and your brand reads the same in every transcript. Rules work on words, abbreviations and phrases, not on symbols.
### Accuracy you can measure
For multilingual speech recognition, two measures matter most: how many words it gets wrong, and how often it picks the right language.
#### Word error rate (WER) by datasets
WER counts substitutions, deletions and insertions against a reference transcript,
so lower is better
. On the official Vistaar protocol, Prisma v3.0 recorded a macro WER of 16.93 across nine Indian languages and seven datasets. That is 15.3% lower than ElevenLabs Scribe v2 (19.98), 17.5% lower than Microsoft Azure STT (20.51) and 36.3% lower than Deepgram Nova 3 (26.57). Prisma v3.0 scored lower than ElevenLabs Scribe v2 and Deepgram Nova 3 on every one of the seven datasets, and lower than Microsoft Azure STT on six of the seven.

#### Language identification (LID)
98% language identification accuracy on the Vistaar and Svarah corpora, for clips longer than 3 seconds.
When a voice agent picks the wrong language, the whole turn is written in the wrong script and every later step inherits the mistake. Language identification (LID) decides which language is being spoken. Prisma v3.0 gets it right on 98 of every 100 clips longer than 3 seconds, so one agent can serve callers in all ten languages and follow them when they switch, with no “press 1 for Hindi” menu.
Setting
What it does and when to use it
Automatic detection
The model identifies the language and writes it in the matching script. Use it when the caller can speak any supported language.

### What better transcripts mean for voice AI
Every voice agent reply starts with call transcription. The more often the transcript is right the first time, the further the agent can take a call alone.
Fewer repeated questions:
Amounts, names and one-word replies are understood the first time, so callers have less reason to repeat themselves.
Fewer handovers to a human:
With fewer wrong turns, more calls stay with the agent. Separately, one- and two-word turns scored a WER of 7.67 on 465 production samples.
Better ticket resolution:
With the right number, product and intent in the CRM entry, fewer tickets need a callback to correct them.
Data where it must stay:
Prisma v3.0 runs in the cloud, in hybrid setups or fully on-premise, including air-gapped environments.
Industry Playbook for Prisma v3.0
### Put your toughest audio to the test
Anything built on speech starts with audio transcription, whether it is a call, a meeting, a video or a voice note. Prisma v3.0 writes the transcript in the language, script and spelling you need, so everything built on top of it starts from the right words.
Try Prisma v3.0
on your own audio. Or just send us your toughest, noisiest, de-identified recording along with your custom vocabulary, such as product and brand names, and we will return transcripts in all four modes to compare with what you use today.
### Frequently Asked Questions
Which mode should I use for a voice agent?
Start with Transcribe. The LLM gets clean text with amounts already in digits. Switch to Code-mix if your intent models or keyword rules expect English terms like EMI or refund in Latin script.
Can I get two modes for the same recording?
Yes, with two requests. Mode is set per request and each request returns one output, so send the same audio twice with different modes. For example, Verbatim for the compliance archive and Transcribe for the agent.
Does inverse text normalisation (ITN) work in every mode?
No. ITN works only in Transcribe mode. Verbatim, Code-mix and Transliterate keep numbers as spoken words, which is what an audit record, a chat-style log or a Roman-script log needs.
How are keyterms prompting different from find and replace?
Keyterm prompting shapes recognition, so the model leans toward words you supply. Find and replace fixes spelling after recognition. For a brand or scheme name, use both: keyterm prompting helps the model hear NACH mandate, and a rule makes sure “nack mandate” is always written NACH mandate.
Does sending more key terms affect accuracy?
No. With up to 200 keyterms per request, accuracy is still better than without keyterm prompting. Send the terms the call is likely to contain, such as product, brand and scheme names.
What audio does it accept?
Native 8 kHz telephony audio and 16 kHz app or VoIP audio. It is trained and evaluated on six real telephony codecs, so it is built for noisy, code-mixed audio.

## Introducing the Prompt Engine: Scenario-Based Prompting for Complex Conversations

TL;DR:
The Prompt Engine is Gnani AI's scenario-based prompting capability in the Agent Builder, built for complex business conversations. Instead of reading one long prompt on every turn, the agent reads only the scenario it is currently in. For example for a renewal call that handles objections, or a claims conversation with a dozen branches, that means lower token usage, lower latency and a cost per turn that stays steady as the conversation grows.
### Why do complex conversations cost more?
A single prompt works well for a narrow use case. There is little to read, so every turn is fast and cost-efficient.
Complex use cases are different. A renewal call that has to handle objections, a claims conversation with a dozen branches or a multi-step interview all need the prompt to cover every branch and fallback. The agent then reads all of it on every turn, including the parts that have nothing to do with what the customer just said.
That is how a single prompt scales: efficient when the use case is narrow, heavier on every turn as it widens. More branches mean more tokens per turn, so cost and latency climb, and at enterprise call volumes that adds up quickly.
### What is the Prompt Engine?
The Prompt Engine is Gnani AI's scenario-based prompting capability, built into Agent Builder for complex business use cases. It breaks a conversation into scenarios, self-contained pieces of the flow, so the agent works from the piece it is in rather than the whole script.
### Single prompt vs. the Prompt Engine
Both approaches are valid. The right one depends on how complex the conversation is.
Aspect
Single prompt
Prompt Engine (scenario-based)
Best fit
A narrow, straightforward use case
A complex use case with several branches, objections or fallbacks
How it reads the conversation
The full prompt on every turn
Only the current scenario on each turn
Token usage per turn
Low, because the prompt is small
Stays low as the conversation covers more ground
Latency
Fast, as there is little to read
Fast, as only the relevant scenario is read
Example
A simple FAQ AI Agent or a single-step reminder call
A renewal call with objections, a multi-branch claims conversation
### Why this matters as conversations get complex
Lower token usage:
Cost per turn stays low even as the conversation covers more ground, instead of climbing with every branch.
Lower latency:
Less text to read each turn means a faster response, however many scenarios make up the conversation.
Cost efficiency at scale:
Adding a scenario for a new case does not make any other scenario bigger, so cost per turn does not climb as complexity is added.
### How scenario-based prompting works
Real conversations do not run in a straight line. A customer might answer a question before it is asked, circle back to an earlier point or raise something unrelated mid-topic. Scenario-based prompting builds transitions and fallbacks around that.
Appointment Booking Agent
#### Split the conversation into scenarios
Instead of one long prompt anticipating every turn, the conversation is divided into scenarios. The agent starts at one, such as confirming who is on the line, and moves to the next, such as finding out where a renewal stands.
#### Carry details forward
Some transitions pull a detail from what the customer just said, a name for example, and carry it into the next scenario. The agent does not need the whole conversation repeated back to it.
#### Configure ahead, decide live
Scenarios, transitions and fallbacks are set up in advance in Agent Builder. The path each call takes is decided in real time, based on what the customer says.
#### Read only what is relevant
At any moment the agent reads only the scenario it is in. That keeps each turn fast and cost-efficient, however complex the overall conversation gets.
### What this looks like in a real call
Take a motor insurance renewal reminder. It moves through five scenarios: confirming who is on the line, finding out where the renewal stands, making the case for renewing on time, working through hesitation, and closing with a payment link, a callback or a handoff to a specialist.
Customers rarely follow the script, and the agent does not need them to:
They say the vehicle has been sold:
the scenario the agent is in picks it up and moves accordingly.
They mention a competitor’s offer:
a global transition catches it, wherever the call is.
They ask for a human or want the calls to stop:
also caught globally, so it never depends on the step the agent is on.
Each agent sets up its own fallbacks, because a renewal reminder and a claims conversation need different instincts.
### What this means for your team
For the people building agents:
Debug and improve one piece of a conversation without touching the rest, and add a scenario for a fresh situation without making the others bigger or slower.
For the customer on the call:
The agent can hold a long, branching conversation instead of only a short, predictable one. That matters most when the call is complicated: a renewal with a few objections, a claims conversation, a payment discussion that does not resolve the first time.
### Start with your most complex use case
Complex conversations should not cost more on every turn. With the Prompt Engine, the agent reads only the scenario it is in, so token usage and latency stay low however many branches you add. Your most complex enterprise use cases, solved with our prompt engine.
Talk to the Gnani AI team
to see how scenario-based prompting works.
### Frequently Asked Questions
What is the Prompt Engine?
It is Gnani AI's scenario-based prompting capability inside Agent Builder. It breaks a complex conversation into scenarios, so the agent reads only the scenario relevant to where the conversation currently is, instead of the full prompt on every turn.
Does the Prompt Engine replace single-prompt agents?
No. A single prompt still works well for a straightforward use case. The Prompt Engine is built for complex use cases, with enough branches, objections and fallbacks that a single prompt would keep growing with every case it needs to cover.
How does scenario-based prompting lower token usage and latency?
Each turn reads only the scenario relevant to where the conversation currently is, not the entire prompt, so the amount of text read on every turn stays small even as the conversation covers more ground.
What are global transitions?
They are fallbacks that apply whichever scenario the agent is in, built for things like a callback request, a competitor mention or a customer asking for a human. They sit above the individual scenarios, so they are caught wherever the conversation is.
Can teams configure their own scenarios?
Yes. Scenarios, transitions and fallbacks are configured ahead of time inside Agent Builder, and teams can add a scenario for a fresh case without changing the rest of the conversation.
Is the Prompt Engine available today?
Yes. It is built into Agent Builder now for teams running complex business use cases.

## Prompt Meaning in Hindi: प्रॉम्प्ट क्या है

### TL;DR
Prompt meaning in Hindi: प्रॉम्प्ट का मतलब है वह निर्देश जो आप किसी AI मॉडल को देते हैं। A prompt is the instruction you give an AI model, written in plain language. प्रॉम्प्टिंग उस निर्देश को अच्छी तरह लिखने का कौशल है। A good prompt states the role, the task, the input and the output format. A weak prompt states only the task and leaves the model to guess the rest, which is where most disappointing results come from.
### Prompt meaning in Hindi: प्रॉम्प्ट का मतलब
प्रॉम्प्ट एक निर्देश है। आप AI से जो चाहते हैं, उसे शब्दों में लिखना ही प्रॉम्प्ट है।
The English word prompt means to cause something to happen, or a cue given to an actor. In AI the second sense is closer. A prompt is the cue you hand the model, and the model responds to what is in the cue rather than to what you had in mind.
यह अंतर महत्वपूर्ण है। मॉडल आपके इरादे को नहीं पढ़ता। वह सिर्फ आपके लिखे शब्दों पर काम करता है।
That single fact explains most of what follows. If the output is vague, the prompt was vague. If the output is in the wrong format, the prompt did not specify a format.
### प्रॉम्प्ट और प्रॉम्प्टिंग में क्या अंतर है
प्रॉम्प्ट एक चीज़ है। प्रॉम्प्टिंग एक कौशल है।
A prompt is the text itself. Prompting is the practice of writing, testing and refining that text until the output is reliable. एक बार सही उत्तर मिल जाना अलग बात है, और हर बार सही उत्तर मिलना अलग बात है। The second is the one that matters in business, because a prompt that works once and fails on the next twenty inputs is not usable in production.
### Types of prompts and their Hindi meaning
प्रॉम्प्ट कई प्रकार के होते हैं। नीचे दी गई तालिका में हर प्रकार का मतलब और उपयोग दिया गया है।
प्रॉम्प्ट के प्रकार / Types of prompts
Type
हिंदी में मतलब
What it does
कब इस्तेमाल करें
Instructional
निर्देशात्मक प्रॉम्प्ट
States the task directly and expects the model to carry it out
जब काम स्पष्ट हो और उदाहरण की ज़रूरत न हो
Zero-shot
बिना उदाहरण वाला प्रॉम्प्ट
Asks for the output with no worked example attached
आसान और आम कामों के लिए
Few-shot
कुछ उदाहरण वाला प्रॉम्प्ट
Shows two or three worked examples so the model copies the pattern
जब उत्तर का प्रारूप हर बार एक जैसा चाहिए
Role-based
भूमिका आधारित प्रॉम्प्ट
Assigns the model a role, which narrows its tone and vocabulary
ग्राहक से बातचीत और सहायता वाले कामों में
Chain-of-thought
चरणबद्ध सोच वाला प्रॉम्प्ट
Asks the model to work through the steps before answering
गणना और तर्क वाले कामों में
Extraction
जानकारी निकालने वाला प्रॉम्प्ट
Pulls named fields out of a longer text into a fixed structure
ट्रांसक्रिप्ट और दस्तावेज़ से डेटा निकालने के लिए
अधिकतर व्यावसायिक काम के लिए instructional और few-shot प्रॉम्प्ट सबसे उपयोगी होते हैं। For most business tasks you will combine two or three of these rather than picking one.
### How to write a good prompt for business
एक अच्छे प्रॉम्प्ट में चार हिस्से होते हैं। A workable prompt names four things.
Role (भूमिका).
मॉडल को बताइए कि वह किस भूमिका में है। "You are a collections agent for a bank" narrows the vocabulary and tone before the model starts.
Task (काम).
एक प्रॉम्प्ट में एक ही काम रखिए। Two tasks in one prompt usually means one of them gets done badly.
Input (जानकारी).
जो डेटा चाहिए, वह प्रॉम्प्ट में दीजिए। The model cannot see your CRM. If the account status matters, put the account status in the prompt.
Output format (उत्तर का प्रारूप).
उत्तर किस रूप में चाहिए, यह लिखिए। Say "answer in two sentences" or "return a list of three options" and you will get that shape back.
इसके बाद एक पाँचवाँ कदम है जिसे लोग छोड़ देते हैं। There is a fifth step people skip: state what the model should do when it does not know. "If the account number is missing, ask for it instead of guessing" prevents a category of confident wrong answers.
### Hindi prompt examples you can reuse
नीचे कुछ उदाहरण हैं। हर उदाहरण में पहले कमज़ोर प्रॉम्प्ट है, फिर बेहतर प्रॉम्प्ट।
#### उदाहरण 1: ग्राहक को जवाब लिखना
कमज़ोर प्रॉम्प्ट: "ग्राहक को जवाब लिखो।"
बेहतर प्रॉम्प्ट: "आप एक बैंक के कस्टमर सपोर्ट एजेंट हैं। ग्राहक ने अपने खाते से कटे हुए शुल्क के बारे में शिकायत की है। शिकायत का विवरण नीचे दिया गया है। तीन वाक्यों में विनम्र हिंदी में जवाब लिखिए, जिसमें शुल्क का कारण और अगला कदम दोनों हों। अगर विवरण में शुल्क की तारीख नहीं है, तो जवाब देने के बजाय तारीख पूछिए।"
#### उदाहरण 2: कॉल का सारांश
कमज़ोर प्रॉम्प्ट: "इस कॉल का सारांश दो।"
बेहतर प्रॉम्प्ट: "नीचे एक ग्राहक कॉल का ट्रांसक्रिप्ट है। इसका सारांश चार बिंदुओं में दीजिए: ग्राहक की समस्या, एजेंट ने क्या किया, समस्या हल हुई या नहीं, और अगला कदम क्या है। हर बिंदु एक वाक्य का हो।"
#### उदाहरण 3: जानकारी निकालना
कमज़ोर प्रॉम्प्ट: "इसमें से ज़रूरी जानकारी निकालो।"
बेहतर प्रॉम्प्ट: "नीचे दिए गए ट्रांसक्रिप्ट से सिर्फ ये चार चीज़ें निकालिए: पॉलिसी नंबर, दावे की राशि, घटना की तारीख, और ग्राहक का शहर। हर चीज़ को अलग पंक्ति में लिखिए। जो जानकारी ट्रांसक्रिप्ट में नहीं है, उसके सामने ‘उपलब्ध नहीं’ लिखिए।"
ध्यान दीजिए कि तीनों बेहतर प्रॉम्प्ट में भूमिका, काम, जानकारी और प्रारूप चारों मौजूद हैं। Notice that each stronger version names the role, the task, the input and the output shape, and says what to do with missing data.
### Where prompting fits in a voice AI deployment
टेक्स्ट चैट में प्रॉम्प्ट लिखना आसान है। वॉइस में यह मुश्किल हो जाता है। Writing prompts for a chat window is forgiving. Writing them for a live phone call is not, for three reasons.
First, the input is a transcript, and transcripts contain recognition errors. A prompt that assumes clean text will break on a misheard account number. Second, the caller interrupts, so the model sees partial sentences. Third, latency is visible: a caller notices a two-second pause in a way a chat user does not, so prompts have to be short enough to process quickly.
इसीलिए वॉइस एजेंट के लिए प्रॉम्प्ट छोटे, स्पष्ट और गलती सहने वाले होने चाहिए। In a production voice stack the prompt sits between speech recognition and speech synthesis. Gnani AI runs
Prisma v2.5
for speech to text and
Timbre v2.5
for the reply, with the reasoning layer in between. The published
model pages
carry the current specifications, and the
documentation
covers how prompts are configured against them.
Code-switching deserves a line of its own. भारतीय ग्राहक अक्सर एक ही वाक्य में हिंदी और अंग्रेज़ी मिलाते हैं। If your callers do that, the prompt has to tolerate it, and so does the speech recognition underneath. Gnani AI reports 96 percent code-switch accuracy on Prisma v2.5 across mixes including Hinglish. That is a vendor-stated figure measured on Gnani AI traffic, so test it on your own recordings.
### Common mistakes
बहुत लंबा प्रॉम्प्ट।
A long prompt is not a precise prompt. Extra sentences add ways to be misread.
एक प्रॉम्प्ट में कई काम।
Split them into separate prompts, because a prompt carrying two jobs usually does one of them badly.
उदाहरण न देना।
दो अच्छे उदाहरण अक्सर दस निर्देशों से बेहतर काम करते हैं।
Testing on one input.
एक इनपुट पर सही उत्तर का मतलब यह नहीं कि प्रॉम्प्ट तैयार है। Run it against twenty real cases before you trust it.
ग्राहक की निजी जानकारी प्रॉम्प्ट में डालना।
Account numbers, Aadhaar, PAN and health details in a prompt are personal data under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, and they travel wherever the prompt travels. Redact before you send, and confirm the handling with your legal and compliance team.
### Why prompt meaning in Hindi matters for Indian businesses
भारत में अधिकतर ग्राहक बातचीत अंग्रेज़ी में नहीं होती। Most customer conversations in India do not happen in English, and a team that can only write prompts in English will write prompts that do not match the language their customers actually use. Understanding prompt meaning in Hindi is the first step toward writing instructions that produce usable Hindi output rather than translated English output, and the difference is audible on a phone call.
अगर आप वॉइस एजेंट बना रहे हैं, तो
Gnani AI के समाधान
देखिए, या
डेमो बुक कीजिए
। For related reading, see the explainer on
automation meaning in Hindi
and the
Gnani AI blog
.
### Frequently Asked Questions
What is the prompt meaning in Hindi?
प्रॉम्प्ट का मतलब है वह निर्देश जो आप AI मॉडल को देते हैं। A prompt is the instruction you give an AI model in plain language. मॉडल उसी निर्देश के आधार पर उत्तर देता है, इसलिए निर्देश जितना स्पष्ट होगा, उत्तर उतना बेहतर होगा।
प्रॉम्प्ट और प्रॉम्प्ट इंजीनियरिंग में क्या अंतर है?
प्रॉम्प्ट वह टेक्स्ट है जो आप लिखते हैं। प्रॉम्प्ट इंजीनियरिंग उस टेक्स्ट को बार-बार सुधारने और परखने की प्रक्रिया है ताकि हर बार भरोसेमंद उत्तर मिले। व्यावसायिक उपयोग में दूसरी चीज़ ज़्यादा मायने रखती है।
अच्छा प्रॉम्प्ट कैसे लिखें, उदाहरण सहित?
चार हिस्से रखिए: भूमिका, काम, जानकारी और उत्तर का प्रारूप। उदाहरण के लिए "ग्राहक को जवाब लिखो" कमज़ोर है, जबकि "आप एक बैंक के सपोर्ट एजेंट हैं, नीचे दी गई शिकायत का जवाब तीन वाक्यों में विनम्र हिंदी में लिखिए" स्पष्ट है क्योंकि इसमें चारों हिस्से मौजूद हैं।
क्या AI को हिंदी में प्रॉम्प्ट दिया जा सकता है?
हाँ। आधुनिक मॉडल हिंदी में लिखे प्रॉम्प्ट समझते हैं, और हिंदी उत्तर चाहिए तो हिंदी में प्रॉम्प्ट देना अक्सर बेहतर काम करता है। मिश्रित भाषा वाले प्रॉम्प्ट भी काम करते हैं, लेकिन उन्हें अपने असली डेटा पर परखना ज़रूरी है।
Do longer prompts give better results?
No. Length and precision are different things. A long prompt adds more sentences that can be misread and more instructions that can conflict. Say the role, the task, the input and the output format, say what to do when information is missing, and stop.
क्या प्रॉम्प्ट में ग्राहक की निजी जानकारी डालनी चाहिए?
नहीं, बिना ज़रूरत नहीं। खाता संख्या, आधार, पैन और स्वास्थ्य से जुड़ी जानकारी डिजिटल पर्सनल डेटा प्रोटेक्शन अधिनियम के तहत व्यक्तिगत डेटा है। भेजने से पहले उसे हटाइए या छिपाइए, और अपनी लीगल तथा कंप्लायंस टीम से पुष्टि कीजिए।

### Vector search, and why retrieval decides whether your AI answers are right
TL;DR:
Vector search finds information by meaning rather than by matching words. Text is converted into numerical embeddings, and the system returns the passages whose embeddings sit closest to the query's. In a retrieval-augmented generation pipeline, vector search is the step that decides which source passages the language model is allowed to answer from, which makes it the main lever on accuracy. A query for "card declined overseas" returns the international transaction policy even though the document never uses the word "declined".
Keyword search fails on the way people actually ask questions. A customer says their card stopped working abroad; the policy document says "cross-border authorisation limits". No shared keywords, no match, and an agent or an AI answers from nothing. Vector search closes that gap, and this guide covers how it works, where it breaks, and what an enterprise implementation has to get right.
### What vector search actually does
#### Embeddings and distance
An embedding model converts a piece of text into a list of numbers, typically several hundred to a few thousand of them. Passages with similar meaning land near each other in that numerical space. At query time the same model embeds the question, and the system returns the stored passages whose vectors sit closest, measured by cosine similarity or dot product.
Nothing here understands the text. The model has learned, from a very large amount of training data, which pieces of language tend to appear in similar contexts. That is enough to match a customer's phrasing to a policy writer's phrasing, and it is the whole trick.
#### The retrieval loop
A working pipeline runs four steps. Documents are chunked and embedded once, into an index. An incoming query is embedded with the same model. The index returns the top-k nearest chunks. Those chunks go to the language model as context, with an instruction to answer only from them and to cite which chunk it used.
That last instruction is what separates a grounded answer from a plausible invention. If the retrieved chunks do not contain the answer, a well-configured system says so rather than filling the gap.
ENTERPRISE VOICE AI
See Gnani AI's Voice AI Agent in action
200+ Enterprises · 30M daily calls · 10 Indic languages
Book A Demo
### Keyword, vector and hybrid search compared
Teams usually arrive expecting to replace keyword search. The better answer is usually to run both. Keyword search is exact and predictable, and it still wins on identifiers, product codes and policy numbers, which are precisely the strings a semantic model is worst at.
Keyword, vector and hybrid retrieval
Dimension
Keyword search (BM25)
Vector search
Hybrid with reranking
Matches on
Literal terms and their statistics
Semantic proximity of embeddings
Both, merged and re-scored

Often misses entirely

Strong and exact

Rare in-house jargon
Works if the term is indexed
Depends on the embedding model's training

Indexing cost
Low

Query latency
Lowest

Explaining a result

Required for the vector half

Natural-language FAQ over clean content
Mixed enterprise corpora, the common default
Hybrid retrieval runs both and merges the result lists, usually with reciprocal rank fusion, then reranks the merged set with a cross-encoder. It costs more per query and it is close to the default for production enterprise search, because the failure modes of the two methods are different and they cover for each other.
### Chunking, the step most implementations get wrong
Chunk size decides retrieval quality more than the embedding model does, and it gets far less attention. Chunks that are too small lose the context that made the passage meaningful. Chunks that are too large dilute the embedding, so a document about twelve topics matches weakly on all of them.
Three practices hold up in production. Split on semantic boundaries, meaning sections and subsections, rather than on a fixed character count. Overlap adjacent chunks slightly so an answer that straddles a boundary is not cut in half. Attach metadata to every chunk, including source document, section, effective date and the access group allowed to see it.
That metadata is not administrative overhead. It is how you filter retrieval by permission, so a contact centre agent handling retail customers never receives a chunk from a private banking policy, and how you exclude a superseded document the day it is superseded.
### Where vector search meets voice
Retrieval inside a live phone call is a harder problem than retrieval in a chat window, because the budget is a few hundred milliseconds and the input arrives as audio rather than clean text. Three things have to hold.
Transcription has to be accurate enough that the embedding is of what the caller said. Gnani AI's
Prisma v2.5 speech to text model
is trained on 14M+ hours of telephonic audio, and Gnani AI reports under 4% word error rate on Indian speech, 96% code-switching accuracy and sub-200ms streaming latency. A transcription error at the start of the pipeline cannot be recovered by better retrieval downstream.
Retrieval has to finish inside the conversational gap. Gnani AI reports under 800ms end-to-end response latency for
Gnani Agents
in live conversations, which is the budget the whole loop including retrieval has to fit inside.
The answer has to be spoken back without an awkward pause. Gnani AI's
Timbre v2.5 text to speech model
, in Beta, covers 10+ Indic languages, and Gnani AI reports sub-100ms time to first audio and a mean opinion score of 4.23 on 8kHz telephony.
The same retrieval layer also serves the human side of the floor.
Gnani Assist
surfaces the policy passage to a live agent mid-call, which is the lower-risk way to deploy retrieval first, because a person checks every answer before the customer hears it.
### Grounding, and what vector search does not fix
Retrieval reduces invention by restricting the model to supplied passages. It does not eliminate it. Three failure modes survive.
Retrieval miss.
The right passage exists but ranks below the cutoff, so the model answers from adjacent material that looks relevant. Reranking and hybrid retrieval reduce this.
Conflicting sources.
Two versions of a policy are both indexed and both retrieved. The model picks one, usually without flagging the conflict. Effective-date metadata and an index hygiene process are the fix, not a better prompt.
Confident synthesis.
The model stitches two partially relevant chunks into an answer neither supports. Requiring per-sentence citation makes this visible to a reviewer.
Measure retrieval separately from generation. Track whether the correct chunk appeared in the top-k at all, because a generation problem and a retrieval problem look identical from the outside and have completely different fixes.
### Running it where the data has to stay
Indexing enterprise documents means creating a second copy of your knowledge base, embeddings included. For a bank or an insurer, that copy inherits every restriction the originals carry. Embeddings are derived from the source text and should be treated as sensitive, not as anonymised numbers.
Gnani AI's
Artha sovereign stack
runs the reasoning and speech layers on infrastructure the customer controls, including on-premise and air-gapped, which keeps the index and the model inside the same boundary. The underlying open-weight model,
Evon v3.3
, has 30B total parameters with roughly 3.5B active per token, a 128K context window and Apache 2.0 weights, and Gnani AI reports single-node inference.
Indian customer data falls under the DPDP Act. Banking retrieval brings RBI expectations, insurance brings IRDAI, and US healthcare brings HIPAA. Gnani AI states it is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and ISO 27001 certified, and HIPAA, GDPR and PCI-DSS compliant. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
### A sequence that works
Pick one document set and one audience.
One product's policy documents, one agent queue. Breadth is what kills these projects.
Clean before you index.
Remove superseded versions. An index built on a messy share drive produces confidently wrong answers.
Chunk semantically, attach metadata.
Source, section, effective date, access group, on every chunk.
Start hybrid.
Keyword plus vector with reranking, rather than vector alone, then simplify if the data says you can.
Build the eval set first.
Fifty real questions with known correct sources, written before you tune anything.
Deploy to agents before customers.
Retrieval behind a human is the cheapest place to find out what your index gets wrong.
Keep the feedback loop.
Log every retrieval, every answer, and every agent correction, and re-run the eval set when the index changes.
### Frequently asked questions
What is vector search?
Vector search finds information by meaning instead of by matching words. Text is converted into numerical embeddings, and the search returns the passages whose embeddings are mathematically closest to the query's. It retrieves the right document when the user's phrasing and the document's phrasing share no words.
What is the difference between vector search and keyword search?
Keyword search matches literal strings and is exact, fast and predictable, which makes it strong on identifiers, codes and policy numbers. Vector search matches meaning, which makes it strong on paraphrase, synonyms and natural phrasing. Most production enterprise systems run both and merge the results, because they fail in different ways.
How does vector search work in RAG?
In retrieval-augmented generation, vector search is the retrieval step. Documents are chunked and embedded into an index ahead of time. At query time the question is embedded, the nearest chunks are returned, and those chunks are passed to the language model as the only material it is permitted to answer from. Retrieval quality therefore sets the ceiling on answer quality.
Does vector search stop AI from making things up?
It reduces invention substantially but does not remove it. The model can still answer from a near-miss passage when the correct one ranks below the cutoff, pick one of two conflicting documents without flagging the conflict, or synthesise across partially relevant chunks. Per-sentence citation and separate measurement of retrieval accuracy are what make these failures visible.
What chunk size should I use for vector search?
Split on semantic boundaries such as sections and subsections rather than on a fixed character count, and overlap adjacent chunks slightly so answers that straddle a boundary survive. Chunks that are too small lose context; chunks that are too large dilute the embedding so the passage matches weakly on everything it covers.
Can vector search run inside a live phone call?
Yes, within a tight latency budget. Gnani AI reports under 800ms end-to-end response latency for Gnani Agents in live conversations, which the transcription, retrieval, reasoning and speech synthesis steps all have to share. Transcription accuracy matters most, because an error there cannot be recovered later in the pipeline.

### 6 Tips To Simplify Your Real Estate Lead Generation Strategies
There is no magic bullet in the real estate business. Otherwise, every agent would’ve been a multi-millionaire. Real estate is a heavily competitive market where everyone is using the same type of marketing strategies to generate leads for them. Everyone is bidding for the same keywords and talking to the same database of people. Before we dive deep into the strategies to generate real estate leads, let's discuss briefly about what it means by lead generation for real estate and how it works?Lead generation in real estate is a marketing process that aims at encouraging interest in a particular product to generate a sales channel and then a lead into a potential prospect and eventually a client, then to close the sale. Getting the right agent to drive your real estate lead generation is, of course, the first step towards a sustainable business, but once you do that, your next set of challenges will be to ensure a steady flow of leads. Real estate agents need to be highly efficient and must look for ways to improve in terms of generating leads. In real estate business, lead comes generally through ads, trade shows, third parties and other marketing efforts. In this article, we talk about how you can improve your real estate lead generation in 2022. Here’s what you can do:
### Real estate lead generation ideas in 2022
In this new normal period, the known channels of marketing have changed a lot and many new marketing channels have opened for businesses. Here are the important areas you should cover to generate leads
#### Testimonials & Referrals
This is 'gold' to generate leads. Nothing works like a referral and a testimonial to generate real estate leads. Trust has always been a key criterion for clients when selecting who to do a business deal with, specially in real estate. Not only does this save time, but it also is a warmer lead to engage with clients. One way to get leads for real estate business is to create partnerships with local businesses that can share referrals in return for business opportunities for them with your clients.
#### New age media
Social media is obvious, but what do you do in it? New-age content should be your go-to strategy for real estate lead generation. For example – reels, piggybacking on relevant viral trends, virtual tours of properties. And then there are SEO, advertising, content marketing, etc. And once in a while, it’s always okay to inject a few old-style potential marketing styles to generate tactics like radio ads. Coming back to the point of which social media channels to choose – Facebook, Facebook Ads, Instagram, NextDoor, Quora, Snapchat, Tik Tok might be some of the first options to build an audience of buyers and sellers.
Facebook-
As we have shifted into the digital age, real estate agents are aware of new opportunities for generating leads through captivating marketing. Facebook ads are super effective to get in front of the ready -to-purchase audience. Facebook ads, facebook live chat, leads forms are popular ways for generating leads for real estate through facebook. You can also add links to forms that would direct clients to your website.
#### Conversational AI
According to a Forrester report, 63% of customers return to a website with in-built live chat support, therefore, increasing leads. A conversational AI tool can be a blessing for realtors. A non-stop support system, it can take an unlimited number of calls, schedule meetings, capture contact details, return calls at the convenience of customers, answer FAQs, promote the right solutions, hand over a conversation to a human at the right time, and the latest advanced NLP, NLU engines are capable of providing empathetic customer support and keep clients engaged and thus get more leads.
#### Use CRM
Using Customer Relationship Management software will take your efficiency to the next level. There are plenty of options like AgileCRM, Wise Agent, Streak CRM, Zoho, Apptivo, etc., available out there to choose from based on your priorities and needs. These tools help organize and grow your leads. They can be used for better lead management, marketing, communications, and overall higher productivity. CRM tools help to get, manage and follow up with potential leads in one place.
#### Q&As
Platforms like Quora are a great way for you to generate leads. By answering questions that potential clients are asking, you help them directly and, more importantly, when they are asking for it. This will help you to earn their trust. Once that happens, you will create an inflow of leads to be nurtured for business opportunities and use them to get the best leads for your real estate business.
#### Hustle
Not for the impatient; these are things that take your time and effort but no money, like an open house or networking, or cold calling. The real estate business is demanding, and it is wise not to leave any channel for lead generation. Hustling helps you stay relevant, resourceful, and known in the market. It creates a name for you and picks up your clients instantly rather than waiting for them to approach you. Though there are chances to experience hang-ups, you need to build a thick skin to become a top real estate agent.
#### Bonus Points
While we are on the topic, here are a few Bonus pointers:
Follow up –
In the last two years, people have changed priorities and are demanding a very different set of requirements when it comes to real estate. Initiating conversations that are left mid-way with clients is a no-no. Following up without disturbing potential leads and with a clear-cut strategy is a must.
Millennial strategy –
Always have a special strategy for those who comprise the highest section of customers. In this case, it is the millennials. The National Association of Realtors reported as early as 2017 that 99 percent of millennials used technology at some stage of their home buying process. Right from the way they use technology to how they are more open to buying/selling houses to the latest marketing trends of needing more space to work from home, there has to be a clear, well-thought real estate lead generation strategy for them.
### In Summary:
It can get a little difficult when choosing which ideas to adopt. Which ones should you select? Which looks worthy of investing your limited time and budget? Start smart.You may have a limited budget, time, or a team. Start smart by first identifying and laying out your priorities. Remember:
Be where your customers are (online and in-person).Use tools that help you be more efficient and productiveBe helpful and keep your clients’ needs in mindBe consistent in your real estate leads generation efforts.

How is AI used in real estate?
AI is used in real estate to help you find the best home. It can look at the data of the homes you’re interested in and help you find more matches with the features you want. It can sift through millions of homes and narrow them down to the ones that fit your criteria.
What are the 4 stages of an AI workflow?
After a few starter projects, engineers quickly learn that AI is not just modeling but rather a complete set of steps that includes data preparation, modeling, simulation and test, and deployment.
What is an algorithm in real estate?
Real estate companies are increasingly using artificial intelligence in every aspect of buying, selling, and home financing. Algorithms can now go through millions of documents in seconds, looking through property values, debt levels, home renovations, and even some of a homeowner’s personal information.

### Real time agent assist in one paragraph
Real time agent assist is software that listens to a live call, retrieves the answer the agent needs while the customer is still speaking, and prompts the next step before the conversation goes wrong. It differs from post-call quality assurance in timing: QA tells a supervisor what went wrong yesterday, real time agent assist corrects it inside the call. The category covers four jobs: live knowledge retrieval, guided workflows, compliance prompting, and after-call admin.

Gnani Assist
delivers an 18% improvement in agent efficiency, 70% faster time to proficiency, a 30% increase in CSAT, and over 90% reduction in after-call admin.
### Why post-call coaching arrives too late
A traditional contact centre finds its problems in the rear-view mirror. A supervisor samples a handful of calls, scores them against a rubric, and books a coaching session for the following week. By then the agent has taken another two hundred calls, and whatever went wrong in the sampled one has been repeated across most of them.
The sampling rate is the deeper problem. Manual QA covers a fraction of a percent of interactions in most centres, so the score a supervisor sees is an estimate drawn from a tiny slice.
Gnani Analytics
works across the full corpus rather than a sample, which is what makes trend detection reliable enough to act on.
Real time agent assist attacks the same problem from the other end. Instead of improving the review, it removes the need for one on routine failures. If the agent is about to quote a policy that expired last quarter, the correction appears on screen while the sentence is still forming.

### What a real time agent assist system actually holds
The term covers a range of products, and the range matters when you write an RFP. Four capabilities separate a genuine real time agent assist deployment from a glorified knowledge base search box.
#### Live knowledge and policy retrieval
The system transcribes the call as it happens, identifies the question being asked, and surfaces the relevant policy or product answer without the agent typing a query. Transcription quality sets the ceiling here. On Indian telephony that means handling 8kHz audio and code-mixed speech, which is what
Gnani Prisma v2.5
is trained for across more than 14 million hours of real call audio.
#### Guided workflows and compliance prompts
Regulated conversations have mandatory steps. A collections call carries disclosure requirements, a KYC call carries verification steps, and missing one creates an audit finding rather than a bad customer experience. Guided workflows present those steps in order and record that they happened.
#### Next best action
Once the system knows the account context and the customer's stated problem, it can propose the specific action that resolves it. This is where agent assist stops being a reference tool and starts changing outcomes.
#### After-call admin
Summaries, disposition codes and CRM updates consume a large share of handle time and produce most of the data quality problems downstream. Automating them is the least glamorous capability in the category and usually the fastest payback.
### Real time agent assist in a regulated contact centre
Take a banking support queue. A customer calls about a transaction they do not recognise. The agent needs the transaction history, the fraud policy for that product, the verification questions appropriate to the customer's tier, and compliance-approved language for what happens next.
Without assist, the agent holds the customer while searching three systems. With assist, the history and the policy appear as the customer describes the problem, and the verification path is prompted in the right order. Where voice authentication is deployed through
Gnani Biometrics
, the identity check itself completes in under five seconds without security questions, which
reports removes around 40 seconds from average handle time.
Regulated deployments carry obligations beyond the product. Indian customer data falls under the DPDP Act, BFSI deployments fall under RBI guidelines, and any voice agent in the flow must disclose that it is AI. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.

### What to measure before and after
Most agent assist business cases fail because nobody captured the baseline. Pull these numbers for the four weeks before the pilot, and pull them the same way afterwards.
Average handle time
, split between talk time and after-call work, because assist moves them independently.
First call resolution
, measured by repeat contact within a defined window rather than by agent self-report.
Time to proficiency
for new hires, measured as weeks until they hit the team median on quality score.
Compliance adherence
, measured as the share of calls where every mandatory step was completed.
CSAT
, segmented by call type, since assist helps most on complex calls and barely moves simple ones.
Split the pilot group and the control group by agent rather than by queue. Queue-level splits get contaminated by routing changes, and you will spend the readout arguing about attribution instead of deciding whether to expand.
### How to pilot real time agent assist
Start with one call type that is high volume and well defined. Collections, order status and appointment rescheduling all work, because the correct answer is knowable and the failure modes are visible in the data.
Check integration early. Assist is only as good as the systems it can read, so confirm that your CRM, your knowledge base and your telephony platform all expose what the product needs.

### Where real time agent assist fits next
Real time agent assist is the cheapest place to start if your contact centre already has humans doing work that a model could prepare for them. It does not require you to automate a customer-facing conversation, which makes it an easier internal sell than a fully autonomous voice agent, and it produces the transcript corpus that later automation depends on. ### Frequently asked questions
What is real time agent assist?
Real time agent assist is software that listens to a live customer conversation and gives the human agent answers, next steps and compliance prompts while the call is still in progress. It sits alongside the agent rather than replacing them, and it covers knowledge retrieval, guided workflows, next best action and automated after-call admin.
How is agent assist different from a chatbot?
A chatbot talks to the customer. Agent assist talks to the agent, and the customer never sees it. The two are often deployed together, with autonomous agents handling routine contacts and assist supporting the human on everything that escalates.
Does real time agent assist reduce average handle time?
It reduces after-call work first and talk time second. Summaries, disposition coding and CRM updates automate cleanly, and Gnani AI reports over 90% reduction in after-call admin for Gnani Assist. Talk time moves more slowly, because it depends on how quickly the agent trusts the suggestions.

Have you ever wondered how companies like Uber adjust prices instantly, or how banks flag fraudulent transactions the moment they occur? That’s the power of
real time analytics
. It processes and analyzes live data as it’s generated, allowing organizations to respond instantly instead of waiting for end-of-day reports.
In this blog, you’ll learn
what real time analytics is
, why it’s becoming the backbone of modern enterprises, its
key components
,
real-world applications
, and
how it differs from traditional analytics
. By the end, you’ll understand how to use real time insights to gain competitive advantage and improve business outcomes.
### What Is Real Time Analytics?
Real time analytics
refers to the continuous processing and interpretation of data as it’s created, enabling immediate action. Unlike batch processing—which collects data and analyzes it later—real time systems analyze information within milliseconds.
This approach uses
streaming technologies
like Apache Kafka, Flink, or Spark Streaming to handle high-volume data from sensors, apps, or APIs. For instance, when a user completes a transaction, real time analytics can instantly detect anomalies, trigger alerts, or update dashboards.
According to
IDC
, by 2026, over
65% of Global 2000 firms
will rely on real time analytics to enhance operational efficiency and customer experience. This shows its growing role in a data-driven economy where time equals competitive edge.
### Why Real Time Analytics Matters Today
Speed isn’t just a metric—it’s a differentiator. Modern businesses operate in environments where
milliseconds determine outcomes
. Real time analytics bridges the gap between data availability and decision-making.
Here’s why it’s crucial:
Faster Decision-Making:
Companies can respond to changes instantly, improving agility.
Enhanced Customer Experience:
Real time insights help personalize recommendations and detect issues early.
Operational Efficiency:
Automated alerts and data-driven workflows reduce manual effort.
Competitive Advantage:
Immediate insights allow proactive actions before competitors react.
A practical analogy is like driving with GPS navigation. Batch analytics is like checking your route after the trip;
updates you continuously, helping you avoid traffic or adjust to changes dynamically.
### The Critical Role of Agentic AI in Real-Time Decision-Making
Agentic AI represents the next evolution beyond traditional artificial intelligence. Agentic AI refers to AI systems capable of acting autonomously, adapting in real-time, and solving complex multi-step problems based on context and objectives. While generative AI creates content based on prompts, Agentic AI takes initiative, makes decisions, and executes actions without constant human oversight.
The convergence of real-time analytics and Agentic AI creates powerful autonomous systems. Agentic analytics delivers instant insights by continuously monitoring data streams, making informed decisions in real-time as new information becomes available. This combination enables businesses to not just see what's happening but automatically respond with appropriate actions.
Consider a practical banking scenario. When a potentially fraudulent transaction occurs, real-time analytics engines immediately flag the anomaly. Agentic AI then autonomously decides whether to block the transaction, request additional authentication, or allow it to proceed based on risk assessment, all within milliseconds. JPMorgan uses agentic AI to detect fraudulent credit card transactions in real-time, preventing billions in potential losses annually.
The forecast for Agentic AI adoption is compelling. According to a Deloitte report, 25 percent of enterprises currently using generative AI will launch agentic AI pilots in 2025, with adoption doubling to 50 percent by 2027. Furthermore, Gartner forecasts that by 2029, agentic AI will autonomously resolve 80 percent of common customer service issues without human intervention, resulting in a 30 percent reduction in operational costs.
### Core Components Powering Real-Time Analytics Engines
Real-time analytics engines consist of several integrated components working in harmony to process live data streams effectively. Understanding these building blocks helps businesses appreciate how instant insights become possible.
#### Data Ingestion and Stream Processing
The foundation begins with data ingestion, where information flows continuously from multiple sources like customer interactions, IoT sensors, transaction systems, and communication channels. Real-time analytics platforms use distributed processing systems to handle large volumes of data with low latency, ensuring analysis happens almost instantaneously.
Stream processing frameworks like Apache Kafka enable the continuous flow of data at high speeds. These systems must handle varying data velocities and volumes without bottlenecks. The challenge isn't just collecting data but organizing it for immediate analysis while maintaining quality and consistency.
#### Data Transformation and Enrichment
Raw data rarely arrives in analysis-ready format. Data undergoes normalization to ensure consistency and enrichment with additional context, such as translating IP addresses into geographical locations or identifying device types from user agent strings. This transformation happens in real-time, adding meaningful context that makes insights actionable.
For Gnani.ai's voice AI solutions, this might involve converting speech to text, identifying customer sentiment, detecting intent, and enriching the conversation with historical customer data, all while the interaction is still happening. The enriched data then feeds into analytics engines for pattern detection.
#### Analytics and Pattern Recognition
The analytics layer applies complex computations to identify patterns, correlations, and anomalies in streaming data. Machine learning algorithms continuously analyze behaviors to detect deviations from normal patterns. Real-time analytics processes data as it's collected, providing immediate insights, enabling predictive capabilities that anticipate customer needs.
In fraud detection scenarios, analytics engines compare each transaction against millions of historical patterns to calculate risk scores within milliseconds. Advanced systems evaluate transaction risk in under 200 milliseconds, enabling real-time fraud detection without delaying legitimate payments. This split-second analysis protects customers while maintaining seamless experiences.
#### Visualization and Action Triggers
Insights mean nothing without effective communication to stakeholders. Real-time dashboards provide intuitive visualizations that make complex data understandable at a glance. More importantly, real-time analytics engines trigger automated actions based on predefined rules or AI-driven decisions.
When Gnani.ai's analytics engines detect a customer showing signs of frustration during a voice interaction, the system can automatically escalate the call to a human agent, offer a discount, or adjust the conversation strategy, all without manual intervention. These automated responses happen faster than any human could react, ensuring customers receive immediate assistance when needed.
### Real-World Applications Across Industries
Real-time analytics engines deliver transformative value across multiple sectors, with particularly strong applications in banking, healthcare, and insurance.
#### Banking and Financial Services Applications
The banking sector faces constant pressure to prevent fraud while delivering frictionless customer experiences. Real-time analytics engines enable financial institutions to protect customers without creating unnecessary friction. Consumer fraud losses increased by 25% year over year, totaling more than $12.5 billion in 2024, making advanced fraud detection capabilities essential.
For Gnani.ai customers in banking, real-time analytics power multiple use cases. During loan qualification calls, the system analyzes customer responses, cross-references financial data, and assesses creditworthiness in real-time, enabling instant preliminary decisions. In collections scenarios, analytics engines detect payment propensity and emotional state, allowing agents to adjust negotiation strategies dynamically.
Pre-due and post-due collections benefit significantly from real-time customer insights. The system identifies the optimal time to contact customers, predicts which communication channels they prefer, and determines the most effective messaging approach based on historical patterns and current behavior. This precision dramatically improves collection rates while maintaining positive customer relationships.
#### Healthcare and Insurance Solutions
Healthcare providers and insurance companies deal with sensitive information requiring both security and speed. Real-time analytics enables better patient care and streamlined claims processing while detecting fraudulent activities.
In healthcare applications, Gnani.ai's real-time analytics engines assist patients in finding network hospitals and medical services instantly. During pre-visit confirmation calls, the system verifies appointments, checks insurance eligibility, and answers common questions without human intervention. For insurance companies, claims processing benefits from instant fraud detection that identifies suspicious patterns before payouts occur.
The insurance sector has seen remarkable results from real-time analytics implementation. Smart home and real-time monitoring technologies helped cut fraudulent home insurance claims by 14% in 2025, demonstrating measurable fraud prevention benefits. Additionally, blockchain-based authentication and real-time analytics reduced cyber and identity theft-related insurance fraud by about 11% in 2025.
Service booking, remainder calls for policy renewals, and customer feedback collection all leverage real-time analytics to optimize timing and messaging. When customers call with questions about their coverage, Gnani.ai's voice AI provides instant answers by accessing policy details in real-time, eliminating hold times and improving satisfaction.
#### Customer Experience Enhancement
Across all industries, real-time analytics dramatically improves customer experiences by enabling personalization at scale. By leveraging real-time data and insights, businesses can deliver hyper-personalized interactions that resonate with customers and create more engaging experiences.
Welcome calling campaigns use real-time sentiment analysis to adjust conversation tone based on customer reactions. If analytics detect confusion or frustration, the system adapts explanations, offers additional help, or seamlessly transfers to a human agent. This adaptive approach creates natural, empathetic interactions that customers appreciate.
Feedback and survey systems benefit from real-time analytics by asking contextual questions based on recent interactions. Rather than generic surveys, customers receive targeted questions about specific touchpoints they experienced, improving response rates and data quality. The insights gathered feed back into analytics engines, creating continuous improvement loops.
### Conclusion
Real-time analytics engines have evolved from a competitive advantage to a business necessity. By processing live data streams and delivering instant insights, these systems enable organizations to make better decisions faster, improve customer experiences dramatically, and operate more efficiently than ever before.
Gnani.ai's real-time analytics engines, powered by Agentic AI, represent the cutting edge of this transformation. From banking applications like loan qualification and collections to healthcare use cases like appointment confirmations and claims processing, real-time insights drive measurable business outcomes across industries.
The combination of speed, accuracy, and autonomous decision-making creates experiences customers expect and business results executives demand. While implementation challenges exist, the benefits far outweigh the costs, and purpose-built platforms significantly reduce complexity.
As we look toward a future where AI agents work alongside humans, real-time analytics will remain the foundation enabling these systems to act intelligently and autonomously. The organizations investing in these capabilities today are positioning themselves to lead their industries tomorrow.
Get in touch with us to know more about how Gnani.ai's real-time analytics engines can transform your customer interactions and business operations.
### Frequently Asked Questions
What is the difference between real-time analytics and batch processing?
Real-time analytics processes data immediately as it's generated, providing insights within milliseconds to seconds. Batch processing collects data over periods like hours or days before analyzing it, resulting in delayed insights. Real-time systems enable immediate action while batch processing provides retrospective analysis. Organizations use both approaches for different purposes, with real-time analytics handling time-sensitive decisions and batch processing supporting comprehensive historical analysis.
How does Agentic AI enhance real-time analytics capabilities?
Agentic AI adds autonomous decision-making capabilities to real-time analytics. While analytics engines identify patterns and generate insights, Agentic AI interprets those insights and takes appropriate actions without human intervention. This combination enables systems to not just detect fraud but block transactions, not just identify frustrated customers but adjust conversation strategies, creating truly autonomous operational capabilities that respond intelligently to changing conditions.
What industries benefit most from real-time analytics engines?
Banking and financial services see significant fraud prevention and customer experience improvements. Healthcare providers use real-time analytics for patient monitoring and service coordination. Insurance companies benefit from instant claims processing and fraud detection. Retail organizations leverage real-time insights for personalization and inventory management. Essentially, any industry where customer experiences, operational efficiency, or risk management depend on timely information can benefit substantially from real-time analytics.
How quickly can real-time analytics systems process data?
Modern real-time analytics engines process data within milliseconds to seconds. Fraud detection systems evaluate transactions in under 200 milliseconds, enabling instant approvals or blocks. Voice AI systems like Gnani.ai analyze sentiment and intent during conversations with latency measured in milliseconds, ensuring natural interactions. The specific speed depends on data volume, processing complexity, and infrastructure capabilities, but sub-second processing is standard for most applications.
What are the main challenges in implementing real-time analytics?
Key challenges include integrating data from multiple sources with varying formats and speeds, ensuring consistent data quality across streams, building infrastructure capable of handling high-velocity data, balancing processing speed with accuracy, maintaining compliance with privacy regulations, and managing implementation costs. Organizations often partner with specialized platforms like Gnani.ai to address these challenges through proven solutions rather than building everything from scratch.
How does real-time analytics improve customer experience?
Real-time analytics enables personalization at scale by understanding customer needs as they emerge. Systems can adapt conversations based on detected sentiment, provide context-aware responses using complete customer history, resolve issues faster through immediate problem identification, prevent fraud without creating friction for legitimate customers, and deliver proactive service by anticipating needs before customers articulate them. These capabilities create seamless, intuitive experiences that build customer loyalty.
What role does machine learning play in real-time analytics?
Machine learning algorithms analyze patterns across millions of data points to identify anomalies, predict outcomes, and recommend actions. These models continuously learn from new data, improving accuracy over time without manual retraining. In fraud detection, machine learning adapts to evolving tactics fraudsters employ. In customer service, algorithms learn which resolution strategies work best for different situations. Machine learning transforms static analytics into adaptive systems that become more intelligent with every interaction.
