### What Is Debt Collection Software?
Debt collection software is the system a lender or recovery agency uses to manage delinquent accounts end to end: segmenting the portfolio, contacting borrowers across voice, WhatsApp, SMS and chat, capturing promises to pay, recording every interaction for audit, and routing the accounts that need a human negotiator to one.
The category has split in two. One half is the system of record that holds accounts, allocations and payment plans. The other half is the contact layer that actually reaches the borrower. The contact layer is where the economics of recovery are decided, because an account nobody reaches never pays, and it is the half that voice AI has changed.
A voice AI collections agent is software that holds the conversation itself. It calls the borrower, identifies itself as an AI assistant, confirms identity, states the outstanding amount, negotiates within pre-set limits, captures a promise to pay and logs the whole exchange. It is not a recorded message and it is not a menu tree.
### Why Is Debt Collection Software Changing in 2026?
It is changing because the constraint in recovery has always been contact capacity, and that constraint has moved. A collections team can only make so many calls in a shift, which forces agencies to work the high-balance accounts and leave the long tail of small balances largely untouched.
Three things shifted at once. Conversational models became good enough to negotiate rather than only to announce. Telephony-grade speech recognition in Indian languages became accurate enough to trust with account numbers and amounts. And regulators tightened the evidence requirements around collections conduct, which made exhaustive logging an advantage rather than an overhead.

### How Does Voice AI Compare to Diallers and IVR in Collections?
The three approaches differ most in what happens when the borrower says something unexpected. A predictive dialler connects a human who can respond. A rules-based IVR plays the next prompt regardless. A voice AI agent interprets the response and continues the conversation.

### What Should Debt Collection Software Actually Do?
It should reach the borrower in their own language, complete the routine conversation without a human, and leave an audit trail a regulator can read. Everything else is secondary to those three.

### How Does Voice AI Collections Stay Compliant?
Compliance in collections rests on three things: who you called, what was said, and whether you can prove it. Automated calling makes the first two easier to get wrong at scale and the third easier to get right.
The regimes that apply depend on where the borrower is and what the debt is:
Digital Personal Data Protection Act.
Call recordings, transcripts, call metadata and borrower identifiers are personal data under India's DPDP Act. Account numbers and payment history are sensitive by any reasonable reading.
Reserve Bank of India guidance.
Lenders and their recovery agents operate under RBI expectations covering collections conduct, permitted contact hours and borrower grievance handling.
TRAI regulation.
Outbound voice and SMS in India fall under TRAI rules on consent, commercial communication and DND registration. A collections call campaign is outbound telephony.
FDCPA and TCPA.
US borrowers bring the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act and the Telephone Consumer Protection Act into scope, including restrictions on contact frequency and timing.
AI disclosure.
The agent states that it is an AI assistant, in the script, in every language, at the start of the call. This is non-negotiable and it belongs in the prompt rather than in a policy document.
Where the data sits is a design decision rather than a contractual one. Gnani AI offers cloud, private cloud, on-premise and air-gapped deployment, and is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and ISO 27001 certified, and HIPAA, GDPR and PCI-DSS compliant. Voiceprints and speaker embeddings used for passive verification are biometric data and carry the highest sensitivity classification, so their enrolment and storage need their own review. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
### How Do You Measure Collections Performance After Deployment?
Measure the funnel, not the call count. Contact rate, right-party contact rate, promise-to-pay rate, promise kept rate and cost per rupee recovered describe the recovery process. Calls dialled describes effort.
Right-party contact rate
by language and by time slot, which usually exposes a language gap before anything else does.
Promise-to-pay conversion
, measured as promises captured divided by right-party contacts.
Promise kept rate
within the agreed window, which is the only number that correlates with cash.
Cost per rupee recovered
, segmented by bucket, so the long tail is costed honestly.
Compliance exception rate
from full-corpus monitoring, read as a trend rather than as individual incidents.
Escalation quality
, measured as the share of handoffs where the human collector had full context.
Choosing debt collection software in 2026 comes down to whether the contact layer can hold a real conversation in the borrower's language, settle within limits, and produce the evidence trail afterwards. For how this sits inside a wider banking deployment, see
agentic AI for banking
and the
Gnani AI model stack
, or
book a demo with Gnani AI
.
### Frequently Asked Questions
What is debt collection software?
Debt collection software is the system a lender or recovery agency uses to manage delinquent accounts end to end: segmenting the portfolio, contacting borrowers across voice, WhatsApp, SMS and chat, capturing promises to pay, recording every interaction for audit, and routing accounts that need a human negotiator to one.
How do voice AI agents differ from predictive diallers in collections?
A predictive dialler connects a human who can adapt to an unexpected reply. A voice AI agent interprets the reply itself and continues the conversation, at concurrent capacity a headcount-limited team cannot reach. The two are complementary: diallers suit hardship and settlement work, voice AI suits reminders and long-tail balances.
Can an AI agent negotiate a settlement?
Only inside a pre-approved band. A well-designed collections agent settles within defined limits and escalates anything outside them to a human negotiator with full context attached. It should never improvise a discount, and the limits belong in configuration rather than in the prompt.
Which regulations apply to AI-driven collections calls in India?
India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act covers borrower records, recordings and transcripts. RBI guidance covers collections conduct, contact hours and grievance handling for lenders and their recovery agents. TRAI rules cover outbound consent and DND. US borrowers add FDCPA and TCPA. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
Does the agent have to say it is an AI?
Yes. The agent discloses that it is an AI assistant at the start of every call, in every language, written into the script rather than left to a policy document. In collections this is both a disclosure obligation and a conduct expectation.
What should we measure after deploying collections automation?
Measure the recovery funnel rather than call volume. Track right-party contact rate by language and time slot, promise-to-pay conversion, promise kept rate within the agreed window, cost per rupee recovered by bucket, compliance exception rate from full-corpus monitoring, and escalation quality.

One of the most common reasons why customers jump ship to a competitor is because of shoddy service. If you can’t get it right, then no matter how good your product is in the market, things will come crashing down. Customer service is gauged on customer interactions.
### What is Customer Interaction?
They are moments where potential customers engage with your business. It could be noticing your ad on social media or interacting with an agent on your website’s live chat feature. If the prospect has bitter after-effects post the interaction with your brand, they might not come back at all.Let us look at six ways to improve customer interactions:
### Communicate Clearly
Customers want to know what exactly you offer. If your products have new features and there is any change in your billing structure, communicate the changes clearly to the users. Effective communication is all about being relevant, concise, and being to the point. No matter what it is, whether it is an Instagram story or a promotional email to your newsletter subscribers.Another important channel where prospects often communicate is with your customer service agents. Make sure that they use a natural and conversational tone, and mix it up with a friendly attitude.
### Personalize the Interactions
People want personalized experiences when they go shopping.
According to Liveclicker
, for every $1 that marketers spend on advanced personalization, they get a return of $20. Why? Because people value personalized offerings and they will always come back for more because you give them exactly what they want. A one-size-fits-all formula doesn’t work with most people.Customers should feel as if the agent is glad to talk to them and that they will do everything possible within their power to offer them what they are looking for. Being cheerful and communicating positively is important for a personalized experience.
### Ask for Feedback & Close the Loop
Getting feedback directly from the customer will offer a treasure trove of information. It shows the customers that you care and are willing to make amends to better the relationship and their experience.
Surveys offer the customers a chance to voice their opinions.
The most important step in a survey is to close the feedback loop. What does that mean? When you ask for feedback, your customers respond with suggestions, ideas, and complaints. You need to act on this feedback, and once you do, share the updates with the customers. This is called closing the feedback loop. Customers will not only feel valued when you do this but they will also be bolstered to offer more honest feedback the next time too.
### Be Empathetic
Empathy is one of the most underrated emotions in the world. The world will be a better place if there is more empathy.
In customer interactions, empathy is even more crucial
. There are simple ways you can show empathy in your customer interactions. Let us look at a few of them:
Apologize to your customers when there has been a mistake from your side.
Be patient when they do not understand the instructions that you are passing
Thank the customers for sharing their feedback, for being patient with outages, or for the simple fact that they are in business with you.
Repeat and confirm what they are asking for
Let the customer vent if they have been wronged
Use empathetic statements such as “I am sorry, I can completely relate,” or “I would be upset if this happened to me too.”
### Delight Your Customers
One of the biggest parts of delighting someone is to offer them something that they were not expecting in the first place. They don’t have to be massive gestures. It could be something as simple as a handwritten note, a shoutout on social media, company swags, etc. It will create a deeper bond for the customer with your brand. Emotional connections like these, even though they are pretty simple, are a huge motivator for customers to stay loyal.
### Do Not Interrupt the Customer:
While not interrupting someone while they are speaking might sound like advice for high schoolers, most adults are still guilty of this. People want to be heard, and the last thing they want to feel is being disregarded. Allow the customers to fully speak their minds before offering suggestions or reassurance.How you interact with your customers will directly affect your bottom line. You need to keep them engaged and offer them more reasons to come back to you. Every interaction that a customer has with your brand should be a pleasure.Setting a guideline and training all your customer service agents and staff who are interacting with your customers is a laborious task. Deploying Conversational AI in the customer engagement channels lets the brands deliver a uniform customer engagement no matter what time or on what channel.Augment Conversational AI along with the existing customer engagement staff will improve productivity by 10%. If you haven't thought about adopting Conversational AI, this is the best time to think about it.
Request Demo
### Frequently Asked Questions
What are simple ways to improve customer interactions?
Simple improvements include communicating clearly and promptly about product updates or billing changes, personalizing interactions instead of using one size fits all messaging, and closing the loop on customer feedback. Practicing empathy, delighting customers with small unexpected gestures, and not interrupting customers while they speak also help.
Why does personalization matter in customer service?
Liveclicker data shows that for every dollar spent on advanced personalization, marketers see a 20 dollar return. One size fits all approaches fail because customers expect tailored offerings, and agents should convey genuine helpfulness rather than following a generic script.
How should agents practice empathy with frustrated customers?
Agents should apologize for errors, acknowledge emotional states, and use statements such as saying they would feel upset too in the same situation. Letting customers fully express their frustration before responding, and confirming understanding of the request, helps the customer feel heard.
What role can conversational AI play in customer interactions?
Deploying conversational AI helps standardize engagement quality across channels and times of day, rather than relying only on individual agent performance. AI augmentation can improve productivity by 10 percent, supporting consistent communication, feedback handling and personalization at scale.
Why is closing the feedback loop important for customer service?
Surveys gather actionable insights, but the value comes from acting on that feedback and communicating updates back to customers afterward. This shows customers their input matters, which increases the likelihood they will offer candid feedback again in the future.

An intelligent agent in AI is a system that perceives its environment, decides what to do about it, and acts, without a human instructing it at each step. The definition is old, it predates the current wave of language models by decades, and it is still the most useful frame available for thinking about what enterprise software is becoming.
This guide covers the definition properly, the properties that separate an agent from ordinary automation, the four agent types and where each belongs, and then the part textbooks leave out: what actually happens when you put one into a regulated enterprise with a phone line attached.
### TL;DR
An intelligent agent in AI is an autonomous software entity that perceives its environment through sensors or data inputs, reasons about what it perceives against a goal, and acts on that environment to move toward the goal. Five properties define one: autonomy, perception, reasoning, action and learning. Agents are classified as reactive, deliberative, collaborative or hybrid, depending on whether they hold internal state and plan ahead. In an enterprise setting the theory is the easy part. What decides success is whether perception survives a noisy phone line, whether the action layer handles a failed write to a system of record, and whether the whole thing produces an audit trail a regulator will accept.
### What is an intelligent agent in AI?
An intelligent agent is anything that can be viewed as perceiving its environment through sensors and acting upon that environment through actuators, in pursuit of a goal. That framing comes from the classical AI literature and it holds up well, because it is deliberately indifferent to how the agent is built.
A thermostat fits the definition at its simplest. It senses temperature, compares it to a target, and switches a relay. Nobody calls it intelligent, and the reason is instructive: it has no representation of its environment beyond a single number, no capacity to plan, and no ability to improve.
The interesting agents sit further along that axis. They carry a model of the world they operate in, they can reason about a sequence of actions rather than a single one, and they can revise their behaviour based on what happened last time. A collections agent that remembers a borrower asked for a callback on Thursday, and adjusts the next contact accordingly, is doing something a thermostat cannot.
The word that does the real work in the definition is
acts
. A model that produces text and stops is not an agent. It becomes one when its output is wired to something that changes the world: an API call, a database write, a transfer to a human.
### The five properties every intelligent agent needs
These five properties are what separate an intelligent agent from a script that happens to call a language model.
#### Autonomy
The agent operates without step-by-step instruction. Autonomy is a spectrum rather than a binary, and in practice you set its bounds deliberately: an agent may be free to reschedule an appointment but not to issue a refund. The design question is never whether to grant autonomy but where exactly to draw the line, and what happens at the line.
#### Perception
The agent takes in the state of its environment. For a text agent that means a message and some context. For a voice agent it means an audio stream arriving over a telephone network, which is a substantially harder problem and the one most deployments underestimate.
#### Reasoning
The agent decides what to do next given what it perceived and what it is trying to achieve. This is where language models earn their place, and also where they are most often over-credited. A model that reasons beautifully about a request it misheard produces a confident, fluent, wrong action.
#### Action
The agent changes something. It calls a function, writes a record, sends a message, hands over to a person. Function-calling accuracy is measurable and worth measuring: Gnani AI reports ranking first on Berkeley BFCL v3 at 37.99% agentic function-calling accuracy, a benchmark built specifically to test whether an agent picks the right tool with the right arguments.
#### Learning
The agent improves from experience. In an enterprise this is the property to be most careful with, because an agent whose behaviour drifts between audits is a compliance problem regardless of whether the drift was an improvement.

### The types of intelligent agents
The standard taxonomy sorts agents by how much internal state they carry and how far ahead they plan. It is worth knowing because it tells you which type a given problem needs, and choosing a more sophisticated agent than the problem requires is a reliable way to make a system slower and harder to debug for no benefit.
The four types of intelligent agents, and where each one belongs
Agent type
What it perceives
How it decides
What it remembers
Where it is the right choice
Reactive

Maps perception straight to a response with no planning step

Deliberative

Collaborative

Hybrid

Most production enterprise systems are hybrid. A voice agent handling a payment conversation reacts within the turn, because it has to respond inside a second, while a planning layer tracks where the conversation needs to get to across the whole call.
### What changes when an intelligent agent meets an enterprise
Every property in the taxonomy above turns into a specific engineering problem once the agent is running against real customers and real systems. These are the four that decide deployments.
#### Perception becomes a speech recognition problem
When the channel is a phone call, perception is not parsing text. It is recognising speech that arrives at 8kHz, compressed, over a mobile network, from a speaker who switches language mid-sentence. Accuracy measured on clean studio audio tells you very little about that.
Gnani AI reports that
Gnani Prisma v2.5
is trained on more than 14 million hours of real telephonic audio, with under 4% word error rate for Indian speech and 96% code-switching accuracy across its ten production languages. Those figures are measured on telephony audio, so they do not compare directly to numbers published against clean recordings. The
speech to text API
documents the language coverage in detail.
An agent that mishears the amount has not made a reasoning error. It has made a perception error, and no amount of model capability downstream will recover it.
#### Action becomes a write problem
In a textbook the action is atomic. In production it is an API call to a system of record that can be slow, can fail, and can succeed while returning an error. Ask any vendor what their agent tells the customer when the write times out mid-conversation. The honest answer involves an explicit failure path and a handover. The dishonest answer is that it does not happen.
This is also where the distinction between an agent and an assistant becomes concrete. An assistant drafts the update. An agent commits it, which means the agent needs transactional discipline an assistant never does.
#### Governance becomes an audit problem
A regulated enterprise cannot deploy a system whose decisions it cannot reconstruct. That means recording, per interaction, what the agent perceived, what it decided, which tool it called with which arguments, and what came back.
Plexus
, which is in early access on a waitlist, is built around that requirement, composing agents into workflows with guardrails, observability and audit logging.
#### Learning becomes an explainability problem
Continuous learning after deployment is the property enterprises ask for and then, on inspection, often decline. If the agent's behaviour changes between audits, you have to be able to say what changed and why. Most teams settle on a versioned release cycle with offline evaluation rather than live adaptation, which trades some responsiveness for the ability to answer a regulator's question.
### How to measure an intelligent agent deployment
Agent projects fail quietly more often than they fail loudly, usually because nobody agreed what success looked like before launch. Four measures are worth fixing up front.
Task completion rate.
The share of interactions where the agent reached the goal without a human. Measure it per intent, because a blended number hides the intents that are failing.
Perception accuracy on your own data.
Word error rate on your recordings, by language, not the vendor's benchmark on theirs.
Action correctness.
How often the agent called the right tool with the right arguments. Function-calling benchmarks give you a baseline, your own logs give you the truth.
Escalation quality.
How often the agent handed over, and how often it should have handed over and did not. The second number matters more and almost nobody tracks it.
Gnani AI reports under 800ms live conversation response latency for
Gnani Agents
, which is the budget a spoken interaction has to stay inside before the conversation stops feeling like one.
### Where to start with an intelligent agent in AI
Pick one workflow with a narrow intent, a clear definition of done, and an existing manual baseline you can compare against. Instrument the audit trail before you instrument anything else. Then extend, once the perception layer holds up on your own data rather than on a benchmark.
On the deployment question, an intelligent agent handling regulated conversations raises the same residency and control issues as any other system touching customer data. Gnani AI supports cloud, private cloud, on-premise and air-gapped deployment, and the
Artha sovereign stack
runs the models on infrastructure the customer controls. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
If you are moving from theory to build, we have written a
practical guide to building AI agents
, covered
how autonomous decision making works in agent systems
, and looked at
no code agent builders
for teams without engineering capacity. The
solutions
pages set out the workflows these agents are most often pointed at.
### Frequently asked questions
What is an intelligent agent in AI?
An intelligent agent in AI is a software entity that perceives its environment, reasons about what it perceives against a goal, and takes action to move toward that goal without being instructed at each step. The classical definition centres on sensors and actuators, which makes it indifferent to implementation: an agent can be a rules engine, a planner, a language model wired to tools, or a combination.
What is the difference between an intelligent agent and a chatbot?
A chatbot responds; an intelligent agent acts. A chatbot's output is a message, so its effect on the world ends when the message is delivered. An agent's output includes calls to other systems, which means it can book the appointment, update the record or move the money rather than telling the user how to do those things. The engineering consequence is that an agent needs error handling, permissions and an audit trail that a chatbot does not.
What are the four types of intelligent agents?
Reactive, deliberative, collaborative and hybrid. Reactive agents map perception straight to action with no internal state, which makes them fast and predictable. Deliberative agents hold a model of the world and plan a sequence of actions. Collaborative agents coordinate with other agents toward a shared goal. Hybrid agents combine a reactive layer for speed with a deliberative layer for planning, which is what most production enterprise systems end up being.
Are large language models intelligent agents?
Not on their own. A language model is a reasoning component, and a powerful one, but it has no perception of an environment beyond its input and no ability to act beyond producing text. It becomes part of an intelligent agent when it is wired to inputs that observe a real environment and to tools that change it. Treating the model as the whole agent is the most common architectural mistake in this area.
What do intelligent agents need to work in a regulated enterprise?
Three things beyond the model itself: perception accurate enough on the real channel rather than on clean test data, an action layer with explicit handling for failed or ambiguous writes, and an audit trail that records what was perceived, decided, called and returned for every interaction. Residency and deployment mode usually follow from the sector's rules, so confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
How do you measure whether an intelligent agent is working?
Task completion rate per intent, perception accuracy measured on your own data, action correctness against your own logs, and escalation quality in both directions. The last one is the most revealing and the least tracked: how often the agent should have handed over to a human and carried on instead.

### TL;DR
A multilingual NLP model handles many languages inside one set of shared representations, instead of running a separate model per language or translating everything into English first. The advantage enterprises underestimate is not coverage. It is that one model, one orchestration layer and one governance process replace a per-language stack, so adding the eleventh language costs far less than the second one did. The advantage they overestimate is accuracy on languages the model barely saw in training. Multilingual NLP is a cost and consistency play with a real accuracy floor, and the floor is where the pilot should look first.
### What multilingual NLP is, and what it replaces
Three architectures compete for the same job in an enterprise contact centre or back office.
The first is one model per language. It gives you the best per-language accuracy when you have enough data for that language, and it gives you a maintenance problem that grows linearly. Eleven languages means eleven training pipelines, eleven evaluation sets and eleven approval cycles.
The second is translate-then-process. Translate the input into English, run your English model, translate the response back. It is cheap to stand up and it fails in predictable ways: domain terms lose their meaning, regulatory wording drifts, and sentiment inverts on anything idiomatic.
The third is a native multilingual NLP model. One model maps text from many languages into a shared vector space, so intent, entities and sentiment are detected in the language the customer actually used. Knowledge learned in a high-resource language transfers to a low-resource one, which is what makes the eleventh language affordable.
That transfer property is the whole argument. Everything else follows from it.
ENTERPRISE VOICE AI
See Gnani AI's Voice AI Agent in action

### The advantage nobody budgets for: one governance surface
Per-language stacks fragment governance quietly. Each language ends up with its own test set, its own release cadence and its own idea of what an acceptable error is, usually because different teams built them at different times. By the time a regulator asks how a disclosure is worded in Kannada, nobody can answer without three meetings.
A single multilingual layer collapses that. One change management process, one audit trail, one place where a disclosure template lives. For regulated industries this is often worth more than the accuracy difference, because the cost of an inconsistent disclosure across languages is not a model metric.
The same applies to PII handling. Redaction rules written once for a shared representation are easier to prove correct than eleven separate redaction configurations, and under the DPDP Act the burden of proof sits with the enterprise. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
### Where multilingual NLP breaks: code-switching and the data floor
#### Code-switching is the normal case in India
A customer who opens in Hindi, names the product in English and gives the amount in a mix of both is not an edge case in Indian contact centres. Models trained on clean monolingual corpora degrade sharply on this input, and language-identification-first architectures fail hardest, because they try to pick one language before the sentence is over.
The fix is training on genuinely code-mixed data rather than on concatenated monolingual data. Gnani AI reports 96% code-switching accuracy across Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish for Prisma v2.5, trained on 14M+ hours of real telephonic audio, with under 4% word error rate on Indian speech. Those figures are vendor-stated and published on the
Prisma v2.5 speech to text API
page. The underlying problem is covered in more depth in
code-switching speech recognition for Hinglish
.
#### Tokenisation is a hidden cost in Indian scripts
Models built on English-first tokenizers fragment Devanagari, Tamil and Bengali text into many more tokens per word, which raises inference cost and eats context window on exactly the languages you added the model for. Gnani AI reports that Evon v3.3 uses a 163,072-token vocabulary rebuilt for Indian scripts and consumes roughly 20% fewer tokens per Indian word than the GPT-5 family tokenizer, with 30B total parameters and around 3.5B active per token. Details are on the
Evon v3.3 release page
Check the tokenizer before you check the benchmark. A model that scores well and costs twice as much per Indian-language conversation has a commercial problem that no accuracy chart will show you.
#### Low-resource languages still have a floor
Cross-language transfer reduces the data you need. It does not remove it. Expect a measurable accuracy gap on your smallest languages, and plan a small curated dataset plus active learning for each one rather than assuming transfer will cover it.

### Where multilingual NLP sits in a voice stack
In a voice deployment the NLP layer is sandwiched between two others, and the layer above it usually sets the ceiling. Speech recognition produces the transcript. The multilingual model reads intent, entities and sentiment from it. An orchestration layer turns that into an action against a core system, in the same way regardless of which language the request arrived in.
Two consequences follow. First, a transcription error propagates: if the ASR drops the account number, no amount of language understanding recovers it, which is why entity-level accuracy belongs in the evaluation alongside
word error rate
. Second, every layer adds latency, and the budget is tight in a live call. Gnani AI reports under 800ms live conversation response latency for
Gnani Agents
, and the component-by-component breakdown is set out in
what causes latency in voice AI
Deployment location is the third constraint. For BFSI, insurance and healthcare workloads the model often has to run where the data already is. The
Artha sovereign stack
runs the reasoning, speech and orchestration layers on infrastructure the enterprise controls, and Gnani AI reports single-node inference for Evon v3.3, which is what makes on-premise and air-gapped deployment practical at that parameter count.
### How to evaluate a multilingual NLP model properly
Build a gold test set per language from your own real utterances, not from translated English ones. Translated test sets flatter translate-then-process architectures and tell you nothing about code-switching.
Report intent accuracy and entity recall per language, never as a blended average. The average hides the language that is failing.
Include a code-switched subset in every language pair your customers actually mix, and score it separately.
Measure tokens consumed per conversation per language alongside accuracy. That number drives your running cost.
Measure end-to-end task completion, because a correct intent that fails to complete the workflow is worth nothing operationally.
Have native speakers review a sample. Automated scoring misses register, politeness and the kind of error that reads as rude rather than wrong.
Gnani AI does not publish pricing, so per-conversation economics have to come out of the commercial conversation. That is a genuine disadvantage early in an evaluation, and worth raising in the first call.
### Treating language as an asset rather than a coverage checkbox
The enterprises getting real value from multilingual NLP are not the ones with the longest language list on a slide. They are the ones who picked two or three high-volume journeys, built proper per-language test sets, measured the floor on their weakest language, and only then expanded. One orchestration layer and one governance process is the compounding advantage, and it compounds precisely because adding a language stops being a project.
The
Gnani AI model family
page covers how the speech, speech-to-speech and reasoning layers fit together across Indian languages, and you can
book a demo
to run your own multilingual call data against the stack.
### Frequently asked questions
What is multilingual NLP?
Multilingual NLP is a single language model that processes and generates text or speech across many languages using shared internal representations, rather than one model per language. Because the representations are shared, intent and entity knowledge learned in a well-resourced language transfers to a scarce-data one, which is what makes broad language coverage affordable for an enterprise.
How is multilingual NLP different from machine translation?
Translation converts text from one language into another and then hands it to a separate model. Multilingual NLP interprets intent, entities and sentiment directly in the language the customer used. The practical difference shows up on domain terms, regulatory wording and code-switched sentences, all of which translation pipelines distort before the understanding step ever runs.
Does multilingual NLP handle code-switching?
Only if it was trained on genuinely code-mixed data. Models trained on separate monolingual corpora and architectures that identify the language before processing both degrade on mid-sentence switches. Gnani AI reports 96% code-switching accuracy for Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish on Prisma v2.5. Test any vendor's claim on your own recordings, because code-switching patterns vary by region and customer segment.
What does multilingual NLP cost to run in Indian languages?
Cost is driven as much by tokenisation as by model size. English-first tokenizers split Devanagari, Tamil and Bengali into many more tokens per word, which raises per-conversation cost and consumes context. Gnani AI reports roughly 20% fewer tokens per Indian word for Evon v3.3 against the GPT-5 family tokenizer. Measure tokens per conversation per language during evaluation.
Which industries benefit most from multilingual NLP?
Those with high interaction volume across many languages and a compliance obligation attached to the wording: banking and lending, insurance, telecom and healthcare. The pattern that predicts value is repetitive conversations in languages your current stack handles poorly, which is where per-language maintenance cost is highest and accuracy is lowest.

### TL;DR
To reduce latency in voice AI you have to stop treating it as one number. The delay a caller hears is the sum of six stages: audio transport, speech recognition, end-of-speech detection, reasoning, speech synthesis and the return trip down the telephony leg. Each has its own budget and its own fix, and the largest contributor is usually not the model. Endpointing and tool calls are the two stages that quietly eat hundreds of milliseconds while the engineering attention goes to the language model. Measure each stage separately on production calls, set a per-stage budget, stream everything that can stream, and hold the total inside roughly 800 milliseconds from the caller's last word to the first returned sound.
### What latency means in a voice conversation
Human conversation runs on a tight clock. Stivers and colleagues, writing in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences in 2009, measured the gap between a yes-or-no question and its answer across ten languages and found median gaps between 0 and 300 milliseconds. Later work by Levinson and Torreira puts the most common gap at around 200 milliseconds. People do not wait to hear the end of your sentence before planning a reply; they predict it and start speaking on cue.
This is why voice AI latency behaves differently from web latency. A page that loads in 900 milliseconds feels fast. A voice agent that replies 900 milliseconds after you stop talking feels like it did not understand you, and callers respond by repeating themselves, which corrupts the next turn and makes the problem worse.
ENTERPRISE VOICE AI
See Gnani AI's Voice AI Agent in action
200+ Enterprises · 30M daily calls · 10 Indic languages
Book A Demo
### What causes latency in voice AI, stage by stage
Measured end to end, the delay a caller experiences breaks into six stages. The table below gives the shape of a workable budget alongside the figures Gnani AI publishes for each layer. Treat the published figures as vendor-stated, measured under Gnani AI's conditions, and reproduce them on your own traffic.
A voice AI latency budget, stage by stage
Stage
What is being measured
Gnani AI published figure
Where the time usually goes
Audio transport

Gnani AI targets under 800 ms of response time in live conversations across Gnani Agents. All figures above are published by Gnani AI and measured under Gnani AI's own conditions. Reproduce them on your own traffic before adopting them as targets.
#### Audio transport
Before any model sees the audio, it has to arrive. A PSTN call routed through a carrier, a media gateway and a session border controller accumulates delay that no amount of model optimisation recovers. Co-locating the media path with inference, and keeping the number of hops between the carrier and the recognition layer small, is the cheapest latency work available and the most often skipped.
#### Speech recognition
Batch recognition waits for the utterance to finish, then transcribes. Streaming recognition emits partial hypotheses as the caller speaks, so the downstream stages can start early.
Prisma v2.5
streams at sub-200 millisecond latency on 8 kHz telephony audio. Accuracy matters to latency here too: a mis-recognition forces a clarification turn, and a clarification turn costs a full round trip rather than a few hundred milliseconds.
#### End-of-speech detection
This is the stage that most often ruins an otherwise fast system. The agent has to decide the caller has finished. Set the silence threshold long and every turn inherits that wait. Set it short and the agent interrupts, which costs far more than it saves because the caller starts again. Fixed silence timers are the wrong tool. Semantic endpointing, which considers whether the utterance is actually complete, and barge-in handling that lets the caller cut in are what move this number. We cover the mechanics in
our guide to real-time barge-in
.
#### Reasoning
What the caller perceives is time to first token, not total generation time, because synthesis can begin on the first few words.
Evon v3.3
publishes 302 milliseconds to first token and 257 tokens per second, at 30 billion parameters with roughly 3.5 billion active per token. The Mixture-of-Experts design is the reason a large model can answer quickly: only a fraction of the weights run for any given token.
#### Tool calls and retrieval
This stage is absent from most latency diagrams and present in most production systems. A balance lookup, a CRM read or a policy check inserts a network round trip into the middle of the turn, and a slow backend can exceed every model stage combined. Two fixes work: start the call in parallel with generation where the result is predictable, and fill the gap with speech rather than silence so the caller knows the agent is working.
#### Speech synthesis
Again the number that matters is time to first audio, not time to complete the utterance.
Timbre v2.5
publishes sub-100 millisecond time to first audio and streams, which means the caller hears the opening words while the rest is still being produced.
### How to reduce latency in voice AI
Six changes, in the order that usually pays best.
Instrument each stage separately before changing anything.
One end-to-end number tells you there is a problem and nothing about where. Timestamp the caller's last speech frame, first partial transcript, endpoint decision, first reasoning token, first audio frame and first audio at the handset.
Fix endpointing before touching the model.
Replace fixed silence timers with semantic endpointing, and enable barge-in. This is routinely the largest single saving available.
Stream every stage that can stream.
Partial transcripts into reasoning, first tokens into synthesis, first audio frames onto the line. A pipeline that streams end to end is not the sum of its stages, because the stages overlap.
Move the slow backend call off the critical path.
Prefetch what is predictable, run in parallel what is not, and cover the remainder with a short spoken acknowledgement rather than dead air.
Shorten the physical path.
Deploy inference in the same region as the telephony termination. For workloads that cannot leave the building,
Artha
runs the full stack on-premise or air-gapped, which removes the public network leg entirely.
Consider removing the text intermediate.
A cascaded pipeline pays the handoff cost between recognition, reasoning and synthesis on every turn.
Warp v2.0
is a native speech-to-speech model at 5 billion parameters with sub-200 millisecond P95, which collapses three stages into one.
### Why latency gets worse at peak hours
A system that measures well in testing and badly at 6pm is usually queuing, not computing. Inference capacity is finite, and when concurrent sessions exceed what the deployment can serve, requests wait before they are processed. The stage timings each look normal; the total does not.
The diagnosis is to plot your per-stage timings against concurrent session count rather than against wall clock. If latency rises with concurrency, it is a capacity problem and no model change will fix it. Gnani AI reports support for 35,000 or more simultaneous streams at the recognition layer and more than 30 million daily voice interactions across its
enterprise deployments
. Whatever platform you run, ask for the concurrency ceiling and the latency curve at 80% of it, not the figure at one session.
### What to hold yourself to
Knowing how to reduce latency in voice AI is mostly a measurement discipline. Set a per-stage budget, publish it to the team, and treat a regression in any single stage as a defect rather than waiting for the total to breach. Gnani AI targets under 800 milliseconds of response time in live conversations across
Gnani Agents
, which leaves enough headroom under the human turn-taking gap that callers stop noticing the machine. For how to turn these budgets into enforceable targets and alerts, see
our piece on latency targets and enforcement
### Frequently asked questions
How do I reduce latency in voice AI?
Start by measuring each of the six stages separately, then fix end-of-speech detection first, because fixed silence timers are usually the largest single contributor. After that, stream every stage that can stream, move backend lookups off the critical path, and deploy inference in the same region as your telephony termination. Change the model last, not first.
What factors affect latency in real-time voice AI conversations?
Six: audio transport across the carrier and gateway, streaming speech recognition, end-of-speech detection, reasoning time to first token, any tool call or database lookup inside the turn, and speech synthesis time to first audio. Concurrency sits underneath all of them, because queuing at peak load inflates every stage at once.
What is latency in conversational AI?
It is the time between the caller finishing a sentence and hearing the first sound of the reply. It is not model inference time, which is only one component, and it is not time to a complete response, because a streaming system starts speaking before it has finished generating.
What latency should a voice API provide?
Judge each layer on its own published figure rather than on an end-to-end claim. Streaming recognition in the region of 200 milliseconds, synthesis time to first audio under 100 milliseconds, and reasoning time to first token around 300 milliseconds leave room for transport and endpointing inside a total under 800 milliseconds. Ask which of these are measured at the median and which at P95, because the difference is large.
Which voice bot has the lowest latency?
Published numbers are not comparable across vendors, because they measure different things. One counts model compute only, another counts the full turn including the telephony leg, and the two differ by hundreds of milliseconds. The only useful comparison is a trial on your own call paths, with your own timestamps, at your own peak concurrency.
Why does my voice AI system get slower during peak hours?
Almost always queuing rather than computation. When concurrent sessions exceed the capacity the deployment can serve, requests wait to be scheduled, and every stage inflates together. Plot per-stage latency against concurrent sessions. If the curve rises with load, add capacity or raise the concurrency ceiling, because no model tuning will address it.

### What a multilingual voicebot is, in short
A multilingual voicebot is a voice agent that holds a spoken conversation in more than one language, understands what the caller wants, and completes the action behind the request. It differs from an IVR in that the caller speaks naturally instead of pressing keys, and it differs from a chatbot in that it has to survive real telephony: 8kHz audio, background noise, interruptions, and callers who switch language mid-sentence. In Indian deployments that last point is the whole problem. A system that handles Hindi and English separately but breaks on a sentence containing both is not multilingual in any way that matters on a live call.
### From IVR to a multilingual voicebot
The lineage is worth understanding because it explains what most enterprise voice systems are still carrying. Touch-tone IVR asked the caller to translate their problem into a number, and the menu tree was the product. Keyword-matching systems in the 2000s let people speak but only recognised a fixed vocabulary, so anything phrased unexpectedly fell through to an operator.
Speech recognition and natural language understanding improved through the 2010s, which made free-form speech workable and moved the difficulty from recognition to dialogue management. What changed more recently is that the reasoning layer can hold context across turns, ask a clarifying question and decide on an action, rather than following a script an engineer drew in advance. That is the practical difference between a voice bot and a voice agent, and it is why containment stopped being the only measure worth tracking.
### What multilingual actually has to mean
Vendors count languages on a slide. Buyers should test four separate capabilities, because a language count tells you almost nothing about any of them.
#### Recognition on telephony audio
An 8kHz phone line discards most of the frequency range a model trained on studio audio relies on. Gnani AI reports that
Gnani Prisma v2.5
is trained on more than 14 million hours of real telephonic audio and reaches under 4% word error rate on Indian speech, with first place in eight of nine Indian languages on the Kathbath Noisy 8kHz benchmark. Any vendor's accuracy figure should come with the sample rate attached, and yours should be measured on your own recordings.
#### Code-switching inside one sentence
Indian callers routinely mix languages inside a single clause. Handling Hindi and English as two separate modes does not solve this. Gnani AI reports 96% code-switching accuracy on Prisma v2.5 and explicit support for Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish. This is the capability to test first, because it fails silently: the transcript looks plausible, the intent is wrong, and the call goes sideways two turns later.
#### Reasoning in the language, not through English
A system that translates an Indian language into English, reasons in English and translates back loses meaning at both boundaries and adds latency at both. Gnani AI reports that
Evon v2.0
reasons across 11+ Indic languages directly, tuned for BFSI, insurance, healthcare and telecom, and that the open-weight Evon v3.3 uses a vocabulary rebuilt for Indian scripts that needs roughly 20% fewer tokens per Indian word than the GPT-5 family tokenizer. Fewer tokens per word is a cost and latency argument as much as a quality one.
#### Speech output that sounds like the language
Correct pronunciation of Indian names, numerals read in lakh and crore rather than millions, and prosody that fits the context. Gnani AI reports that
Gnani Timbre v2.5
, currently in Beta, covers 10+ Indic languages in the production API with a mean opinion score of 4.23 on 8kHz telephony and time to first audio under 100ms.
ENTERPRISE VOICE AI
See Gnani AI's Voice AI Agent in action
200+ Enterprises · 30M daily calls · 10 Indic languages
Book A Demo
### The stack behind a multilingual voicebot
Four layers run in sequence on every turn, and the latency budget is the sum of all of them plus the network. Recognition turns audio into text. Reasoning decides what the caller wants and what to do. Action completes the task in a back-end system. Speech synthesis turns the reply back into audio.
Gnani AI reports response latency under 800ms in live conversations on
Gnani Agents
, sub-200ms streaming from Prisma v2.5, and under 250ms p95 first byte from Timbre v2.5. Those are measured differently from each other, so they do not simply add up, and no vendor's published component numbers should be assembled into an end to end figure by a buyer. Ask for the end to end number, measured on a real call, on your network.
There is a fifth option worth knowing about. Gnani AI reports Warp v2.0 as a 5 billion parameter model that goes speech to speech directly, with no text layer in between and sub-200ms P95. Removing the text intermediate removes an error surface as well as a latency step, which matters most on exactly the code-mixed speech that trips the four-layer pipeline.

### Where a multilingual voicebot earns its place
The pattern that works is a high-volume, repetitive contact reason with a deterministic answer and an API that can finish the job. Collections and payment reminders, appointment booking and rescheduling, onboarding and know-your-customer steps, lead qualification, renewals, and status enquiries all fit. Gnani AI reports these as live use cases on Gnani Agents across BFSI, telecom, insurance, healthcare and consumer durables, with 200+ enterprise deployments and 30M+ daily voice interactions.
The pattern that fails is a contact reason requiring judgement, or one where the action lives in a back office no API reaches. Those belong with a human, supported by
Gnani Assist
rather than replaced by an agent. Being honest about that boundary early is what stops a voice programme from stalling at the second use case.
### What to test before you buy
Word error rate on your own recordings, at 8kHz, in every language you actually receive, measured separately for monolingual and code-mixed calls.
End to end response latency on a live call over your network, not the sum of component figures from a datasheet.
Barge-in behaviour. Interrupt the agent mid-sentence and see whether it stops cleanly and keeps the context.
Escalation. Confirm the human receives the full conversation history rather than a cold transfer.
Write access. Have the agent complete an action in your system of record during the pilot rather than describe one.
Change control. Find out who edits a live flow, how long the change takes to reach production, and whether it needs a vendor ticket.
### Compliance for multilingual voice agents
Call recordings, transcripts and call metadata are personal data under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act. Outbound calling is subject to TRAI rules on consent and do-not-disturb. Financial services carry RBI expectations, insurance carries IRDAI, and US health data brings HIPAA into scope.
The requirement that gets missed most often is disclosure: the agent has to say it is AI, in every language it speaks, in the opening turn. Translating the disclosure as an afterthought produces wording that is technically present and practically useless. Gnani AI is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and ISO 27001 certified, and states HIPAA, GDPR and PCI-DSS compliance, with cloud, private cloud, on-premise and air-gapped deployment where data cannot leave the network. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
### Where this leaves you
A multilingual voicebot is worth deploying when the contact reason is repetitive, the answer is deterministic and an API can complete the action. Judge vendors on code-switching accuracy measured on your own 8kHz recordings, on end to end latency on a real call, and on whether the agent can write to your system of record rather than only read from it. Language counts on a slide are the least informative number in the evaluation. To hear the stack on a live call,
book a demo
, or read the model specifications on
the models page
.
### Frequently asked questions
What is a multilingual voicebot?
A voice agent that holds a spoken conversation in more than one language, understands the caller's intent, and completes the action behind the request. The useful definition is behavioural rather than numerical: it recognises telephony-quality speech in each language, handles callers switching language mid-sentence, reasons without translating through English, and speaks each language with correct pronunciation and number formats.
How is a voice bot different from a chatbot and an IVR?
An IVR navigates a fixed menu through keypresses or a small fixed vocabulary. A chatbot handles typed text, where spelling is unambiguous and there is no latency pressure inside a turn. A voice bot has to recognise noisy speech in real time, handle interruptions, and reply fast enough that the pause is not audible, which makes it the hardest of the three to deploy well.
How many languages can a voice bot handle?
Gnani AI reports 40+ languages at model level and more than 10 Indic languages in production speech recognition. The more useful question for a buyer is not the count but the depth: which languages are production-grade on 8kHz audio, which are supported for code-switching, and which have been tested on accents from your customer base.
Do multilingual voicebots handle Hinglish and other mixed speech?
The good ones do, and it is the capability most worth testing because it fails quietly. Gnani AI reports 96% code-switching accuracy on Prisma v2.5 with named support for Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish. Ask any vendor for a test on your own code-mixed recordings rather than a demo call in a single language.
How fast does a voice bot have to respond?
Fast enough that the caller does not hear a gap where a human would have replied. Gnani AI reports response latency under 800ms in live conversations. Measure the end to end number on your own network, because component latencies published by any vendor are measured under different conditions and cannot be added together.
Does a voice bot have to disclose that it is AI?
Yes, in the opening turn, in every language it speaks. Build it into the script design rather than adding it before launch, and have your legal and compliance team approve the wording for each market and each language.

### What is Agentic AI?
Agentic AI refers to artificial intelligence systems that can operate independently, making decisions and taking actions without constant human input. Unlike traditional AI, which relies on predefined rules and instructions, Agentic AI adapts to its environment, learns from interactions, and solves problems dynamically. This ability to function autonomously makes it a powerful tool for businesses and industries looking to automate complex tasks. Agentic AI combines advance technologies like
LLMs, SLMs
and
Machine Learning (ML)
to improve efficiency and streamline operations. These AI-powered agents can manage customer support inquiries across omnichannel platforms, including both voice and chat. Since these systems can process vast amounts of information in real-time, they help businesses make faster and more informed decisions. If you're involved in selecting, implementing, or managing AI solutions, understanding agentic AI should be a priority. It’s not just another technology to explore when convenient—it’s a new approach to using AI for problem-solving, optimizing operations, and improving outcomes across your organization.
### The History of Agentic AI
Conversational AI
has come a long way,
evolving from simple chatbots
to intelligent assistants that can understand language and make decisions on their own. Earlier versions of conversational AI worked by matching patterns and providing scripted responses within a limited scope. These systems could only handle basic queries and lacked real understanding of language. As AI models have been trained on larger amounts of data, their ability to generate natural, human-like responses has greatly improved. Large language models (LLMs) like
GPT-4
can now engage in more meaningful conversations. However, businesses need more than just AI that can respond well—they need systems that can
handle complex inquires
and make decisions without constant supervision. This has led to the development of AI that can set its own goals, think through problems, and connect with business tools to complete tasks. These advancements are making AI-powered assistants more useful in the workplace. They can now follow instructions more accurately, break down multi-step tasks, and adjust their actions based on new information. This shift is helping businesses automate more complex processes, making operations smoother and more efficient. In summary, Agentic AI signifies a paradigm shift in artificial intelligence, moving beyond traditional models to create autonomous systems capable of complex problem-solving and adaptive learning. This evolution is set to redefine how businesses operate in an increasingly digital landscape.
### How does Agentic AI differ from Gen AI in terms of autonomy and decision-making-
Agentic AI marks a paradigm shift and is now AI’s third wave. Unlike Generative AI, which creates content based on prompts, Agentic AI is autonomous. Where Generative AI is reactive, Agentic AI is proactive and can solve complex problems independently. Below is a comparative analysis of how they differ in terms of autonomy and decision-making:
AspectGenerative AIAgentic AIAutonomy
Operates reactively; generates responses based on input prompts but does not act independently. Functions proactively; sets its own objectives and takes actions without requiring explicit instructions.
Decision-Making
Generates outputs based on learned patterns from training data but does not evaluate different outcomes or make strategic choices. Engages in reasoning, problem-solving, and adaptive decision-making by evaluating different scenarios and selecting the most effective course of action.
Interaction with Environment
Processes information passively and provides outputs without considering real-time context or updates. Continuously interacts with its environment, gathers real-time data, and adjusts its decisions based on changing conditions.
Goal-Oriented Behavior
Does not set goals; it generates text, images, or code based on user queries. Can define and pursue objectives, break tasks into steps, and make decisions to achieve goals efficiently.
Execution Capability
Requires human intervention to use generated content effectively; lacks the ability to execute complex tasks. Can perform end-to-end task automation by integrating with enterprise systems, executing workflows, and making adjustments based on outcomes.
Use Cases
Content creation, summarization, translation, and creative writing. IT automation, customer support, business workflow automation, and autonomous task management. Understanding these distinctions is crucial for organizations aiming to leverage AI technologies effectively. While Generative AI excels at creating content based on existing data patterns, Agentic AI extends beyond content generation to autonomously execute tasks and manage workflows, thereby offering a more comprehensive solution for complex business needs.[caption id="attachment_42651" align="aligncenter" width="1024"]
🔄 Agentic AI Workflow – Streamline operations with intelligent automation, predictive analytics, and AI-powered call routing for a seamless customer experience.[/caption]
### How does agentic AI work?
Agentic AI is designed to operate with a high degree of autonomy, enabling AI systems to reason, make decisions, and take actions without continuous human intervention. Unlike traditional automation, which follows predefined workflows, agentic AI dynamically adapts to new information and adjusts its actions accordingly. This is achieved through a structured process that includes perception, reasoning, action execution, and continuous learning.
#### Perception: Understanding Context and Inputs
Agentic AI starts by gathering and processing information from multiple sources, including structured databases, unstructured text, APIs, enterprise systems, and real-world interactions. It utilizes advanced
natural language processing (NLP)
,
Large language models
Machine learning
to interpret user requests, system states, and environmental factors. By recognizing patterns, analyzing historical data, and detecting real-time changes, the AI builds a contextual understanding of the situation, ensuring accurate responses and actions.
#### Reasoning and Planning: Autonomous Decision-Making
One of the core differentiators of agentic AI is its ability to
reason and plan
. Using
large language models (LLMs), S
mall language models(SLMs)
and other advanced machine learning models, it breaks down complex tasks into smaller, manageable steps. Unlike traditional AI that executes predefined workflows, agentic AI
sets goals dynamically
, determines optimal action sequences, and adapts strategies based on changing conditions.
It evaluates multiple potential outcomes before choosing the most efficient course of action.
It refines decision-making processes by learning from previous successes and failures.
Action Execution: Automating Tasks Across Systems
Agentic AI seamlessly interacts with enterprise applications, APIs, and digital tools to
execute actions
and automate workflows. By integrating with CRM systems, cloud services, databases, and communication platforms, it can:
Retrieve and process information in real-time.
Automate multi-step workflows across different systems.
Execute complex commands without human intervention.
Unlike rule-based automation, which is limited to predefined responses, agentic AI dynamically adjusts its execution path based on feedback, errors, or unexpected developments.
#### Learning and Adaptation: Continuous Improvement
A key feature of agentic AI is its ability to
learn from experience
. By leveraging reinforcement learning and feedback mechanisms, it refines its strategies and enhances its performance over time.
It continuously updates its understanding based on new data.
It improves accuracy by recognizing patterns in past interactions.
It self-corrects errors to enhance reliability.
This continuous learning cycle ensures that agentic AI becomes more efficient and effective the more it operates within an enterprise ecosystem. Agentic AI marks a shift from static, rule-based automation to
adaptive, goal-driven AI systems
that can
reason, plan, execute, and learn
. By integrating with enterprise tools, making independent decisions, and automating complex workflows, agentic AI is revolutionizing industries, enabling businesses to scale operations, enhance decision-making, and improve efficiency with minimal human oversight.
### Key Benefits of Agentic AI and Agentic Automation:
#### Increased Efficiency and Productivity :
These systems can handle complex, decision-intensive tasks that were previously managed by humans, allowing employees to focus on strategic initiatives and creative problem-solving.
By automating routine and time-consuming processes, organizations can achieve higher productivity and reduce operational bottlenecks. Integrating Agentic AI in customer support ensures faster, more accurate responses while freeing employees to focus on high-value, strategic activities.
#### Enhanced Customer Experiences :
AI-powered agents can provide personalized and responsive interactions at scale,
Delivering consistent customer experience
and loyalty.
With the ability to operate 24/7, these agents ensure consistent customer support and can quickly address customer inquiries and issues.
#### Improved Decision-Making with AI Automation
Agentic AI leverages machine learning models to process vast amounts of data, identify patterns, and generate intelligent recommendations, helping businesses make faster and more informed decisions.
AI-powered agents enable real-time decision-making by continuously analyzing incoming data, adjusting strategies, and responding dynamically to changing business conditions.
#### Scalability and Flexibility
Unlike traditional automation, agentic AI can handle unpredictable workflows, scaling operations up or down based on demand and optimizing resource allocation.
AI agents seamlessly integrate with enterprise systems, ensuring smooth workflow automation across different business functions and departments.
#### Higher Operational Efficiency and Cost Savings
Automating complex and labor-intensive processes
reduces operational costs
by minimizing manual effort, allowing businesses to optimize workforce utilization
.•
AI-powered agents improve accuracy and consistency by reducing human errors in data-driven and repetitive tasks, leading to better efficiency and performance.
### What are the most significant use cases of agentic AI today?
Agentic AI is transforming various industries by enabling systems to perform complex tasks autonomously, leading to increased efficiency and innovation. Some of the most impactful use cases today include.
#### Customer Service Enhancement
AI agents are transforming customer support by automating routine communications and enhancing self-service capabilities. This leads to reduced response times and improved customer satisfaction, as AI agents can handle inquiries efficiently and provide consistent support.
#### Insurance Claims Processing
In the insurance sector, agentic AI automates the entire claims process—from initial filing to final payout. This automation results in faster processing times, reduced errors, and a significantly improved customer experience, as claims are handled swiftly and accurately.
#### Supply Chain Optimization
Agentic AI analyzes vast amounts of data in real-time to optimize routes, predict potential bottlenecks, and adjust inventory levels based on demand fluctuations. This dynamic optimization ensures efficient delivery of goods and services, reducing costs and enhancing customer satisfaction.
#### Financial Services Advancements
In financial institutions, agentic AI provides personalized investment advice and manages risk by analyzing extensive data to identify potential vulnerabilities. This proactive approach helps in minimizing losses and strengthening the overall resilience of the financial system.
#### Healthcare Innovations
Agentic AI accelerates drug discovery and development by rapidly analyzing massive datasets to identify potential drug targets and predict their efficacy. Additionally, AI agents recommend personalized treatment plans based on individual patient data, improving patient outcomes and optimizing resource use. These applications demonstrate how agentic AI is driving significant improvements across various sectors, making processes more efficient, accurate, and responsive to changing needs.

Agentic AI is redefining how companies approach
customer support automation
. Unlike traditional AI systems that rely on static rules, Agentic AI leverages autonomous AI capabilities to automate customer service processes with a higher degree of flexibility and intelligence. This shift toward AI-driven workflow automation enables
businesses to streamline operations, reduce response times, and deliver more personalized customer experiences.
One of the key benefits of Agentic AI in customer support is its
ability to handle complex
, multi-step interactions without human intervention. It goes beyond simple scripted responses by adapting to
real-time customer queries
, learning from past interactions, and making context-aware decisions.
For example
, an Agentic AI use case in a support center might involve an AI agent autonomously guiding customers through troubleshooting steps, escalating issues only when necessary, and even predicting future problems based on user behavior.Moreover,
AI process automation powered by Agentic AI
ensures that repetitive tasks like ticket categorization, data entry, and follow-up communications are handled efficiently. Agentic AI will also benefit
from its ability to integrate seamlessly with existing CRM systems, chat platforms, and other enterprise tools. This intelligent automation ensures that customer support workflows are not only faster but also more accurate and consistent across channels.

Investing in agentic AI is becoming increasingly crucial for enterprises looking to stay competitive in today’s fast-evolving business landscape. Unlike traditional AI systems that operate within predefined parameters, agentic AI exhibits goal-directed behavior, enabling it to autonomously set objectives and execute actions to achieve them. ### Frequently Asked Questions
What is agentic AI?
Agentic AI refers to systems that operate independently, making decisions without constant human input by combining large language models, small language models and machine learning. Unlike simple chatbots, they can set goals, connect to business tools, and handle multi-step tasks on their own.
How is agentic AI different from generative AI?
Generative AI is reactive, producing content in response to a prompt, while agentic AI is proactive and goal oriented, executing entire workflows on its own. Agentic systems evaluate scenarios and adjust their actions based on real time context as they work.
How does agentic AI actually work?
It follows a four step process, perception, where it gathers data from databases and APIs, reasoning and planning, where language models break tasks into steps, action execution, where it integrates with CRM and cloud systems, and learning and adaptation, where reinforcement learning improves it over time.
What are the main benefits of agentic AI for businesses?
Benefits include increased efficiency that frees employees for strategic work, better customer experiences through 24/7 personalized interactions, improved decision making from pattern recognition, easier scalability, and cost savings from reduced human error in repetitive tasks.

TL;DR.
Agent assist is AI that works alongside a human agent during a live conversation. It listens to the call, retrieves the right policy or account answer in real time, prompts the next best action, and writes the summary and CRM update when the call ends. It does not replace the agent. On Gnani AI deployments it is associated with an 18% improvement in agent efficiency, 70% faster time to proficiency for new hires, and a 90%+ reduction in after-call admin, as published on the Gnani AI enterprise page.
### What agent assist actually does during a live call
Agent assist sits in the background of a conversation your agent is already having. Three things happen at once. The call audio is transcribed as it streams. The transcript is matched against your knowledge base, product catalogue and policy documents. The matched answer surfaces on the agent's screen while the customer is still speaking.
That loop has to close in under a second to be useful. If the suggestion lands after the agent has already improvised an answer, it is noise. This is why the speech layer matters more than the interface. Indian contact centre audio arrives at 8kHz over mobile networks, often with two languages inside one sentence, so an assist layer built on studio-quality English transcription degrades the moment it meets a real queue.
Gnani Prisma v2.5
is trained on 14M+ hours of real telephonic audio and reports under 4% word error rate on Indian speech with 96% code-switching accuracy.
The post-call half is quieter and often worth more. Summaries, disposition codes, CRM fields and follow-up tasks are generated from the transcript instead of typed by the agent after the customer has hung up.
ENTERPRISE VOICE AI
See Gnani AI's Voice AI Agent in action
200+ Enterprises · 30M daily calls · 10 Indic languages
Book A Demo
### Agent assist compared with an AI voice agent
These two products get confused constantly, and buying the wrong one is an expensive mistake. An AI voice agent handles the conversation itself, with no human on the line. Agent assist never speaks to the customer. It changes what the human knows and how fast they know it.
Most contact centres run both. The voice agent takes the repetitive, high-volume intents such as balance checks, payment reminders and appointment slots. The calls that survive triage reach a human, and those are the harder ones, which is exactly where assist pays for itself.

Outcome figures are Gnani AI published figures for its own platform.
### Where agent assist earns its place
Two conditions predict whether a deployment works. The first is agent turnover. If a third of your floor is new every quarter, the gap between a tenured agent and a four-week agent is pure cost, and a real-time knowledge layer closes part of it. The second is policy complexity. Lending, insurance and telecom plans change often enough that no agent reliably holds the current rules in their head.
Collections.
Surfacing the current settlement rules and the permitted language for a given bucket while the conversation is live. The
collections voice AI
page covers how this fits a recovery workflow.
Support escalations.
Pulling case history and the last three interactions so the customer does not repeat themselves.
Onboarding and KYC.
Prompting the exact document list and the verification order for the product being opened.
New-hire ramp.
Guided workflows that keep a four-week agent inside policy without a supervisor on their shoulder.
### What agent assist improves, with the numbers Gnani AI publishes
Gnani AI reports the following outcomes for
: an 18% improvement in agent efficiency, 70% faster time to proficiency, a 30% increase in CSAT, and a 90%+ reduction in after-call admin. These are vendor figures measured across enterprise deployments, so treat them as a directional benchmark and agree your own baseline before a pilot.
Pick the metrics before the pilot starts, not after. Average handle time is the obvious one and the easiest to game. First contact resolution, policy adherence on monitored calls, and time to proficiency for new hires are harder to move and tell you more. Quality scoring across the full call corpus rather than a sampled few comes from
Gnani Analytics
, which is usually bought alongside assist for exactly this reason.
### What to check before you buy agent assist
Language coverage on your actual traffic.
Ask for word error rate on 8kHz telephony audio in the languages your queue speaks, not on clean studio recordings. The two numbers are not comparable.
Latency, end to end.
Transcription speed alone means nothing. Measure the gap between the customer finishing a sentence and the suggestion appearing.
Knowledge ingestion.
How your policy documents, product catalogue and past tickets get in, and how a policy change propagates the same day.
Desktop integration.
Whether it runs inside the CRM your agents already use. Gnani Assist lists integrations with Salesforce, Zendesk, WhatsApp, Viber and Telegram.
Deployment mode.
Cloud, private cloud, on-premise or air-gapped. For regulated buyers this decides the shortlist before any feature does.
### Compliance considerations for regulated contact centres
Agent assist processes call audio and transcripts, which are personal data under India's DPDP Act. BFSI deployments carry RBI expectations, insurance carries IRDAI, and outbound telephony carries TRAI consent and DND rules. Where the assist layer also touches voiceprints or speaker embeddings, that data is biometric and sits at the highest sensitivity tier.
Practically, this means checking where transcripts are stored, how long they are retained, who can read them, and whether the model runs inside your network. Gnani AI is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and ISO 27001 certified, and is HIPAA, GDPR and PCI-DSS compliant, with cloud, private cloud, on-premise and air-gapped deployment options described on the
