### TL;DR
Voice biometrics in banking verifies a caller from the physical and behavioural characteristics of their voice instead of something they have to remember. A voiceprint is captured once at enrolment, stored as a numerical vector, and compared against live speech on every later call. It removes the security question and the one-time password from the authentication step, which is where most contact centre fraud and most customer friction both live. The deciding factors in a deployment are the match threshold, the anti-spoof layer and the fallback path, not the headline accuracy figure on a vendor slide.
### What voice biometrics in banking actually checks
A voiceprint is not a recording. It is a numerical representation of traits that distinguish one speaker from another: vocal tract length, pitch range, nasality, cadence, articulation habits. The system extracts those traits, stores the vector, and later compares a fresh sample against it to produce a similarity score.
That is a different job from understanding what was said. Speech recognition answers "what are the words". Speaker verification answers "is this the same person". Gnani AI separates the two:
Gnani Prisma v2.5
handles speech to text, and Gnani Biometrics handles verification, anti-spoofing and synthetic-speech detection. Gnani AI reports that its biometrics layer extracts more than 300 voice features per call and supports cross-lingual enrolment, so a customer enrolled speaking Hindi can be verified speaking English. The product detail sits on the
enterprise platform
page.
The verification can run passively in the background while the customer explains why they called, which means the authentication step disappears from the customer's experience of the call rather than being made faster.
ENTERPRISE VOICE AI
See Gnani AI's Voice AI Agent in action
200+ Enterprises · 30M daily calls · 10 Indic languages
Book A Demo
### How a bank enrols and verifies a voiceprint
#### Enrolment sets the ceiling
Verification accuracy can never exceed the quality of the enrolment sample. Enrol a customer from a clean mobile call and then try to verify them from a noisy landline and the score drops, because the channel characteristics differ. Enrolment should happen on the channel the customer will actually use.
Two approaches exist. Passive enrolment builds the voiceprint from recorded servicing calls, with consent, which scales across an existing book quickly. Active enrolment asks the customer to repeat a phrase, which gives cleaner audio and a cleaner consent record but requires a deliberate customer moment. Most banks run passive for the back book and active at onboarding.
#### Verification is a threshold decision
On a later call, live speech is scored against the stored voiceprint and the score is compared with a threshold. Set the threshold high and genuine customers get rejected. Set it low and impostors get through. That trade-off is the whole design, and it is why a vendor's fraud detection rate quoted on its own tells you very little. Gnani AI reports a 99%+ fraud detection rate and verification in under five seconds for Gnani Biometrics. Ask any vendor, including this one, for the false rejection rate measured at the same threshold on the same audio, because the two numbers only mean something together.
#### Text dependent and text independent
Text dependent verification uses a fixed phrase. It needs less audio and is simpler to implement, and it is also easier to attack with a recording. Text independent verification works on whatever the customer happens to say, which is harder to replay but needs more speech before it reaches a confident score. A common pattern is text independent for routine servicing and text dependent for high-value transactions, with step-up authentication layered on top.
### Why passwords, security questions and OTPs keep failing
Knowledge-based authentication fails because the knowledge is not private. Date of birth, mother's maiden name, last transaction amount and registered address can be looked up, socially engineered or bought. A one-time password shifts the problem to the device: it fails when the customer has no signal, when the SIM has been swapped, and most often when a fraudster on another line is talking the customer through reading the code out loud.
Voice biometrics changes what is being checked rather than making the same check harder. The comparison below sets out how the three methods differ on the dimensions that matter in a contact centre.

The operational effect shows up in handle time. Gnani AI reports a 40 second reduction in average handle time and a 20%+ improvement in customer satisfaction where passive verification replaces a scripted security questionnaire. On a large contact centre those seconds compound into a meaningful capacity change.
### What voice biometrics in banking does not solve
Three failure modes deserve honest treatment before a deployment, because each one produces a real customer at a real branch.
Illness and voice change.
A heavy cold, a sore throat or a dental procedure shifts the acoustic profile enough to depress the score. The system needs a fallback path that does not humiliate the customer.
Channel mismatch.
A customer enrolled on a handset and calling from a car speakerphone presents a materially different signal. Good systems compensate; none compensates perfectly.
Synthetic and cloned speech.
Voice cloning from a few seconds of public audio is now cheap. Verification without an anti-spoof and deepfake detection layer is verification against an attack that no longer requires skill. Gnani AI lists anti-spoof and deepfake detection as part of its biometrics product rather than as an add-on.
The fallback matters as much as the primary path. A customer who fails verification should land in a defined step-up flow with a human who has the context, not back at the start of the queue. Support for that agent is covered on the
real-time agent assist
### Consent, DPDP and handling biometric data
A voiceprint is biometric personal data. Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act it carries obligations on notice, consent, purpose limitation, retention and breach reporting, and RBI guidance applies to the bank's technology and outsourcing arrangements on top of that. Consent for a recorded call is not automatically consent to derive and store a biometric template from it, which is the point most programmes get wrong.
Three practical requirements follow. Capture consent for enrolment explicitly and separately, in the language the customer is being served in. Define a retention and deletion path for voiceprints, including what happens when a customer closes the account. And decide where the templates live: Gnani AI supports cloud, private cloud, on-premise and air-gapped deployment, with the fully sovereign configuration described on the
Artha sovereign AI stack
page. Gnani AI is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and ISO 27001 certified, and HIPAA, GDPR and PCI-DSS compliant.
Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
### How to evaluate a voice biometrics vendor
Test on your own call recordings
, in your own languages, across the channel mix you actually receive. A benchmark run on clean studio audio predicts nothing about an 8kHz line.
Ask for false acceptance and false rejection rates at the same threshold
, and for the threshold itself. A single accuracy number is not an answer.
Test the anti-spoof layer with current cloning tools
, not with a recording played back from a phone speaker.
Check cross-lingual enrolment
if your customers switch languages between calls, which in India they routinely do.
Review the fallback design
end to end, including what the agent sees when verification fails.
Confirm deployment mode and data residency
against your own regulatory position before the commercial conversation.
### Where this leaves the password
Voice biometrics in banking has moved from a differentiator to an expectation in contact centres that handle volume. The authentication step was always the part of the call that served the bank rather than the customer, and passive verification removes it without removing the control. Gnani AI reports more than 200 enterprise deployments across BFSI and other regulated sectors. Sector-specific detail sits on the
agentic AI for banking
page, and related deployments are collected on the
customer stories
### Frequently asked questions
What is voice biometrics in banking?
It is caller verification based on the physical and behavioural characteristics of a person's voice. The bank captures a voiceprint once at enrolment, stores it as a numerical vector rather than as audio, and compares live speech against it on later calls to produce a similarity score. It replaces security questions and one-time passwords at the authentication step.
Is voice biometrics safer than a password or an OTP?
It depends on configuration. The match threshold, the anti-spoof layer and the fallback path decide the real security level. Voice biometrics removes the attacks that work against knowledge and device factors, such as social engineering of security answers and SIM swap, and introduces a different one, synthetic speech, which needs a deepfake detection layer to counter.
Can a recording or a cloned voice defeat voice biometrics?
A plain replay is defeated by liveness and anti-spoof checks. Cloned speech is the harder problem, and cloning from a few seconds of public audio is now inexpensive. Any deployment without an explicit anti-spoof and deepfake detection layer should be treated as incomplete rather than merely imperfect.
What happens if a customer has a cold?
Illness shifts the acoustic profile and depresses the similarity score, so some genuine customers will fail verification. The system needs a defined step-up path that routes the customer to a human with full context rather than back to the start of the queue.
How long does verification take?
Gnani AI reports verification in under five seconds for Gnani Biometrics, running passively while the customer explains why they called, so the authentication step does not add time to the call.
Does a bank need separate consent to enrol a voiceprint?
Consent to record a call is not the same as consent to derive and store a biometric template from it. Under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, enrolment consent should be captured explicitly and separately, in the language the customer is being served in, with a defined retention and deletion path. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.

### TL;DR
An AI voice assistant built for enterprise work is a different system from the assistant on a phone. Consumer assistants answer one question at a time for one signed-in user. An enterprise AI voice assistant runs outbound and inbound calls at contact centre volume, authenticates the caller, follows a regulated script, writes back to a CRM and hands off to a human with the conversation history intact. The distinction stopped being theoretical in September 2026, when Google retired Google Assistant on Android, Wear OS and its smart home devices and moved users to Gemini. Teams that scoped a voice programme around the old consumer assistant now need to re-evaluate.
### What changed in 2026
Google shut down Google Assistant on 4 September 2026 and replaced it with Gemini across Android, Wear OS and compatible home devices. Assistant survives only on older Android 8.1 and Android Go handsets.
Gemini is a capable general assistant. It reasons across text, images and voice, it handles open-ended questions well, and for the everyday tasks people actually ask a phone to do it is a clear step up from what it replaced. Credit where it is due: for consumer search, drafting and device control, a general assistant of that class is the right tool.
That is not the same job as running a collections campaign across two million borrowers in nine languages. Consumer assistants are designed around a single signed-in user on a single device. Enterprise voice work starts from a call list, a compliance script, a telephony carrier and an audit trail.

### What an enterprise AI voice assistant has to survive in India
#### Code-mixed speech is the default, not the edge case
A borrower in Pune switches between Marathi, Hindi and English inside a single sentence. A model trained on clean monolingual audio treats that as noise.
Gnani Prisma v2.5
is trained on 14M+ hours of real telephonic audio and reports 96% code-switching accuracy across Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish, with under 4% WER on Indian speech, according to Gnani AI's published model documentation.
#### Telephony audio is not studio audio
Enterprise calls arrive at 8kHz over a carrier network, compressed, with background noise and dropped packets. Benchmarks run on clean 16kHz recordings do not predict performance on that signal. Gnani AI reports Prisma v2.5 ranking first in 8 of 9 Indian languages on Kathbath Noisy 8kHz. When you compare any two vendors here, check that both measured on the same audio conditions, because results on clean studio audio and results on noisy telephony do not compare directly.
#### Volume and concurrency decide the architecture
A mid-size NBFC runs millions of outbound attempts a month, concentrated into legally permitted calling windows. That is a concurrency problem before it is an AI problem. Gnani AI reports 35,000+ simultaneous streams and 30M+ daily voice interactions across 200+ enterprise deployments. Response latency in live conversations runs under 800ms on
Gnani Agents
.
### How to evaluate an AI voice assistant before you commit
#### Run the pilot on your own recordings
Vendor demos use audio the vendor chose. Hand every shortlisted vendor the same 500 anonymised calls from your own queue, covering your worst accents, your noisiest lines and your most code-mixed speakers. Score word error rate, intent accuracy and containment on that set. De-identify the recordings before they leave your environment, and confirm the data-sharing terms with your legal team first.
#### Check deployment mode against your regulator
An RBI-regulated lender, an IRDAI-regulated insurer and a hospital handling patient data each face different constraints on where audio can be processed. Gnani AI offers cloud, private cloud, on-premise and air-gapped deployment, and
Artha
runs the full stack on infrastructure the customer controls. Ask every vendor the same question: where does the audio physically go, and who can read it.
#### Test the handoff as carefully as the happy path
The call that matters is the one the assistant cannot finish. Does the human agent receive the transcript, the intent, the sentiment and the account context, or does the customer repeat themselves from the top?
Gnani Assist
carries that context into the live agent conversation and handles the post-call summary.
### Mistakes teams make when they move off a consumer assistant
Assuming a general assistant's language list maps to production telephony performance. Model-level language support and production ASR quality on 8kHz call audio are different claims.
Scoping only inbound. Most of the measurable return in BFSI sits in outbound collections, renewals and verification.
Skipping the AI disclosure. Voice agents have to tell the customer they are talking to an AI, and that line belongs in the script from day one.
Treating consent and DND as a later problem. TRAI rules on outbound telephony shape the dialler logic, not the launch checklist.
Measuring accuracy without measuring containment. A model can transcribe well and still fail to close the conversation.
### Where this leaves a buyer
Choosing an AI voice assistant for enterprise work comes down to four questions. Does it handle your languages on your audio quality. Does it hold up at your concurrency. Can it deploy where your regulator requires. Does it hand off cleanly to a human. A consumer assistant was never built to answer those, and after September 2026 the most widely deployed one is no longer available in its old form at all.
Gnani AI does not publish pricing, which is a real disadvantage when you are building a business case early and need a number before a sales conversation. You can see the model specifications on the
models page
, read the deployment detail across
the solutions
, or go straight to
the developer documentation
and test the APIs yourself.
### Frequently asked questions
Is Google Assistant still available in 2026?
No. Google retired Google Assistant on 4 September 2026 across Android, Wear OS and its smart home devices, and replaced it with Gemini. It remains only on older handsets running Android 8.1 or earlier, and on Android Go.
Can a consumer AI voice assistant run contact centre campaigns?
Not as designed. Consumer assistants are built around a single signed-in user responding to prompts on a device. Contact centre work needs outbound dialling against a call list, carrier integration, per-call compliance scripting, concurrency in the tens of thousands and an audit trail. Those are enterprise platform features rather than assistant features.
What languages does an enterprise AI voice assistant need in India?
More than a language list suggests. Gnani AI supports 40+ languages at model level with 10+ Indic languages in production ASR, and the harder requirement is code-switching, where speakers mix two or three languages inside one sentence. Ask vendors for accuracy on code-mixed telephony audio specifically, not for a count of supported languages.
How long does it take to deploy an AI voice assistant?
Gnani AI reports under 20 minutes to go live on Gnani Agents for a standard configuration. A regulated deployment with core banking integration, custom vocabulary and a compliance review takes considerably longer, and the integration work rather than the model is usually what sets the timeline.
What should I measure during an AI voice assistant pilot?
Word error rate on your own audio, intent accuracy, containment rate, average handle time, and the quality of the human handoff. Containment matters most commercially, because a conversation the assistant closes without a human is the one that changes your cost per contact.
Does an enterprise AI voice assistant have to disclose it is AI?
Yes, and it should regardless of jurisdiction. Gnani AI requires the disclosure in every voice agent script. Rules on automated calling, consent and DND vary by regulator, so confirm the specific obligations with your legal and compliance team before deployment.

Curious how empowering every team member to build their own AI agent could transform productivity and innovation? Let’s dive in and explore the future of work with personal AI agents!
### From Chatbots to Co-Workers: The Evolution of Team-Built AI Agents
The journey of AI agents began with simple programs designed to mimic human machines that could think, leading to the creation of foundational systems that could follow logical rules and even simulate dialogue, though these early agents were limited to pre-programmed responses and narrow tasks.As technology advanced, AI agents evolved from basic chatbots to sophisticated systems capable of learning from user interactions, adapting to individual needs, and making complex decisions. The introduction of digital assistants and smart home devices marked a turning point, embedding AI agents into daily life and workplace routines. These agents became more proactive, personalized, and capable of understanding context, fundamentally changing how teams interact with technology.The ability for every team member to build their own agent is rooted in this rich history of innovation. Modern tools allow individuals to create custom agents tailored to unique workflows and business needs, enabling greater efficiency and adaptability. This democratization of agent-building empowers teams to automate tasks, personalize solutions, and drive continuous improvement, reflecting how far agentic AI has come from its humble beginnings.
### How Democratized GenAI Drives Efficiency and Engagement
The modern business landscape is a dynamic and often unpredictable arena. Characterized by rapid technological advancements, constant market shifts, and the ever-increasing demand for hyper-personalized experiences, organizations are constantly seeking innovative ways to gain a competitive edge. In this environment, Generative AI (GenAI) has emerged not merely as a futuristic concept, but as a tangible and powerful tool with the potential to revolutionize how businesses operate, interact with their customers, and drive efficiency across all levels.However, the prevailing approach to AI deployment within many organizations still adheres to a traditional, top-down model. This involves centralized control, where access to AI development and implementation is restricted to specialized teams such as IT departments, centralized innovation labs, and data science teams. While these teams undoubtedly possess the technical expertise necessary to build and manage complex AI systems, this centralized approach often creates bottlenecks and fails to fully leverage the transformative potential of GenAI across the entire organization.At Inya.ai, we champion a different paradigm: the democratization of AI. We firmly believe that to truly unlock the power of GenAI and thrive in environment, businesses must empower every employee, regardless of their technical background, to build, test, and deploy AI agents tailored to their specific needs and workflows. This fundamental shift in how organizations approach AI adoption is not just a matter of technological advancement; it's a strategic imperative that can lead to significant improvements in efficiency, innovation, employee engagement, and ultimately, business success.
### The Crippling Limitations of Centralized AI Development
The traditional model of centralized AI development, while seemingly efficient in its control, often proves to be a significant impediment to widespread AI adoption and the realization of its full potential. This bottleneck arises primarily from the inherent disconnect between the technical expertise of the central AI teams and the deep, nuanced understanding of day-to-day operations held by frontline employees.Consider the typical AI development lifecycle in a centralized model. Business users identify a problem or an opportunity for automation and submit a request to the central AI team. This request then enters a queue, often competing with numerous other projects across different departments. The AI team, lacking direct experience with the specific workflow in question, must then engage in a time-consuming process of gathering requirements, understanding the context, and translating the business need into a technical specification. This back-and-forth communication can lead to misunderstandings, lost nuances, and ultimately, a solution that may not perfectly address the original problem.The consequences of this centralized approach are manifold and can significantly hinder an organization's ability to leverage AI effectively:
Delays:
Business users often face frustrating delays, waiting weeks or even months for an AI-powered solution to their problems. This protracted development cycle can stifle innovation and prevent teams from responding quickly to evolving market demands or customer needs.
Lost Context:
The intricacies and nuances of frontline work are often lost in translation as requirements are relayed from business users to the central AI team. This can result in AI agents that are technically sound but lack the contextual awareness to be truly effective in real-world scenarios.
Limited Use Cases:
Centralized AI teams typically prioritize the top 5–10 use cases deemed most strategic by leadership. This leaves a vast landscape of potential AI applications within individual teams and workflows untapped, limiting the overall impact of AI adoption across the organization.
Burnout:
The overwhelming demand from various departments can quickly lead to burnout within the central AI teams. These teams become stretched thin, struggling to keep pace with the influx of requests, ultimately stalling the overall growth and implementation of AI initiatives.The stark reality of this bottleneck is highlighted by a McKinsey report, which found that a mere 15% of AI use cases successfully move beyond the pilot phase. A significant contributing factor to this low success rate is the implementation delays and the misalignment between centrally developed AI solutions and the actual operational needs of the business users.The key takeaway is clear: to truly scale AI and unlock its transformative potential, organizations must move away from an "AI-for-the-few" model and embrace an "AI-for-everyone" approach.
### Unleashing the Power of Domain Expertise Through User-Built Agents
When frontline employees are empowered to build their own AI agents, organizations tap into a wealth of real-time domain expertise that is simply inaccessible to centralized AI teams. These individuals possess an intimate understanding of:
Pain Points:
They experience firsthand the daily frustrations and inefficiencies within their workflows.
Process Inefficiencies:
They have a deep understanding of the bottlenecks and areas for improvement within their specific tasks and responsibilities.
Customer Behaviors:
Those in customer-facing roles possess invaluable insights into customer needs, preferences, and common challenges.
Operational Metrics:
They are directly involved in tracking and managing key performance indicators relevant to their specific functions.By giving these employees, the ability to build AI agents tailored to their specific needs, organizations unlock a multitude of benefits:
Faster Identification of Use Cases: Frontline employees are best positioned to identify opportunities for AI-powered automation and assistance within their daily tasks. This leads to a more rapid and relevant identification of high impact use cases.
More Accurate Workflows: Agents built by those closest to the work are inherently more aligned with the actual processes and nuances of the tasks they are designed to assist with, leading to more accurate and effective workflows.
Higher Adoption Rates: When employees build their own tools, they are more likely to trust and adopt them, leading to higher rates of AI utilization across the organization.
### Real-World Examples of User-Built Agents in Action:
The power of empowering every team member to build their own agents becomes tangible when we examine real-world applications across different departments:
#### Sales Teams:
Problem:
Sales representatives spend a significant amount of time on repetitive lead qualification tasks, manually sifting through inbound inquiries to identify promising leads.
Agent:
A conversational AI agent can be built by sales team members to automatically score inbound leads based on their responses to a predefined set of qualifying questions. This agent can then seamlessly sync qualified leads to the CRM system, freeing up sales representatives to focus on engaging with high-potential prospects.
Impact:
This can lead to up to 30% faster lead response times and a significant increase in conversion rates due to efficient prioritization of qualified leads.
#### Customer Support:
Customer support agents often waste valuable time searching through extensive knowledge bases to find relevant information to address customer inquiries.
A contextual AI assistant can be built by support agents to surface top FAQs, relevant company policies, or product guides based on the specific ticket category and the language used by the customer.
This can result in a 40–60% reduction in average handling time (AHT), leading to improved customer satisfaction and increased agent efficiency.
#### Marketing:
Marketing teams often face the time-consuming task of manually reviewing campaign performance data across various platforms to identify trends and optimization opportunities.
An analytics bot can be built by marketing team members to automatically track key performance indicators (KPIs) such as click-through rates (CTR), cost per lead (CPL), and engagement metrics across different marketing channels. This agent can then send weekly summaries and provide actionable optimization tips directly to the marketing team.
This enables faster iteration cycles, data-driven decision-making, and ultimately, a better return on investment (ROI) on advertising spend.
#### Human Resources (HR):
HR staff often spend a significant amount of time answering repetitive employee queries related to benefits, leave policies, onboarding procedures, and other common HR-related topics.
A virtual HR assistant can be built by HR team members to handle these frequently asked questions, providing employees with instant access to the information they need.
This can lead to a 70% deflection of low-value tickets from HR staff, freeing up their time to focus on more strategic and complex employee-related matters.
### Inya.ai: The No-Code GenAI Platform Empowering Everyone to Build
At Inya.ai, we have developed a no-code GenAI platform specifically designed to remove the traditional barriers to AI agent creation. Our platform is more than just another automation tool; it's a comprehensive GenAI-native environment where building intelligent agents is intuitive, accessible, and scalable across all departments within an organization.
#### Key Capabilities of the Inya.ai Platform:
Drag-and-Drop Visual Builder:
Our platform features an intuitive, drag-and-drop visual interface that allows users to create complex logic flows, integrate prompts, and add robust fallback mechanisms without writing a single line of code. This visual approach makes agent building accessible to individuals with no prior programming experience.
400+ Customizable Templates:
To accelerate the agent building process and provide users with a solid foundation, our agent marketplace offers a library of over 400 pre-built and customizable templates designed for various use cases across sales, support, marketing, logistics, finance, and HR. This eliminates the need for users to start from scratch and provides them with best-practice blueprints.
Live Voice & Chat Testing:
Our platform allows users to test their agents in real-time through both voice and chat interfaces. This live testing capability enables users to simulate conversations, identify potential issues, and optimize the agent's flow and responses instantly, ensuring a seamless user experience.
Function Calling & API Integration:
Inya.ai agents can be seamlessly integrated with other business systems through function calling and API integrations. This allows agents to trigger actions such as updating CRM fields, sending automated emails, retrieving data from external databases, and more, making them deeply embedded within existing operational workflows.
Analytics Dashboard:
Our platform provides a comprehensive analytics dashboard that allows users to measure key performance indicators such as AI agent usage, success rates, user dropout points, and overall ROI. This data-driven approach ensures that every agent delivers measurable value to the organization.
### The Exponential Benefits of Enabling Universal Agent Building
When the ability to build intelligent agents becomes an integral part of every employee's toolkit, organizations unlock a cascade of significant benefits that drive innovation, efficiency, and growth:
Faster Time-to-Impact:
AI Agents can be conceived, built, and deployed in a matter of hours or days, rather than weeks or months. This rapid development cycle allows teams to adapt quickly to changing business needs, market dynamics, and emerging opportunities.
More Relevant, Contextual Agents:
AI Agents built by individuals who are closest to the specific problems they are designed to solve are inherently more accurate, user-centric, and contextually aware. This leads to more effective and impactful AI solutions.
Innovation at Every Level:
Empowering team members to build their own AI agents fosters a culture of innovation throughout the organization. Employees become active problem-solvers, proactively identifying automation opportunities and creating solutions themselves.
Reduced Load on Central AI Teams:
By distributing the responsibility of building operational AI agents, organizations can significantly reduce the workload on central AI teams. This allows technical experts to focus on more complex architectural challenges, strategic AI initiatives, and ensuring overall governance and security.
Increased Employee Engagement:
The ability to build and deploy their own AI-powered tools is inherently empowering for employees. It fosters a sense of ownership, builds confidence in their problem-solving abilities, and increases overall job satisfaction and engagement.
Cross-Org AI Literacy:
When non-technical teams actively engage in building AI agents, they gain practical exposure to fundamental AI concepts such as prompt engineering, large language models (LLMs), natural language processing (NLP), and data mapping. This hands-on experience leads to a higher level of organizational AI literacy over time.
Lower Costs:
By empowering internal users to build their own AI agent for specific use cases, organizations can significantly reduce their reliance on costly external AI consultants for every small automation need. This lowers operational costs and maximizes the utilization of internal talent and capabilities.Navigating Risk and Ensuring Governance in a Decentralized AI LandscapeWhile the benefits of democratizing AI Agent are substantial, organizations must also address the potential risks associated with a decentralized approach. At Inya.ai, we understand these concerns and have built robust tools and features into our platform to support safe and responsible AI democratization.
### Key Risk Areas and Inya.ai's Mitigation Strategies:
RiskHow Inya.ai HelpsData PrivacyRole-based access controls, robust data encryption protocols, and adherence to global compliance standards such as GDPR and SOC2.Inconsistent QualityBest-practice workflows embedded within the platform, version control for agent iterations, guided testing frameworks, and customizable templates.Duplicate AgentsA centralized agent repository with advanced search and tagging functionalities, coupled with an administrator approval process for new agents.Lack of GovernanceComprehensive admin dashboards providing visibility into agent usage and performance, customizable performance thresholds for quality assurance.Skill GapsBuilt-in onboarding tutorials, contextual tips and guidance within the platform, and 24/7 support resources for users of all technical levels.
### Fostering a New Era of Human + AI Agent Collaboration
The goal of empowering every team member to build their own AI agent is not to replace human employees with machines. Instead, it is to amplify human capabilities and foster a new era of seamless collaboration between humans and AI.When every employee can build and leverage AI agents, they transition from:
Manual to Automated:
Automating repetitive and time-consuming tasks, freeing up human intellect for more strategic and creative endeavors.
Reactive to Proactive:
Leveraging AI-powered insights and predictions to anticipate challenges and proactively address them.
Frustrated to Empowered:
Gaining control over their workflows and having the tools to solve their own problems efficiently.In this future of work, AI becomes an intuitive extension of human creativity, decision-making, and problem-solving, augmenting human potential rather than acting as a replacement.
Conclusion: Embracing Distributed Intelligence for a Brighter Future
The era of centralized AI development is rapidly ending. Organizations that recognize the transformative power of distributed intelligence and empower every team member to build their own intelligent agents will be the ones to thrive in the years to come. These forward-thinking organizations will benefit from:
Faster Innovation Cycles:
Driven by the collective intelligence and problem-solving capabilities of their entire workforce.
Leaner and More Efficient Operations:
Through the widespread automation of routine tasks and optimization of workflows.
Superior Customer Experiences:
Delivered through AI agents that are deeply attuned to specific customer needs and contexts.
A More Engaged and AI-Literate Workforce:
Empowered by the ability to shape their own work environment and contribute to the organization's AI-driven future.With innovative platforms like Inya.ai, the ability to build operational, intelligent AI agents is no longer the exclusive domain of data scientists and technical experts. It belongs to everyone within the organization. This is not just the future of AI; it is the future of work itself: autonomous and empowered teams, augmented by the intelligence of AI, working collaboratively to achieve unprecedented levels of success.
#### FAQs
#### What is an AI agent and how can employees use them?
AI agents are autonomous digital tools that automate tasks, answer questions, and streamline workflows. Employees can use them to quickly access information, automate repetitive work, and improve productivity.
#### How does empowering every team member to build AI agents benefit the business?
It increases operational efficiency, reduces costs, and allows employees to focus on high-value tasks. Businesses also benefit from improved decision-making, scalability, and enhanced customer and employee experiences.
#### Do team members need technical skills to build their own AI agents?
Modern AI platforms are increasingly user-friendly, enabling employees without deep technical backgrounds to create and customize agents for their specific needs.

Agents can handle HR queries, IT support requests, onboarding, payroll processing, scheduling, data analysis, and more-freeing up staff for strategic work.
#### How do AI agent improve the employee experience?
They provide instant support, reduce workplace friction, and personalize assistance, leading to higher satisfaction and engagement.
#### Are there risks or challenges in letting everyone build AI agents?
Potential challenges include ensuring data security, maintaining quality control, and providing adequate training so agents align with company policies and standards.Ready to empower your team with intelligent, no-code AI agents?

### From Chatbots to Agents: The Evolution of Enterprise Conversations
Chatbots were built for containment. Their goal was to automate FAQs, reduce call volumes, and deflect tickets. They relied on rules, scripts, and rigid flows. When users stepped outside those boundaries, conversations broke.

Chatbots are limited by three core design flaws:
Rule rigidity:
They depend on predefined paths. If a query doesn’t match, they fail.
Context blindness:
They treat every conversation as isolated. No understanding of past interactions or customer state.
Action paralysis:
They can respond with text but cannot trigger complex backend actions independently.

### What is conversational AI in retail?
Conversational AI in retail is software that handles shopper and customer service conversations in natural language across voice, chat, WhatsApp and SMS, and completes the task being asked about rather than only answering questions. It covers order tracking, returns, stock and delivery queries, and post-purchase support, at a scale no staffed desk matches.
The useful version of the definition includes that last clause. A system that explains the returns policy is a search box with better manners. A system that checks eligibility, raises the return, books the pickup and confirms the refund window has done the work.
### Why does retail need conversational AI now rather than more agents?
Retail contact volume is seasonal in a way headcount cannot be. Festive peaks, sale events and delivery disruptions produce contact spikes of several times baseline over a few days, and a team sized for the peak is idle for the rest of the year.
The second pressure is language. An Indian retailer serving customers beyond the metros is fielding conversations in Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Marathi, Bengali and code-mixed varieties of each, often in the same call. Staffing that mix in every region is expensive, and it is the constraint that keeps regional support thin.
The third is that most of the volume is not judgment work. Order status, delivery slot changes, return eligibility and refund timing are rule-governed queries with a correct answer sitting in a system the customer cannot see.
### Which retail use cases does conversational AI actually handle?
The use cases that work are the ones where the answer already exists in a system and the conversation is the only missing interface. The table below maps the common ones against the channel that suits each.

#### Order tracking and delivery queries
Order status is the highest-volume retail query and the easiest to automate end to end. The agent authenticates the caller, reads the current status from the order management system, and offers the next action, which is usually a delivery slot change rather than an escalation.
#### Returns and refunds
Returns are where conversational AI earns its keep, because the policy logic is explicit and the customer is anxious. An agent that checks eligibility against the purchase date and category, raises the return, books the reverse pickup and states the refund window resolves the whole interaction in one pass.
#### Peak-season surge support
Surge capacity is a structural argument rather than a per-conversation one. Automated channels absorb a spike without a hiring cycle, which changes what a retailer can promise during a sale event. Gnani AI reports that its platform sustains more than 35,000 simultaneous streams and handles over 30 million daily voice interactions across its deployments.
#### Outbound engagement and win-back
Abandoned carts, replenishment reminders and loyalty renewals are outbound conversations rather than inbound ones, and they are governed by consent rules rather than queue capacity. Gnani AI lists outbound engagement among the published use cases for
Gnani Agents
.
### How does multilingual support work at Indian retail scale?
It works when the speech models are trained on the audio retail actually produces, which is noisy 8kHz telephony with code-mixing, not clean studio recordings. That distinction decides whether a regional-language deployment is usable or an experiment.
Gnani AI reports that
Prisma v2.5
, its speech to text model, is trained on more than 14 million hours of real telephonic audio, supports ten or more Indic languages in production along with Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish code-switching, and reaches 96% code-switching accuracy. It reports first place in eight of nine Indian languages on the Kathbath Noisy 8kHz benchmark.
On the output side, Gnani AI reports a mean opinion score of 4.23 on 8kHz telephony for
Timbre v2.5
, its text to speech model, which is currently labelled Beta. Timbre handles lakh and crore cadence, Indian names and numerals, which is the difference between a price read correctly and a price read as a foreign number.
Benchmark figures measured under different audio conditions do not compare directly across vendors. A word error rate on noisy 8kHz telephony is a different measurement from one on clean 16kHz studio audio.
### Does conversational AI have to tell shoppers it is AI?
Yes. Gnani AI's standard is that every voice agent discloses it is AI within the script, at the start of the conversation, and that rule applies to retail deployments the same as to regulated ones.
Two further obligations apply to Indian retail. The
DPDP Act
covers all personal data of Indian customers, and that includes call recordings, transcripts and call metadata, not only the order record.
TRAI
rules govern outbound telephony, including consent and DND registration, which bear directly on cart-abandonment and replenishment campaigns.
Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
### What should a retailer measure after rolling out conversational AI?
Measure containment first, meaning the share of contacts the automated path resolves without a human. It is the one number that tells you whether the deployment removed work or merely moved it.
Then measure three more. First-contact resolution shows whether the automation finished the job or created a callback. Average handle time on the escalated remainder shows whether human agents are getting the hard cases with context or without it. Customer satisfaction on automated conversations, scored rather than surveyed, shows whether the experience held.
Scoring every conversation rather than a sample is what

It is software that handles shopper and customer service conversations in natural language across voice, chat, WhatsApp and SMS, and completes the task being asked about rather than only answering questions. It covers order tracking, returns, stock and delivery queries, and post-purchase support.

Order tracking and delivery status, returns and refunds, stock and availability checks, loyalty and renewals, and outbound cart or replenishment follow-ups. These are rule-governed queries whose answer already sits in a system the customer cannot see, which is what makes them automatable end to end.
Which retail conversations should still go to a human?
Complaints involving goodwill decisions and fraud or chargeback disputes. Both need judgment, discretionary spend or regulated evidence handling, so the better pattern is to escalate them to a human agent with full conversation context rather than automate them.
How does conversational AI handle Indian languages and code-mixing?
It depends on whether the speech models were trained on telephony audio rather than studio audio. Yes. Gnani AI's standard is that every voice agent discloses it is AI within the script at the start of the conversation. For outbound retail campaigns this sits alongside TRAI consent and DND obligations, and the DPDP Act covers call recordings, transcripts and call metadata as personal data.
How does conversational AI help during festive and sale peaks?
Automated channels absorb a contact spike without a hiring cycle, which is a structural benefit rather than a per-conversation one. Gnani AI reports that its platform sustains more than 35,000 simultaneous streams and handles over 30 million daily voice interactions across its deployments.

### What voicebot technology has to get right before a voice sounds human
TL;DR:
Voicebot technology sounds human when four things line up: speech synthesis with context-appropriate prosody, response latency low enough that pauses feel conversational, reliable barge-in so the caller can interrupt, and a persona consistent enough that the voice does not change character mid-call. Voice quality alone does not carry it. A perfectly natural voice that takes two seconds to answer and cannot be interrupted still reads as a machine, and on Indian telephony the audio is 8kHz and often code-switched, so a model tuned for clean English studio audio degrades exactly where enterprise calls live.
Callers form a judgement in the first few seconds and then behave accordingly. A caller who believes they are talking to a machine shortens their sentences, repeats themselves, and starts looking for the escape route to a human. A caller who believes the conversation is working explains the actual problem. The commercial consequence of that difference shows up in containment rate and first-call resolution rather than in any voice quality score.
This matters alongside, not instead of, disclosure. A voice agent should tell the caller it is AI. Sounding human is about removing friction from the conversation, not about concealing what the caller is speaking to.
### The four components of perceived humanness
#### Prosody that matches context
Prosody covers rhythm, stress and intonation. The same sentence delivered with support warmth and with collections firmness carries different meaning, and a synthesis engine that applies one flat register to both sounds wrong in at least one of them. Gnani AI reports context-aware prosody in
Gnani Timbre v2.5 (Beta)
, with an empathetic register for support and an assertive one for collections.
For Indian deployments, prosody also has to handle numerals the way callers say them. Lakh and crore cadence, Indian name pronunciation and Hindi-English code-switching inside a single sentence are the specific places where a general-purpose engine gives itself away.
#### Latency inside the conversational window
Human turn-taking leaves a gap of a few hundred milliseconds. Stretch that gap and the caller starts talking over the agent or assumes the line has dropped. Latency is the component teams most often underinvest in, because it is invisible in a demo recording and obvious on a live call.
#### Barge-in that works
Callers interrupt. They interrupt to correct a misheard account number, to skip a menu they have heard before, and to answer a question before it finishes. A voicebot that keeps talking through an interruption converts a minor error into a failed call. Barge-in depends on the speech recognition layer detecting speech under the agent's own output, which is a harder problem on a compressed telephony channel than in a quiet room.
#### A persona that holds
Persona is the part most teams design first and enforce least. A consistent name, register, vocabulary and level of formality across every path through the conversation is what makes the voice feel like one entity. Inconsistency usually enters through fallback prompts and error messages, which get written last and in a different voice from the main flow.
### What to measure, and what each measurement means
Perceived humanness breaks down into measurable components. The table below gives each one a definition and a reference point, so a procurement conversation can move past subjective impressions of voice quality.
Component
What it measures
Why it decides perceived humanness
Gnani AI reference point
Speech naturalness
Mean opinion score, a listener rating of how natural synthesised speech sounds.
A flat or buzzy voice is identified as synthetic within one sentence.
Timbre v2.5 (Beta): MOS 4.23 on 8kHz telephony.
Time to first audio
Delay between the response being ready and the first audio reaching the caller.
Sets the length of the pause the caller hears after they stop speaking.
Timbre v2.5 (Beta): sub-100ms time to first audio, as published on the models page.
Streaming first byte
95th percentile time to the first byte of the synthesis stream. A different measurement from time to first audio.
Determines consistency under load rather than best-case speed.
Timbre v2.5 (Beta): under 250ms p95 first byte, as published on the TTS API page.
Recognition accuracy
Word error rate on the audio conditions the deployment will actually see.
Mis-transcription breaks the response before synthesis is reached.
Prisma v2.5: under 4 percent WER on Indian speech, trained on 14M+ hours of telephonic audio.
Code-switching
Accuracy on speech that changes language mid-sentence.
Indian callers mix languages routinely. Failure here reads as the agent not listening.
Prisma v2.5: 96 percent code-switching accuracy across Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish.
End-to-end turn latency
Total time from the caller finishing to the agent starting to speak.
The single strongest cue that the caller is talking to software.
Gnani Agents: under 800ms response latency in live conversations. Warp v2.0 speech to speech: sub-200ms P95.
The measurable components of a human-sounding voicebot, with what each one means and the Gnani AI reference point. Figures measured under different conditions do not compare directly across vendors.
Two cautions on reading vendor numbers. Time to first audio and p95 first byte measure different things, so a figure for one cannot be compared against a figure for the other. Mean opinion score on clean 16kHz studio audio is not comparable to mean opinion score on 8kHz telephony, and for contact centre work only the second one predicts anything.
### Where voicebot technology breaks on Indian telephony
The gap between demo and deployment is almost always audio conditions. Enterprise calls arrive at 8kHz, compressed, with background noise and handset variation. Speech recognition trained on studio-quality English transcribes the easy parts of such a call correctly and fails on the emotionally loaded or numerically precise parts, which are the parts that determine whether the call succeeds.
Gnani AI trained
Gnani Prisma v2.5
on more than 14 million hours of real telephonic audio for this reason, and reports under 4 percent word error rate on Indian speech, 96 percent code-switching accuracy across Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish, and sub-200ms streaming latency. The published benchmark detail sits at
the Prisma v2.5 benchmarks
.
Code-switching deserves separate attention. A caller who says an account number in English inside a Hindi sentence is making a completely ordinary request that breaks any pipeline assuming one language per utterance. Handling it natively rather than through language detection and model switching removes both a failure mode and a source of latency.
### Reducing the latency budget
A conventional voice agent chains three steps: speech to text, then a language model, then text to speech. Each step adds its own latency, and the total is what the caller experiences as a pause.
Two levers shorten it. The first is streaming at every stage, so synthesis begins before the full response has been generated. Gnani AI reports WebSocket and SSE streaming at six chunks per second for Timbre v2.5 (Beta). The second is removing the intermediate text layer entirely. Gnani Warp v2.0 is a speech-to-speech model that processes audio directly with no speech-to-text and no text-to-speech stage, which Gnani AI reports at sub-200ms P95. Specifications for both sit at
Gnani AI models
Architecture choices here constrain everything above them. A persona designed for warm, unhurried delivery cannot survive a pipeline that needs a second and a half to respond.
### Designing the persona so it survives contact with real calls
Fix the register before the script.
Decide how formal the agent is, how it handles being corrected, and what it does when it does not know. These three decisions determine more of the perceived personality than the voice selection does.
Write the fallbacks in the same voice.
Error prompts, timeouts and escalation lines are where persona consistency usually collapses.
Script the disclosure naturally.
The agent discloses that it is AI, placed where it does not read as a legal notice.
Design the handoff.
When the agent escalates, the human should receive the full conversation history. Gnani AI reports context-aware handoff with complete history in
Gnani Agents
, alongside support for voice, WhatsApp, chat and SMS from one platform.
Review against recordings, not transcripts.
Transcripts hide the two failures that matter most here, which are wrong prosody and badly timed pauses.
### Compliance obligations that touch voice specifically
Voice agents must disclose that they are AI, and that disclosure belongs in the script rather than in a policy page. Outbound calling in India brings TRAI consent and DND obligations into scope. Call recordings, transcripts and call metadata are personal data under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, with RBI guidance applying to BFSI and IRDAI to insurance.
Voice cloning carries an additional obligation. Speaker embeddings are biometric data, and a cloned voice needs documented consent from the person whose voice was cloned. Where residency is binding,
the Gnani Artha sovereign stack
runs the models inside infrastructure the customer controls.
Gnani AI is SOC 2 Type 2 certified and ISO 27001 certified, and HIPAA, GDPR and PCI-DSS compliant. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.
### Where to start
Measure your current latency on live calls before changing anything else, because it bounds every other design decision. Test speech recognition on your own recorded audio rather than on a vendor sample. Then tune prosody and persona, which are the cheapest components to change and the ones most visibly wrong when the first two are already right.
Voicebot technology has moved past the point where a natural-sounding voice is the hard part. The hard part is holding that quality on compressed, noisy, multilingual calls at production volume. Implementation detail for developers sits in
the Gnani AI documentation
, and teams ready to scope a deployment can
book a demo
### Frequently asked questions
What is voicebot technology?
Voicebot technology is the stack that lets software hold a spoken conversation: speech recognition to understand the caller, a reasoning layer to decide the response, and speech synthesis to deliver it. In production the components that decide whether it works are response latency, barge-in handling and prosody, not the voice selection on its own.
What actually makes an AI voice sound human?
Four things together. Context-appropriate prosody, so the register matches the situation. Response latency inside the few-hundred-millisecond window human turn-taking uses. Reliable barge-in, so the caller can interrupt and be heard. A persona that stays consistent across every path, including error and fallback prompts, where consistency most often breaks.
Does a voicebot have to tell callers it is AI?
Yes. Voice agents disclose that they are AI, and the disclosure belongs inside the script rather than in a separate policy page. Sounding human is about removing friction from the conversation, not about concealing what the caller is speaking to. Outbound calling in India also carries TRAI consent and DND obligations.
Why do voicebots that demo well fail on real calls?
Audio conditions. Enterprise calls arrive at 8kHz, compressed and noisy, often with speech that switches language mid-sentence. Models trained on clean studio English transcribe the easy parts correctly and fail on the numerically precise or emotionally loaded parts that decide the outcome. Gnani AI trained Gnani Prisma v2.5 on more than 14 million hours of real telephonic audio for this reason.
What latency should a voice agent target?
Low enough that the pause after the caller stops speaking reads as conversational rather than as a dropped line. Gnani AI reports under 800ms response latency in live conversations for Gnani Agents, sub-200ms P95 for the Warp v2.0 speech-to-speech model, and sub-100ms time to first audio for Timbre v2.5 (Beta). Note that time to first audio and p95 first byte are different measurements and do not compare directly.
What consent is needed to clone a voice?
Speaker embeddings are biometric data, so a cloned voice requires documented consent from the person whose voice was cloned, plus a record of how the embedding is stored and deleted. In India this sits under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act. Confirm with your legal and compliance team before deployment.

### Frequently Asked Questions
What are multilingual AI agents?
Multilingual AI agents are artificial intelligence-powered tools capable of understanding and communicating in multiple languages, enabling seamless interactions with customers and users worldwide.
Why are multilingual AI agents important for global businesses?
They break down language barriers, allowing companies to serve diverse, international customer bases efficiently and inclusively. This fosters trust, enhances customer satisfaction, and opens new markets that were previously inaccessible due to language constraints.
What is a multilingual AI agent, and how is it different from a translation tool?
A multilingual AI agent is a conversational system built on large language models, speech recognition, and text to speech that can hold a full interaction in a customer's own language, across voice and text. A translation tool converts words from one language to another. An agent understands intent, retains context across turns, handles idioms, slang, and code mixed speech, and resolves the customer's request end to end. The difference matters most in spoken conversations, where accent, dialect, and mid sentence language switching break literal translation but are normal human behaviour.
What does a language barrier actually cost a global operation?
The visible costs are longer handle times, repeat contacts, and the expense of hiring and retaining multilingual staff in every market. The less visible costs are usually larger: customers abandoning a journey because support is unavailable in their language, slower internal decision making when teams work across languages, regulatory exposure when disclosures and consent are not delivered in a language the customer understands, and eroded trust that shows up later as churn. Language coverage also caps market reach and the talent pool a company can hire from.
How do multilingual AI agents handle dialects and code mixed speech?
Coverage is a spectrum, not a binary. A language may be well supported in its standard form while regional dialects, accents, and mixed language speech such as Hinglish remain harder. Handling them well depends on training data that includes the actual dialects and accents of the target market rather than only standard broadcast speech, acoustic models tuned for local telephony conditions, and ongoing evaluation against real customer audio from each region. When scoping a deployment, ask for accuracy measured on in market audio for the specific dialects you serve, not a single global average.
What privacy, security, and bias controls does a multilingual deployment need?
On privacy and security: encryption in transit and at rest, role based least privilege access, audit logging, defined retention and deletion policies, and data residency that matches each market's requirements. India's DPDP Act, GDPR in Europe, and sector specific rules such as those covering financial or health data may all apply at once in a global footprint, and consent notices should be delivered in the customer's own language. On bias: training data spread across languages, dialects, and speaker demographics, per language accuracy monitoring rather than a single aggregate metric, and human review of sensitive or high value interactions. Route production decisions through your legal and compliance teams.
How should an organisation roll out multilingual AI agents?
Start by ranking languages by business value rather than by volume alone, weighing revenue, growth, support cost, and regulatory obligation in each market. Pilot on one or two languages and a bounded set of use cases, define success metrics and a pre launch baseline for containment, resolution time, accuracy, and satisfaction, and design the escalation path to a human agent before launch rather than after. Then expand language by language, monitoring accuracy per language as you go. Two things determine whether it holds up at scale: continuous retraining against real in market conversations, and internal adoption, which usually needs training and visible early wins to overcome resistance from the teams whose work changes.

45% in 2024 to a projected 41% by 2026

75% of customers prefer to buy products in their native language
, and

### Understanding Multilingual AI Agents: Beyond Simple Translation
Multilingual AI agents represent a quantum leap beyond traditional translation tools and basic voice bots. These sophisticated systems combine natural language processing, machine learning, and cultural intelligence to create authentic, context-aware interactions in multiple languages simultaneously. Unlike conventional translation services that work on a word-by-word basis, multilingual AI agents understand intent, emotion, and cultural context to deliver responses that feel natural and culturally appropriate.

Advanced neural networks process incoming queries in real-time, identifying not just the language but also regional dialects, colloquialisms, and cultural references. Machine learning algorithms continuously improve the system's understanding of customer preferences, shopping behaviors, and communication styles specific to different cultural contexts.
Voice AI capabilities add another dimension to multilingual support, enabling customers to interact naturally through speech in their preferred language. The
Voice AI market is projected to reach $47.5 billion by 2034
, growing at a remarkable
34.8% CAGR
, highlighting the significant investment and adoption in this technology sector. These voice-enabled systems can handle complex retail interactions, from product searches to order modifications, all while maintaining cultural sensitivity and linguistic accuracy.
Think of multilingual AI agents as having three distinct layers of intelligence. The first layer handles basic language recognition and translation, similar to traditional tools. The second layer adds contextual understanding, recognizing shopping intent, product categories, and service requirements. The third layer incorporates cultural intelligence, adapting communication styles, product recommendations, and service approaches based on regional preferences and cultural norms.
### The Technology Stack: How Multilingual AI Agents Work
The technological foundation of multilingual AI agents involves several sophisticated components working in harmony. Natural Language Understanding (NLU) forms the core, enabling systems to comprehend customer intent regardless of the language used. This goes beyond simple keyword matching to understand context, sentiment, and underlying customer needs.
Advanced speech recognition technology processes voice inputs in multiple languages, accounting for accents, dialects, and speech patterns specific to different regions. The
AI voice recognition market is estimated to reach $44.7 billion by 2034
, reflecting the critical importance of accurate voice processing in modern customer service applications.
Real-time translation engines powered by transformer models provide instant, contextually accurate translations while preserving the original meaning and emotional tone of customer communications. Machine learning algorithms analyze customer behavior patterns, preferences, and historical interactions to provide personalized recommendations and responses. For example, when interacting with customers from cultures that value indirect communication, the AI agent automatically adopts a more consultative approach, while providing more direct, efficient responses to customers from cultures that prefer straightforward interactions.
Cost optimization

Seamless
omnichannel integration

### Industry Impact and Success Stories

Electronics and technology retailers

Think of the transformation like the difference between having a single interpreter at an international conference versus having native speakers for each delegation. 35% more likely to complete purchases
and

### The Changing Landscape of NBFC Digital Transformation
The financial services sector in India is experiencing unprecedented technological disruption, with NBFCs at the forefront of this digital revolution. Traditional banking models that once required physical presence and documentation are rapidly giving way to tech-enabled solutions that prioritize accessibility, convenience, and inclusivity.
#### The Digital Imperative for NBFCs
NBFCs have recognized that digital transformation isn't optional—it's essential for survival in today's competitive landscape.
According to a 2023 report by KPMG, 78% of Indian NBFCs have accelerated their digital transformation initiatives since 2020
, acknowledging the critical need to evolve their business models to remain relevant.
The digital transformation journey for NBFCs encompasses several key elements:
Modernization of core banking systems
Implementation of cloud-based solutions
Adoption of mobile-first strategies
Integration of advanced analytics and AI
Deployment of conversational interfaces and voice technologies
This multifaceted transformation is driven by both competitive pressures and changing customer expectations. Today's financial consumers, even in semi-urban and rural areas, expect the same level of digital convenience they experience with e-commerce and social media platforms.
#### Beyond Urban Markets: The Bharat Banking Revolution
While digital banking solutions have saturated urban markets, the real growth opportunity lies in the ongoing NBFC digital transformation aimed at serving Bharat—the vast, diverse, and largely untapped market beyond metropolitan India.
This segment, representing over 65% of the country’s population, continues to remain underbanked or unbanked despite increasing smartphone penetration and internet connectivity. To unlock this opportunity, NBFCs are embracing
vernacular voice tech
as a key enabler of
financial inclusion
, allowing them to connect with customers in their native languages and deliver personalized, accessible financial services at scale.
The Bharat banking revolution is characterized by:
Localized financial products designed for semi-urban and rural needs
Simplified user interfaces that accommodate varying levels of digital literacy
Multilingual support across India's diverse linguistic landscape
Voice-first approaches that overcome literacy barriers
Community-based distribution models leveraging local trust networks
NBFCs have recognized that capturing this market requires more than just translating existing apps—it demands a fundamental rethinking of how financial services are delivered and experienced.

Voice technology represents perhaps the most transformative innovation in making financial services accessible to all Indians, regardless of literacy level or technological proficiency.
#### Why Voice Is the Natural Interface for Bharat
For millions of Indians, especially in rural and semi-urban areas, voice represents the most intuitive and natural way to interact with technology. This is particularly true for the following reasons:
Linguistic diversity accommodation
: Voice technology can adapt to India's 22 official languages and hundreds of dialects far more efficiently than text-based interfaces.
Literacy barrier elimination
: With India's literacy rate at around 74%, voice interfaces enable the approximately 340 million Indians who cannot read or write to access financial services independently.
Cultural resonance
: India has a strong oral tradition, with information historically passed through spoken rather than written communication.
Reduced technological intimidation
: Voice interactions feel more human and less technological, reducing anxiety for first-time financial technology users.
Multitasking capability
: Voice allows users to access financial services while engaged in other activities, an important consideration for busy rural households.

in the
NBFC sector

.

financial services speak the customer’s language

psychological impact

Agentic AI

In the NBFC context, Agentic AI manifests as intelligent virtual assistants that can:
Understand complex financial queries in multiple Indian languages
Navigate multi-step processes while maintaining context
Make appropriate recommendations based on customer profiles
Proactively identify customer needs before they're explicitly stated
Learn from interactions to continuously improve performance
This technology enables a level of conversational sophistication that makes interactions feel genuinely human rather than robotic, a critical factor in establishing trust with customers who may be skeptical of technology.

Advanced speech recognition

Natural language understanding

Dynamic response generation

Voice biometrics

Successful implementation requires not just technological sophistication but also deep linguistic and cultural expertise.

### Real-World Impact: Use Cases Transforming NBFC Operations

The lending process, traditionally documentation-heavy and intimidating for many customers, has been dramatically streamlined through voice technology:
#### Loan Qualification
Voice assistants now guide potential borrowers through qualification processes in their native language, explaining requirements clearly and answering questions that might otherwise prevent application completion. This reduces dropout rates and expands the potential customer base.

in the customer's preferred language yield significantly higher response rates and more detailed feedback than text alternatives, providing NBFCs with crucial insights for service improvement.

#### Pre-Due Collections

Even in challenging collection scenarios, voice technology enables conversations that preserve dignity and relationship value, with AI systems capable of negotiating payment plans in the customer's language without the confrontational tone that sometimes characterizes human collections interactions.
### Strategic Advantages for NBFCs Adopting Vernacular Voice Tech
Beyond specific operational use cases, vernacular voice technology offers NBFCs several strategic advantages in an increasingly competitive market.
#### Cost Optimization Through Intelligent Automation
The economic equation for NBFCs is compelling. While implementing sophisticated voice technology requires initial investment, the returns quickly materialize through:
Reduced call center staffing requirements
Lower customer acquisition costs through improved conversion rates
Decreased operational expenses associated with paper-based processes
Minimized losses from fraud through enhanced security measures
Improved collection rates and reduced bad debt

Think of it as the difference between maintaining hundreds of physical branches across diverse linguistic regions versus operating a single, infinitely scalable system that can speak every required language. The economic advantages become even more pronounced as operations scale.
#### Enhanced Customer Experience and Loyalty

Elimination of language barriers that create frustration

Positive word-of-mouth generating new customer acquisition

### Implementation Challenges and Solutions

India's linguistic landscape presents unique challenges for voice technology deployment:

### What is a voicebot for NBFC operations?
A voicebot for NBFC operations is an AI voice agent that holds a real spoken conversation with a borrower in their own language, over an ordinary phone call, and completes a task end to end. Typical tasks are loan qualification, welcome calling, payment reminders, collections follow-up and KYC verification.
The reason this matters to a non-banking financial company is narrower than the usual automation argument. NBFCs have spent a decade building app-first journeys, and those journeys reach a specific kind of customer: literate, English-comfortable, on reliable data, willing to navigate a form. A large part of the Indian lending market is none of those things, and the fallback channel offered to them is an IVR menu. Voice AI is the first channel that serves that customer properly rather than as an exception.
### Which customers do NBFC digital channels miss?
NBFC digital channels miss the customers who can transact by speaking but not by typing. They fall into four recognisable groups, and in Indian lending they overlap heavily with the segments NBFCs most want to grow.
#### Borrowers who prefer a regional language
App journeys are usually built in English first and translated later, if at all. A borrower who is fluent in Kannada or Bengali but not in English will abandon a form and will also abandon an English IVR tree. A spoken conversation in their own language is not a convenience for this group, it is the difference between completing and dropping out.
#### Borrowers on constrained connectivity
Owning a smartphone and being able to use a data-heavy application are different things. A voice call degrades gracefully where an app does not, which makes voice the more reliable channel wherever bandwidth is inconsistent.
#### Borrowers who do not trust a screen with money
A segment of creditworthy customers will use financial products but will not complete a significant transaction without something that feels like a conversation. They are not resistant to technology, they are resistant to doing something consequential with no one to ask.
#### Borrowers with no time to sit with an app
At the other end of the income range, customers who can easily use an app often have no window in which to do it. A phone conversation runs while they commute or work. The channel wins on time, not on literacy.
### Why has voice been the last channel NBFCs automate?
Voice has been last because until recently the technology did not work on the audio NBFCs actually have. Lending calls arrive over 8kHz telephony, in noisy conditions, in a mix of languages, often switching between them inside a single sentence. Speech systems trained on clean English studio audio fail on all four counts at once.
That is a model problem rather than a product problem, which is why the gap persisted. A voice agent is only as good as the transcription underneath it: if the system mishears the borrower, routing is wrong, the retrieved answer is wrong and the disposition logged against the account is wrong.
Gnani Prisma v3.0
, Gnani AI's speech to text model, is trained and evaluated on six real telephony codecs rather than studio recordings, and Gnani AI reports a macro word error rate of 16.93 across the nine Indian languages of the Vistaar benchmark over seven datasets, measured against ElevenLabs Scribe v2 at 19.98, Microsoft Azure STT at 20.51 and Deepgram Nova 3 at 26.57. Gnani AI also reports language identification of 98% on clips longer than three seconds. Those are Gnani AI's published benchmark figures on the Vistaar benchmark and they do not compare directly with accuracy measured on clean 16kHz audio.
The previous generation model,
Gnani Prisma v2.5
, remains available and was trained on 14M+ hours of real telephonic audio, with Gnani AI reporting 96% code-switching accuracy and sub-200ms streaming latency across 10+ production languages including Hinglish, Tanglish and Benglish. Code-switching accuracy is the specific capability that makes a Hinglish collections call usable rather than noise.
### What can a voicebot actually do across the NBFC lifecycle?
A voicebot can run any NBFC workflow where the task is a structured conversation with a known outcome. That covers more of the lending lifecycle than most teams assume, and the strongest cases sit at the two ends: acquisition and recovery.
NBFC workflow
What the voice agent does
Gnani AI capability
Collections, pre-due and early-stage
Reminder call in the borrower's language, captures promise to pay, schedules follow-up
Gnani Agents, collections use case
Loan qualification
Runs initial eligibility questions conversationally and routes qualified applicants
Gnani Agents, lead qualification
Welcome calling after approval
Explains terms, due dates and repayment channel, answers first-week questions
Gnani Agents, onboarding
KYC and account servicing
Verifies the caller before any account action, with no security questions
Gnani Biometrics, passive verification
Document and repayment follow-up
Chases missing documents or failed mandates across voice, WhatsApp and SMS
Gnani Agents, omnichannel
