Section 10
### Conclusion: Rural India Speech Recognition Is Solvable, But Not Accidentally
Rural India speech recognition is not an unsolvable problem. The challenge is systemic: compounding acoustic degradation from microphone hardware, codec compression, network artifacts, and dialect mismatch, all of which standard training pipelines ignore.
Each degradation layer has a known mitigation strategy. Codec augmentation addresses the compression layer. Multi-condition noise training addresses the acoustic environment. Dialect-specific fine-tuning with LM integration addresses language mismatch. On-device LoRA adaptation addresses domain shift in production.
The Viksit Bharat voice AI deployment agenda, including Bhashini-powered IVR and Kisan e-Mitra, will succeed or fail on exactly these engineering decisions. A farmer asking about her PM-KISAN installment in a field in Bihar should receive the same speech recognition accuracy as an urban professional in a quiet office. That parity is achievable with methodical, acoustically-informed engineering.
Gnani AI’s ASR model achieving 24.94% WER on GramVaani, the most acoustically demanding rural India benchmark, is evidence that this engineering approach works. The gap between that number and the 29-37% range of global competitors is not architectural. It is methodological.
“The next billion voice AI users will not speak from quiet rooms into high-end microphones on fast networks. The speech recognition systems serving them need to be built for the conditions that actually exist, not the conditions that would make benchmarking convenient.”
FAQ
### Frequently Asked Questions: Speech Recognition in Rural India
#### Why does speech recognition fail in rural India?
Three degradation layers compound simultaneously: non-stationary rural noise at 0-10 dB SNR; single-capsule MEMS microphones at 58-62 dB(A) with no beamforming; and AMR-NB codec compression limiting audio to 200-3400 Hz on 2G networks. Most models trained on clean 16 kHz studio recordings break under this combination.
#### What is AMR-NB and why does it matter for Indian language speech recognition?
AMR-NB (Adaptive Multi-Rate Narrowband) is the dominant voice codec on 2G GSM networks in India, sampling at 8 kHz and filtering to 200-3400 Hz, which truncates the spectral cues that distinguish retroflex consonants and aspirated stops across Indic languages. A speech recognition model trained on wideband audio and deployed on AMR-NB telephony without adaptation will encounter systematic phoneme confusion.
#### Which Indian languages have the worst speech recognition accuracy?
Odia (best WER 35.1%), Bhojpuri (33.3%), Maithili, and Chhattisgarhi have the highest error rates. The Voice of India benchmark shows WER ranging from 4% to 44% for the same model across districts, highest in South India and North Bihar.
#### How can I improve speech recognition accuracy for rural India telephony deployments?
Three non-negotiable interventions: AMR-NB codec simulation augmentation at all eight bit rates on 40%+ of training data; multi-condition noise training with rural profiles at 0-15 dB SNR; and accepting 8 kHz mono audio natively without upsampling. A 5-gram KenLM with shallow fusion and on-device LoRA adaptation address dialect coverage and data residency constraints.
#### Is Bhashini suitable for production IVR speech recognition in rural India?
Bhashini is the right infrastructure foundation with coverage across 36 Indian languages, but its models require telephony domain adaptation with codec-augmented training data before achieving production-grade accuracy on AMR-NB audio from low-end rural devices. The language gap is largely solved. The acoustic domain gap remains open.

What’s new in Timbre v3.0 text-to-speech?
–
Timbre v3.0 is Gnani’s latest text-to-speech (TTS) model. It adds 12 inline audio tags for expressions, mid-sentence code-switching (in beta), Indian-format number and date reading, and time to first byte under 150 ms. It ships with 13 voices.
How do audio tags work in Timbre TTS?
+
Write the tag inline where you want it performed, for example “<whispers> The sale starts tonight.” The TTS voice performs it at that point in the sentence. All 12 tags work with every voice: coughs, excited, exhales, giggle, laugh, pauses, shouting, sigh, slow, sniffles, whispers and yawns.
Which languages does Timbre text-to-speech support?
Hindi, Indian English, Tamil, Telugu, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Bengali, Marathi and Gujarati, all from a single TTS model.
What does “beta” mean for code-switching in Timbre TTS?
Code-switching is available through the TTS API today, and quality is still improving with each release. We recommend testing it on your own scripts before using it in production calls. Every other Timbre v3.0 feature is generally available.
Do I need SSML for numbers, dates and IDs in text-to-speech?
No. Timbre v3.0 TTS reads amounts in lakh and crore, ₹ values with paise, DD/MM/YYYY dates, masked account numbers, times and percentages in the language of the sentence, with no markup.
Can I use Timbre v3.0 text-to-speech voices in commercial content?
Yes, under the commercial terms of your Gnani plan, including YouTube, podcasts, audiobooks and ads.
How can I call the Timbre v3.0 TTS API?
Three ways. REST returns a finished audio file for batch and on-demand jobs. Streaming sends audio in chunks so playback starts before synthesis finishes. Realtime runs over WebSocket for live voice agents, with plugins for LiveKit and Pipecat. Formats and long-form details are in the docs at docs.gnani.ai.
How do I move from Timbre v2.5 TTS to v3.0?
Point your existing text-to-speech request at the Timbre v3.0 model and pick one of the 13 voices. The request format is unchanged.

### FAQs
Everything you need to know about Gnani AI's platform, models and deployment.
#### What is WER (Word Error Rate)?
Word Error Rate (WER) is the standard metric for measuring speech recognition accuracy. It calculates the percentage of words incorrectly transcribed compared to the reference transcript. Lower WER means higher accuracy. Gnani Prisma v2.5 outperforms all other STT models by 20-30% on Indian languages, which represents state-of-the-art performance for multilingual Indian speech.
#### Does Gnani Prisma v2.5 support telephony-grade audio?
Yes, Gnani Prisma v2.5 is specifically optimized for real-world telephony audio. Unlike most ASR systems trained on clean studio recordings, Gnani Prisma v2.5 is built using enterprise call center audio at 8kHz sampling rate, handling compression artifacts, background noise, and network degradation that are common in telephony environments.
#### How does code-switching work?
Code-switching refers to speakers mixing multiple languages within a single sentence, such as Hinglish (Hindi + English) or Tanglish (Tamil + English). Gnani Prisma models are trained on millions of real Indian conversations with natural code-switching patterns, enabling accurate transcription without requiring speakers to stick to a single language.
#### Is on-premise deployment available?
Yes, Gnani Prisma v2.5 supports cloud, hybrid, and fully on-premise deployments. On-premise deployment ensures complete data sovereignty with air-gapped options for organizations with strict compliance requirements. Our enterprise team provides dedicated support for on-premise installations, including custom hardware configurations.
#### Which Indian languages are supported?
Gnani Prisma v2.5 supports over 10 Indian languages and dialects including Indian English, Hindi, Tamil, Telugu, Bengali, Marathi, Gujarati, Kannada, Malayalam, Punjabi, Odia. We also support code-switched combinations like Hinglish, Tanglish, Benglish, and more.
#### Can audio be streamed in real-time?
Yes, Gnani Prisma v2.5 provides real-time streaming transcription via WebSocket connections. Audio can be streamed as it's captured, with transcription results returned with sub-200ms latency. #### Does Gnani Prisma v2.5 support named entity recognition?
Yes, the model includes built-in named entity recognition (NER) optimized for Indian domains. It can automatically detect and extract entities like PAN numbers, Aadhaar IDs, policy numbers, account numbers, amounts, dates, and domain-specific terms relevant to BFSI, insurance, and telecom sectors.
#### How does latency compare to cascaded ASR systems?
Gnani Prisma v2.5's end-to-end architecture delivers sub-200ms latency, significantly faster than traditional cascaded systems that chain multiple models together. Cascaded systems typically add 1-3 seconds of latency due to sequential processing. The model's single-pass inference enables real-time applications that were previously impossible.

Hinglish is a feature, not a bug.
500 million Indians switch between Hindi and English mid-sentence naturally. A model that treats code-switching as noise produces audible seams at every language boundary, the acoustic equivalent of a dropped call.

### FAQs
Everything you need to know about Gnani AI's platform, models and deployment.
#### What makes this text-to-speech model different from generic TTS systems?
Most text-to-speech systems are trained on limited datasets and struggle with the linguistic complexity of Indian languages. This model is built for multilingual Indian speech, handling regional accents, code-switching, pronunciation, and conversational delivery with greater naturalness and accuracy.
#### Can it handle Hindi-English and multilingual conversations naturally?
Yes. The model is designed to handle code-switched speech, allowing it to seamlessly generate speech across multiple languages within the same conversation without unnatural transitions or pronunciation errors.
#### Is it optimized for contact centres, IVRs, and voice agents?
Yes. The model is built for production voice applications including AI agents, collections, reminders, customer support, IVRs, and outbound engagement. It is optimized for telephony environments and real-world customer interactions.
#### How fast is speech generation for real-time applications?
The model supports streaming speech generation with low latency, making it suitable for conversational AI systems where responsiveness is critical. Audio generation begins in milliseconds, enabling natural back-and-forth interactions.
#### How can developers integrate text-to-speech into their applications?
Developers can access speech synthesis capabilities through APIs and SDKs for real-time and batch use cases. Common implementations include voice agents, conversational AI platforms, contact centres, customer engagement systems, and enterprise workflow automation.
#### Can responses be streamed in real time?
Yes. The WebSocket API begins delivering PCM audio chunks before the full sentence is synthesized. Average first-byte latency is among the least among other providers - enabling genuine real-time conversational AI pipelines.

### Questions, answered
What teams ask before they put AI agents for customer onboarding into production.
Talk to our team →
#### What triggers an onboarding call?
Any event you choose: a loan disbursal, policy issue, account opening, app sign-up or SIM activation. Gnani AI picks up the event from your LMS, CRM or app and calls the customer within hours.
#### Which disclosures can it record?
Key terms, charges, EMI dates, cooling-off periods, consent and any mandatory script your compliance team defines. Each acknowledgement is recorded and logged with a full audit trail.
#### Can it chase KYC and pending documents?
Yes. The agent tells the customer exactly what's missing and sends an upload link on WhatsApp or SMS, then follows up until the step is complete.
#### Does it support voice biometrics?
Yes. With Gnani Biometrics, a customer can enrol their voice with consent during onboarding, so later calls verify them passively in under 5 seconds, with anti-spoof and deepfake detection.
#### Which languages does it support?
40+ languages at model level, with 10+ Indian languages in production speech recognition and code-mixed speech such as Hinglish, so first-time customers in smaller cities are guided in their own language.
#### How long does it take to go live?
A first agent can go live in under 20 minutes from a ready onboarding workflow. Full rollout depends on connecting your LMS, CRM or app and on your own testing and compliance sign-off.
